title: Electrical Engineering Intern
description:
Embarking on a journey with Golden Valley Electric Association as an Electrical Engineering Intern offers an unparalleled opportunity to apply your knowledge in a real-world setting. Located in the scenic Fairbanks, this role not only allows you to engage directly in innovative projects but also empowers you to contribute to mission-focused initiatives that enhance community well-being. With a competitive pay rate of $25.05 per hour, Grade 4 DOE, you will be recognized for your contributions while gaining valuable experience. This internship is a stepping stone to launch your career in electric engineering, where your ideas can shape the future of energy solutions. Join us to ignite your passion for engineering and be part of an energetic team dedicated to excellence and innovation!

Golden Valley Electric Association: What drives us
GVEA is an electric cooperative which maintains 3,391 miles of transmission and distribution lines, 35 substations, and 9 generating facilities. Our system is interconnected with Fort Wainwright, Eielson AFB, Fort Greely, Clear Space Force Station, the University of Alaska-Fairbanks, and all of the electric utilities in the Alaska Railbelt, extending from Homer to Fairbanks. Powering the Interior of Alaska, GVEA contributes to the economic, environmental, and social viability of our communities.

What's your day like?
As an Electrical Engineering Intern at Golden Valley Electric Association, you will play a crucial role in providing engineering services aimed at supporting the planning, construction, operation, and maintenance of the GVEA system. Under the guidance of experienced professionals, you will execute a variety of projects and responsibilities designed to enhance the efficiency and reliability of our electrical services. Your contributions will directly benefit GVEA, our valued members, and fellow employees, ensuring that we meet our mission-focused objectives while adhering to the highest standards of safety and fiscal responsibility. This internship is an excellent opportunity to apply your academic knowledge in a practical setting and to make a meaningful impact on our community. This position typically works Monday – Friday up to 8 hours per day, not to exceed 30 hours per week. Hours are flexible around schooling commitments.

What we're looking for in a Electrical Engineering Intern

title: Data Steward
description:
ABOUT US:

Soliel is an innovative, premium engineering company specializing in providing Enterprise Architecture, Network Design, Engineering, and Operations Support, Software Design and Development, Data Center Design, Deployment and Migration, and Systems Engineering services for both public and private sectors. Our Federal systems integration team manages the complexity inherent with technology change, from requirements planning to architecture, testing to deployment, and beyond. We also offer a complete range of industry-leading services, including architecture, systems development, information assurance, solution and platform integration, and program management, functional, and testing services. Over the years, Soliel's team of technical experts has consistently delivered outstanding innovative solutions and services that meet or exceed customer expectations and satisfaction.


LOCATION: Ft. Eustis / Hybrid

START DATE: ASAP

CLEARANCE: Secret or TS


The Data Steward is responsible for managing and governing architecture data supporting a stable, fully funded Army program. The position develops and maintains data standards, modeling guidance, and data management practices that support consistent and reusable Army architectures. The Data Steward works with architects, developers, functional analysts, and Government stakeholders to manage architecture data, support data integration and exchange, and maintain the quality and usability of architecture information across the Army architecture community.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop and maintain architecture data standards, governance practices, modeling guidance, and data management processes for the Army architecture community.
  • Manage the Army Integrated Architecture Data Standards (IADS) process, including Information Exchange Specifications (IES), data quality standards, data discovery, controlled access, and architecture data management throughout the data lifecycle.
  • Support the development and maintenance of standards that allow verified architecture data to be loaded into the Army Capabilities and Architecture data warehouse and used for enterprise reporting.
  • Coordinate with Army Functional Data Managers, the Army Chief Data Officer, the Architecture Data Board, and other Government stakeholders on architecture data requirements, policies, standards, and governance.
  • Lead or facilitate IADS working groups and technical meetings to identify data issues, build consensus, assess impacts, and develop action plans.
  • Support the exchange and federation of architecture data across approved systems, including the definition of data exchange specifications and interfaces.
  • Maintain and update Authoritative Reference Libraries and make approved architecture information available to architects and decision makers through designated architecture tools and repositories.
  • Support architecture community transitions involving changes to architecture frameworks, requirements processes, reference libraries, and related data standards.
  • Assess architecture data management tools and technologies and recommend solutions that support architecture development, data management, and data reuse.
  • Work with architects, developers, functional analysts, and Government stakeholders to verify and maintain accurate, consistent, and reusable architecture models, data repositories, and architecture data.


REQUIRED SKILLS:

  • Active Secret security clearance.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or other relevant technical field.
  • 5+ years of applicable experience creating UAF architecture viewpoints or UAF certification.
  • 5+ years of applicable experience creating SysML architecture viewpoints or SysML certification.
  • Experience developing DoD CAPDEV, MATDEV, or MBSE architectures.
  • Strong communication and team-building skills.
  • Ability to lead or facilitate technical meetings and work effectively with Government and contractor teams.

PREFERRED SKILLS:

  • Experience with architecture data management or data governance in an enterprise environment.
  • Experience developing or implementing data management solutions for an enterprise or Community of Interest (COI).
  • Experience developing and maintaining data standards, architecture standards, modeling guidelines, or style guides.
  • Experience working with architecture models, data repositories, or architecture data environments.
  • Experience supporting enterprise architecture data integration, data exchange, or federation.

  • Major medical, dental, and vision
  • 401K offering with company match
  • Paid holidays
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)

  • Technical Governance: Writing technical specifications, "as-builts," business cases, and policies to ensure knowledge transfer and system stability.

This is a 12-month fixed-term contract opportunity for an experienced TM1 and IBM Planning Analytics consultant to help deliver the next phase of our Finance transformation program within IBM’s premium cloud-hosted environment. This is a hands-on delivery role combining solution design, development and stakeholder partnership across Finance, FP&A, and operational teams.

You will enhance our driver-based planning environment, develop integrated Balance Sheet and Cash Flow capabilities, enable five-year strategic planning, and improve platform performance, controls, documentation and knowledge transfer.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead requirements workshops and translate business needs into practical solution designs, technical specifications and delivery plans.

  • Design, build and maintain TM1 cubes, dimensions, hierarchies, rules, feeders, TurboIntegrator processes, chores, security and Planning Analytics Workspace content.

  • Enhance existing revenue, expenses, labour, rent, recharge, initiatives and Profit and Loss planning models.

  • Improve system performance, data quality and integration, including synchronisation of development and production environments and reduction of duplicated data.

  • Develop driver-based Balance Sheet models covering working capital, provisions, leases, fixed assets, borrowings, tax and acquisition overlays.

  • Build an integrated Cash Flow model with controlled mappings, automated three-statement reconciliation and exception reporting.

  • Develop a strategic five-year planning capability incorporating baseline performance, growth assumptions and business initiatives.

  • Partner with Finance analysts during iterative development, demonstrations and testing to validate calculations and usability early.

  • Maintain technical and user documentation and provide training and knowledge transfer to internal teams.

Skills and experience:

  • Strong hands-on experience with IBM Planning Analytics / TM1 in a consulting, development or solution-design role.

  • Advanced capability in cubes, dimensions, hierarchies, rules, feeders, TurboIntegrator, chores, security and Planning Analytics Workspace.

  • Experience delivering budgeting, forecasting, scenario modelling and management-reporting solutions.

  • Proven ability to optimise TM1 performance, data integration and model maintainability.

  • Sound understanding of Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow relationships.

  • Ability to translate complex Finance requirements into scalable technical solutions.

  • Strong stakeholder engagement, documentation, testing and delivery skills.

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively across Finance and operational teams.

Employee Benefits

  • Flexible and hybrid working arrangements

  • Access to hundreds of everyday savings including phone bills, fuel and groceries, fashion, restaurants and entertainment.

  • Expert guidance on healthy living on a range of topics like money, work, mind, body, and life.


About us

Australian Clinical Labs (Clinical Labs) is committed to be the pathology provider of choice. Our business is growing rapidly and now has over 5000 employees and a truly national reach. We have approximately 100 NATA accredited laboratories that perform close to 6 million episodes each year for doctors, specialists, patients, hospitals and corporate clients. Clinical Labs services almost 100 private and public hospitals and is the largest provider of pathology services to public hospitals in Australia.

Who we are

We pride ourselves on our patient focus and medical excellence, empowering our people to help us to improve and save patient’s lives. Our culture is agile and willing to change, and we always act with the highest respect and integrity. Clinical Lab’s employees are passionate about what they do, the work environment in which they operate and the safety and wellbeing of all who interact with us.

Other Requirements

You may be required to undergo probity checks as part of the recruitment process including police check and licence check.

Diversity and Inclusion

Australian Clinical Labs is an equal opportunities employer, we encourage applications from people of all ages, nationalities, abilities and cultures – including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, the LGBTQI+ community, people living with disability, and individuals with culturally diverse backgrounds. We’re happy to adjust our recruitment process to support accessibility needs. We also welcome applications from individuals with culturally diverse backgrounds. Australian Clinical Labs is committed to supporting Veteran Employment and Australian Defence Force Veterans and their spouses are encouraged to apply.

Please note, only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

title: Senior Network and Security Engineer - Project Engineering
description:
We're expanding our engineering team and looking for skilled and experienced Senior Network and Security Engineers who thrive in complex environments, and enjoy tackling challenging technical problems. If you’re the type of engineer who gets energised by new technologies, enjoys continuous learning, and wants exposure to a diverse range of projects rather than repetitive BAU work, we want to hear from you.


The Role

Reporting to the Head of Project Engineering, this role will see you as a member of a highly skilled team delivering a diverse range of projects in critical infrastructure environments. You will:

  • Lead technical design workshops with various stakeholders.

  • Design and implement a range of different secure networking technologies - including Cisco SDA - in both greenfield and existing environments.

  • Produce high quality documentation including network diagrams, detailed designs, implementation plans, change requests, and as built documentation.

  • Work a mix of different projects through a combination of leading larger projects with the support of the wider engineering team, working as a team member within large projects, and working autonomously on your own projects.

  • Work with leading technologies including Cisco (routing, switching, SD-WAN, wireless, security) and Fortinet (firewalls, VPNs, and SD-WAN).

  • Be responsible for planning and delivering your work within allocated budgets.

  • Collaborate with customers and internal teams to ensure delivery expectations are met or exceeded.

  • Provide subject matter expertise and input to the solution architects where required to improve scoping.

  • Providing leadership and guidance to junior engineers.

  • Be an escalation point for our managed services team for complex problems.

  • Contribute to the team knowledge base and other knowledge sharing activities.

  • Participate in the on call escalation roster.


What We Are Looking For

  • 5+ years' experience in secure network engineering, preferably in a systems integrator environment.

  • Someone who is equally comfortable working autonomously and within a team

  • Solid hands-on experience with a combination of:

    • Cisco routing & switching (CCNP or CCIE)

    • Cisco and Fortinet next generation firewalls or equivalent

    • Cisco Wireless (Cisco, Meraki or equivalent enterprise Wi-Fi)

    • Cisco ISE or competing NAC products

  • A multitasker that can switch between different complex projects as required.

  • Hands on experience with Cisco SDA and/or Cisco NDFC is highly desirable.

  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and communication skills.

  • Customer-first mindset with ability to work in high-pressure environments.


Certification Requirements (must be current)

  • Cisco CCNP minimum

  • Fortinet NSE4 or higher is highly desirable


Why Join Us?

  • ArchiTech is a Cisco Preferred Partner (Networking, Security, Cloud and AI Infrastructure), a Fortinet Expert partner, and an industry leading integrator in the healthcare industry.

  • Exposure to leading enterprise networking and security technologies.

  • Work and collaborate with a highly skilled and close knit team

  • Structured training and certification pathways (Cisco, Fortinet, and other technologies).

  • Supportive team culture with a focus on learning, innovation, and excellence.


Please Note:

  • You must have a valid Australian driver’s license and use of a personal vehicle to perform this role.

  • This is a hybrid role where employees are required to attend the office 3 days a week.

  • Successful candidate may choose to base this role at either our Port Melbourne or Bendigo offices.

title: Automation Process Analyst
description:
Salary: Competitive, negotiable package.

Automation Process Analyst

We are seeking a part-time Automation Process Analyst to join our team, with flexible and negotiable working hours to suit the right candidate.

The ideal candidate will be a mature, highly organised professional with strong communication skills, experience in business analysis, process improvement, or a similar role, and the ability to think logically. You will work with stakeholders across the business to understand challenges, identify opportunities for improvement, and translate business needs into practical, workable automation and process solutions.

This opportunity is particularly well suited to an experienced professional returning to the workforce, such as a parent re-entering their career after time away, or someone seeking meaningful, rewarding work without the constraints of a traditional full-time role.

Who Are We?

Subnet is a proudly South Australian-owned IT company with a 25+ year legacy of partnering with organisations to deliver tailored technology solutions. We’re not about cookie-cutter fixes – we listen, we design, and we support, so our 300+ customers can focus on what matters most. Our team of tech wizards, creative problem-solvers, and friendly faces are always ready to help.

Why You’ll Love Working at Subnet

  • Tech Your Way: Get a budget to choose your own I.T. equipment, and more perks like extra super, extra leave, or more tech. We’ll even cover your mobile phone bill.
  • Flexibility First: Hybrid work-from-home options and an open approach to flexibility. Subnet understands that much like computers, your life requires administration.
  • Dress for Your Day: Be comfortable, dress down or up depending on your daily commitments. We’ll also help you buy the clothes and accessories you choose.
  • Professional Development: We invest in your ongoing learning and support your continued growth as an expert in your field. Subnet will cover costs and give you study time.
  • Wellbeing Matters: Free vaccination program, standing desks, onsite gym, free parking, support for volunteer commitments and an office close to cafés and shops.
  • Culture Counts: We’re big on positivity, open feedback, and making sure everyone feels included and supported with regular One on One time.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Working with stakeholders, analyse business processes, to understand pain points, manual hand-offs and improvement areas.
  • Gather, document and translate business requirements into clear process maps, SOPs, workflow documentation and structured briefs for the development team.
  • Coordinate automation projects from idea through to delivery, including tracking actions, timelines, project updates, and managing the expectations of stakeholders throughout.
  • Support testing, implementation and continuous improvement by assisting users through UAT, gathering feedback and helping ensure automation outcomes deliver practical business value.
  • Maintain automation governance and documentation, including registers, knowledge bases, project artefacts and reporting that supports prioritisation and visibility of automation initiatives.

What You’ll Bring

  • Experience in business analysis, project coordination or process improvement, with the ability to understand how work gets done and identify opportunities to simplify, improve and automate.
  • Strong process documentation skills, including the ability to produce clear requirements, process maps, SOPs, workflow diagrams or similar documentation.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with confidence working across technical and non-technical teams.
  • Strong organisation and priority-setting skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple pieces of work, track actions and keep projects moving.
  • A practical, curious and detail-focused mindset, with the ability to ask good questions, understand business problems and translate discussions into clear next steps.
  • Comfort working with distributed or overseas teams, including the ability to communicate clearly and maintain momentum across different working styles or locations.

Ready to Make an Impact?

We're looking for someone with a strong work ethic, a collaborative approach, and a genuine passion for making things work better. You don't need to be an automation expert. What matters more is that you're naturally curious, enjoy learning new technologies, ask great questions, and can think on your feet when tackling complex business challenges.

In return, you'll enjoy a supportive team environment, excellent employee benefits, flexibility around your preferred working hours, and the opportunity to make a real impact across the business through process improvement and innovation.

We’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive team and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Apply now with your Resume and a cover letter telling us why you’re the perfect fit!

Want to know more? Reach out to hr@subnet.net.au – we’d love to chat!

title: Episode Advisor

Responsibilities

● Provide comprehensive support to members, helping them to understand and maximize their episode of care benefits.

● Respond to inquiries via phone, email, or chat, offering clear and accurate information to resolve questions and concerns.

● Initiate outgoing communication to assist members in utilizing their Episode Advantage benefits

Benefit Plan Explanation:

Portal Support:

title: Utility Site Superintendent
description:
About the Project:

The Eglinton Crosstown West Extension will bring the Eglinton Crosstown LRT another 9.2 kilometers farther west, creating a continuous rapid transit line from the east end of Toronto into Mississauga. The Stations, Rail, and Systems (SRS) package encompasses the design, construction, integration, and commissioning of key project components.

Position Overview

TRP has a current vacancy for an experienced Utility Site Superintendent to provide field leadership and coordination for utility construction activities across the ECWE SRS project.


The Utility Site Superintendent will be responsible for supervising and coordinating utility construction activities from planning and preparation through installation, relocation, protection, testing, commissioning, restoration, and turnover.


The role will work closely with Project Managers, Construction Managers, Utility Coordinators, Engineering, Design, Traffic & Transit, Environmental, Quality, Health & Safety, Survey, Project Controls, municipal representatives, utility owners, subcontractors, and other project stakeholders.


The successful candidate will have strong experience managing utility construction within active urban environments, particularly where utility work interfaces with major roads, transit infrastructure, station construction, underground structures, existing services, traffic staging, and public access.


This is a highly field-oriented position requiring strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and construction coordination skills.


Key Responsibilities

Utility Construction Supervision

  • This role provides overall on-site leadership for all wet utilities, telecom, gas distribution, drainage, and earthworks activities, ensuring safe, coordinated, and compliant execution in line with the project schedule and contract requirements. The incumbent will direct daily field operations, lead subcontractor coordination meetings and safety briefings, and supervise subcontractors to maintain productivity, quality, and adherence to scope. A key focus is proactive planning and scheduling, including development and management of three-week lookahead plans, daily tracking of quantities and resources, and early identification and resolution of issues that could impact progress. The role requires full-time on-site presence, strong collaboration with project management, design, and survey teams, and rigorous implementation of safety and quality systems, including full compliance with approved method statements and Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), to ensure all work meets specified standards and is properly documented.



Underground Utility Works

Provide field leadership for a broad range of utility construction activities, which may include:

  • Watermains
  • Sanitary sewers
  • Storm sewers
  • Combined sewer systems
  • Stormwater infrastructure
  • Telecommunications
  • Fibre-optic infrastructure
  • Gas distribution
  • Traffic signal infrastructure
  • Utility duct banks
  • Utility chambers and vaults
  • Temporary utility services
  • Utility protection and support systems
  • Utility relocations and abandonments
  • Service connections and tie-ins

Ensure utility installations are coordinated with existing infrastructure and future station, road, rail, and systems requirements.

Utility Relocations & Protection

  • Lead field execution of utility relocation and protection activities.
  • Coordinate utility locates, daylighting, potholing, test pits, surveys, and investigative activities.
  • Confirm existing utility conditions against available records and design information.
  • Coordinate temporary support, shoring, protection, and relocation of existing utilities where required.
  • Ensure existing utilities remain protected and operational throughout construction.
  • Coordinate shutdowns, isolations, cutovers, tie-ins, and service interruptions with utility owners and affected stakeholders.
  • Ensure required notifications and approvals are obtained before utility interruptions or modifications.
  • Identify conflicts between existing utilities and proposed construction and escalate issues promptly.
  • Work with Engineering and Design teams to resolve field conflicts and unforeseen conditions.



Utility Coordination & Interfaces

  • Coordinate utility construction with station excavation, foundations, structures, roadworks, traffic staging, drainage, civil works, tunnel interfaces, and other SRS activities.
  • Coordinate with construction teams working on adjacent work fronts to avoid access, sequencing, and installation conflicts.
  • Participate in utility coordination meetings and construction planning sessions.
  • Review upcoming construction activities to identify utility-related constraints and dependencies.
  • Coordinate utility works around active roadways, sidewalks, pedestrian routes, cycling facilities, transit facilities, and private accesses.
  • Ensure utility construction activities are sequenced appropriately with permanent and temporary traffic management requirements.
  • Coordinate interfaces between existing utilities and new station, rail, electrical, communications, and building systems.
  • Support interface management between TRP, utility owners, municipalities, subcontractors, and other ECWE contractors.



Utility Owner & Stakeholder Coordination

  • Maintain effective working relationships with utility companies, municipalities, agencies, consultants, subcontractors, and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate field activities and inspections with utility owners.
  • Facilitate utility-owner inspections, approvals, testing, shutdowns, cutovers, and acceptance activities.
  • Ensure utility-owner requirements are communicated clearly to field crews and subcontractors.
  • Coordinate responses to utility-owner comments and field directives.
  • Escalate unresolved utility issues that could affect schedule, safety, cost, or construction sequencing.
  • Support meetings and site walks with utility owners and municipal representatives.
  • Maintain awareness of stakeholder commitments and ensure field teams understand applicable requirements.

Construction Planning & Scheduling

  • Participate in short-term and look-ahead planning for utility activities.
  • Develop and maintain detailed work plans for utility construction.
  • Coordinate utility activities with the project master schedule and site logistics.
  • Identify critical path utility activities and potential schedule risks.
  • Coordinate manpower, equipment, materials, subcontractors, and utility-owner resources.
  • Monitor planned versus actual progress.
  • Identify opportunities to improve sequencing, productivity, and construction efficiency.
  • Provide accurate field information to Project Controls for schedule updates and progress measurement.
  • Assist with recovery planning where utility activities fall behind schedule.



Quality Control

  • Ensure utility works are constructed in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, codes, standards, and quality requirements.
  • Coordinate required inspections, testing, surveys, and verification activities.
  • Review installation quality and identify deficiencies before work progresses to subsequent activities.
  • Coordinate pressure testing, CCTV inspection, compaction testing, mandrel testing, electrical testing, continuity testing, and other applicable utility tests.
  • Ensure deficiencies and non-conformances are documented and corrected.
  • Support preparation and completion of inspection and test plans (ITPs).
  • Verify that utility installation records and as-built information are accurately captured.
  • Coordinate utility-owner acceptance and sign-off requirements.
  • Support preparation of quality documentation for turnover and handover.



Safety & Environmental Compliance

  • Promote and enforce a strong safety culture across all utility work activities.
  • Ensure work is performed in accordance with the project Health & Safety Plan, applicable Ontario legislation, and TRP procedures.
  • Conduct and participate in daily pre-task planning, toolbox talks, safety meetings, and site inspections.
  • Ensure crews understand hazards associated with excavation, trenching, confined spaces, live utilities, traffic, heavy equipment, lifting, and working around existing infrastructure.
  • Ensure utility locating and excavation activities are properly planned and controlled.
  • Verify appropriate excavation protection, access/egress, shoring, trench protection, and safe work practices are implemented.
  • Stop unsafe work and immediately escalate significant hazards.
  • Support incident investigations and implementation of corrective actions.
  • Ensure utility activities comply with environmental requirements relating to dewatering, sediment control, spills, dust, noise, waste, and protection of surrounding areas.
  • Coordinate with Health & Safety and Environmental teams on site-specific requirements.


Excavation & Trenching

  • Supervise excavation and trenching activities associated with utility installation and relocation.
  • Ensure excavation activities are properly sequenced and coordinated with utility locates and existing services.
  • Monitor trench conditions, access, shoring, protection systems, dewatering, and safe work practices.
  • Coordinate trench backfill, bedding, compaction, and surface restoration.
  • Ensure excavation activities do not compromise existing infrastructure, adjacent structures, roadways, or temporary works.
  • Coordinate survey and inspection requirements before utilities are covered.



Traffic & Public Interface

  • Coordinate utility work within active roadways and public areas.
  • Work closely with PLAA,Traffic & Transit teams to ensure utility construction follows approved traffic management plans.
  • Coordinate lane closures, sidewalk closures, pedestrian detours, driveway access, cycling routes, and temporary traffic staging.
  • Ensure utility work areas are properly barricaded, signed, protected, and maintained.
  • Coordinate with stakeholder and communications teams when utility activities may affect residents, businesses, pedestrians, transit users, or other members of the public.
  • Ensure construction access and emergency access requirements are maintained.



Field Documentation & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate daily construction records.
  • Prepare daily reports documenting manpower, equipment, activities, progress, delays, issues, inspections, testing, and site conditions.
  • Track utility quantities and installed progress.
  • Record changes, unforeseen conditions, utility conflicts, and field instructions.
  • Support preparation of RFIs, field change requests, technical queries, and deficiency reports.
  • Maintain records of utility-owner inspections and approvals.
  • Ensure as-built information is captured accurately and submitted through the appropriate project processes.
  • Provide photographs and supporting documentation for construction records.
  • Support project reporting and progress measurement.



Subcontractor Management

  • Provide day-to-day field direction and coordination to utility subcontractors.
  • Monitor subcontractor productivity, workmanship, staffing, equipment, and adherence to schedule.
  • Confirm subcontractors are working in accordance with approved methods and project requirements.
  • Coordinate subcontractor access, work areas, materials, inspections, and testing.
  • Identify performance issues and work with the Construction Manager to address deficiencies.
  • Support evaluation of subcontractor progress and completion.
  • Verify quantities and completed work for progress reporting and payment purposes.
  • Ensure subcontractors complete required documentation and closeout activities.



Design & Constructability Support

  • Review utility drawings, specifications, profiles, details, and construction documents for constructability.
  • Identify conflicts between design information and existing field conditions.
  • Participate in constructability reviews and utility coordination workshops.
  • Provide practical field input to Engineering and Design teams.
  • Support resolution of RFIs and technical queries.
  • Review proposed design changes for field feasibility and construction sequencing.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify construction, reduce utility conflicts, improve safety, and minimize disruptions.
  • Assist with development and review of temporary utility arrangements.



Testing, Commissioning & Turnover

  • Coordinate utility testing and commissioning activities.
  • Ensure utility systems are ready for inspection, testing, tie-in, and acceptance.
  • Coordinate final connections and cutovers with utility owners and affected project teams.
  • Support completion of punch lists and deficiencies.
  • Ensure required test results, inspection records, approvals, and certificates are collected.
  • Support preparation of turnover packages and as-built documentation.
  • Coordinate utility-owner acceptance and handover requirements.
  • Ensure temporary utility installations are removed or transitioned as required.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Post-secondary education in Construction Management, Civil Engineering Technology, Civil Engineering, Utilities, or a related discipline is preferred.
  • 7–10 years of progressive construction experience, including significant experience supervising utility construction.
  • Demonstrated experience as a Site Superintendent, Utility Superintendent, General Superintendent, Civil Superintendent, or similar field leadership role.
  • Strong experience with underground utilities, utility relocations, municipal infrastructure, roadworks, or major civil construction.
  • Experience working on large-scale transportation, transit, infrastructure, highway, municipal, or urban construction projects is strongly preferred.
  • Experience working in an active urban environment with significant interfaces between utilities, traffic, public access, and construction activities.
  • Demonstrated experience managing utility subcontractors and field crews.
  • Experience coordinating directly with utility owners and municipal agencies.
  • Strong knowledge of utility construction methods, sequencing, testing, and commissioning.
  • Experience working in a Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build, P3, or similarly complex project environment is an asset.
  • Working knowledge of Ontario construction legislation, codes, standards, and utility requirements.
  • Valid driver's license is required.


What TRP Can Offer You:

  • Competitive Salary
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Employer Matching Retirement Program
  • Life insurance

At TRP, we are committed to providing an environment of mutual respect where equal opportunities are available to all applicants and teammates. Accommodation is available upon request for applicants throughout the recruitment and selection process.

We thank all applicants for their interest. However, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Deposit Operations Business Systems Analyst
description:
Why Stifel

Stifel strives for a culture that puts its clients and associates first: a culture where everyone belongs, everyone is welcome, and everyone contributes to the success of our clients, their careers, and the firm as a whole.

Let’s talk about how you can find your place here at Stifel, where success meets success.

What You'll Be Doing

The Deposit Operations Business Systems Analyst is responsible for administering and supporting the Fiserv Premier Core application and related ancillary banking systems while serving as a key resource for operational reporting, user access management, system configuration, and process improvement initiatives. This role independently analyzes operational data, supports audit and compliance requirements, troubleshoots system-related issues, and partners with business units to improve efficiency, accuracy, and control practices across Deposit Operations and related departments.

What We're Looking For

  • Administer and maintain core banking and operational systems, including product setup, configuration updates, user administration, and system maintenance activities.
  • Independently manage user access controls across multiple banking applications, including onboarding, modifications, terminations, and periodic access reviews.
  • Generate, validate, analyze, and distribute operational and Business Analytics reports to support business and regulatory requirements.
  • Research, troubleshoot, and resolve moderate-complexity system, reporting, and operational issues while coordinating with internal partners and vendors as needed.
  • Monitor system updates, release communications, and vendor notices, assessing operational impacts and assisting with implementation activities.
  • Support internal and external audits by gathering documentation, validating controls, responding to inquiries, and assisting with remediation efforts.
  • Perform data analysis, reconciliations, and exception monitoring to identify trends, risks, inaccuracies, and process improvement opportunities.
  • Maintain operational procedures, process documentation, system specifications, and user administration standards.
  • Participate in testing activities for system upgrades, product implementations, workflow enhancements, and operational changes.
  • Collaborate with business partners to evaluate operational needs and recommend solutions that improve efficiency, controls, and customer service.
  • Provide guidance and knowledge sharing to less experienced team members and serve as a resource within the department.

What You'll Bring

  • Working knowledge of banking operations, deposit operations processes, and financial services environments.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.
  • Ability to interpret data, identify trends, and recommend solutions.
  • Knowledge of user access administration, system controls, and operational risk management principles.
  • Strong attention to detail with a focus on accuracy, completeness, and data integrity.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple assignments and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships across departments and functional areas.
  • Understanding of audit, compliance, and regulatory requirements affecting banking operations.
  • Ability to work independently while exercising sound judgment and escalating issues when appropriate.

Education & Experience

  • Minimum Required: High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Preferred: Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Minimum Required: 3+ years of experience in banking operations, systems administration, business systems support, deposit operations, or a related area.

Licenses & Credentials

  • Minimum Required: None.

Systems & Technology

  • Experience supporting, administering, or working extensively within the Fiserv Premier Core application.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Outlook, Word, PowerPoint).
  • Experience with core banking platforms and ancillary banking systems.
  • Experience utilizing reporting, analytics, or business intelligence tools.
  • Ability to analyze and manipulate data using advanced Excel functions.

About Stifel

Stifel is more than 130 years old and still thinking like a start-up. We are a global wealth management and investment banking firm serious about innovation and fresh ideas. Built on a simple premise of safeguarding our clients’ money as if it were our own, coined by our namesake, Herman Stifel, our success is intimately tied to our commitment to helping families, companies, and municipalities find their own success.

While our headquarters is in St. Louis, we have offices in New York, San Francisco, Baltimore, London, Frankfurt, Toronto, and more than 400 other locations. Stifel is home to approximately 9,000 individuals who are currently building their careers as financial advisors, research analysts, project managers, marketing specialists, developers, bankers, operations associates, among hundreds more. Let’s talk about how you can find your place here at Stifel, where success meets success.

At Stifel we offer an entrepreneurial environment, comprehensive benefits package to include health, dental and vision care, 401k, wellness initiatives, life insurance, and paid time off.

Stifel’s bank and trust companies are equal opportunity employers. All candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, genetic information or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. If you would like more information regarding Equal Employment Opportunity rights and protections, please review the following information: Know Your Rights.

title: Regional Vice President, Enterprise
description:
Company Overview



Docusign brings agreements to life. Over 1.5 million customers and more than a billion people in over 180 countries use Docusign solutions to accelerate the process of doing business and simplify people’s lives. With intelligent agreement management, Docusign unleashes business-critical data that is trapped inside of documents. Until now, these were disconnected from business systems of record, costing businesses time, money, and opportunity. Using Docusign’s Intelligent Agreement Management platform, companies can create, commit, and manage agreements with solutions created by the #1 company in e-signature and contract lifecycle management (CLM).


What you'll do



Docusign brings agreements to life. Over 1.5 million customers and more than a billion people in over 180 countries use Docusign solutions to accelerate the process of doing business and simplify people’s lives. With intelligent agreement management, Docusign unleashes business-critical data that is trapped inside of documents. Until now, these were disconnected from business systems of record, costing businesses time, money, and opportunity. Using Docusign’s Intelligent Agreement Management platform, companies can create, commit, and manage agreements with solutions created by the #1 company in e-signature and contract lifecycle management (CLM). A Regional Vice President Director (RVP) at Docusign directly manages a team of enterprise sellers (6-8). You play a critical role that combines strategic vision with hands-on leadership to drive overall growth of all solutions associated with Docusign’s Intelligent Agreement Management (IAM) platform suite, including Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) & AI solutions. This particular role will manage a team of seven (7) sellers as part of the Southeast Region of the Enterprise Geos Sales Team, reporting to the AVP of North America Enterprise Geos Sales. The Enterprise Geos Segment includes all industry sectors except Financial Services, Insurance, Healthcare and Public Sector.

This position is a people manager role reporting to Area Vice President, Enterprise Sales.

Responsibility

  • Create a comprehensive sales plan for the region that aligns with the company's overall business objectives and revenue targets, including identifying target customers, driving sales goals, and establishing performance metrics

  • Work with sellers to define and optimize their territories and accounts, which involves strategic planning for key accounts, identifying new business opportunities and executive alignment strategies, and developing a repeatable sales process for enterprise deals

  • Own the regional sales forecast and be responsible for monitoring the health of the pipeline, ensuring forecast accuracy by holding sellers accountable, and adjusting strategies to create sustainable growth

  • Use data and analytics to monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) such as seller performance, win rates, average deal size, and sales cycle length and identify areas for improvement and adjust strategies accordingly

  • Build a high-performing team with a growth-mindset by identifying, hiring and nurturing top-tier enterprise sales talent and ensuring a structured onboarding process that sets new hires up for success

  • Provide ongoing coaching and mentorship to help each seller develop their skills, including conducting regular one-on-one meetings, participating in deal reviews, and role-playing complex sales scenarios

  • Create a team environment that is focused on accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement and celebrate successes and provide constructive feedback to address performance gaps

  • Lead by example and motivate the team to exceed their targets, which can involve creating incentives, running internal competitions, and providing a clear vision for success

  • Participate in the most strategic and complex enterprise deals, including joining customer meetings, assisting with negotiations, and helping to close large deals

  • Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with key clients and stakeholders in the region as a trusted advisor

  • Ensure the team is focused on a consultative, value-led sales approach, understanding customer challenges and aligning Docusign’s solutions to provide a clear return on investment (ROI)

  • Coach the team on how to navigate complex enterprise buying processes, identify key decision-makers, and build consensus across multiple stakeholders within an organization

  • Collaborate with the marketing department to develop effective lead generation campaigns and go-to-market strategies

  • Ensure alignment between sales and marketing efforts to drive top-of-funnel growth

  • Work closely with product management to provide customer feedback and ensure the product roadmap aligns with market needs

  • Partner with the customer success team to ensure a seamless handoff after a deal is closed

  • Report on regional performance to senior leadership, providing accurate sales reports, forecasts, and insights on market trends and competitive activity

Basic

  • 12+ years of sales team management experience, specifically within software sales managing Enterprise, complex software selling, SaaS or Platform sales teams

  • 5+ years prior experience selling software in a quota-carrying role

Preferred

  • Track record of building, coaching and enabling a rapidly growing team

  • Experience selling into a variety of industries and territories as well as experience cultivating larger, strategic relationships

  • Strong portfolio of C-level contacts across a variety of large enterprise accounts

  • Capacity to work on cross-functional projects and teams as needed as well as leverage internal resources to problem-solve

  • A player-coach mentality with the ability to coach individually, not a one-size fits all approach

  • Possess strong emotional intelligence

  • Exceptional communication skills, both verbal and written – includes excellent reporting and forecasting skills

  • Active listener and strong collaborator

  • SaaS business acumen and an understanding of key metrics like Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR), Annual Contract Value (ACV) and Total Contract Value (TCV)

  • Familiarity with Google suite, Salesforce, Slack and Zoom

  • Attention to detail and highly organized

  • Resilient and adaptable

  • Willingness to travel 50% or more as needed to support the business

title: Storekeeper
description:
Storekeeper

Position Information

Primary Location: On MV Saga X -Company Vessel alongside Squamish, BC


Employee Status: Rotational – 28 days on/ 14 days off

Company Operating Name: Bridgemans Crew Management Ltd.

Business Address: 342 Water St, Vancouver, BC

Terms of Employment: Hourly - Rotational

Language of Work: English

Hourly Wage: $CAD 21.33 / hour

Benefits Package offered: Extended Health Benefits

Contact Information: careers@brgmans.com



The Company:

Bridgemans Services Group is a leading provider of turnkey marine infrastructure, offering premium floating workforce accommodations (floatels), marine logistics, and marine construction services. Headquartered in Vancouver, BC, Bridgemans operates globally, helping industry leaders execute complex projects in remote locations safely, sustainably, and in partnership with local communities.

We hire passionate professionals across a diverse range of operational roles to support our floating accommodations and marine fleet, including deckhands, marine officers, and captains, as well as hospitality, culinary, and housekeeping team members who ensure our residents and crew experience top-tier service on board our floatels.


Floatel Life:
At Bridgemans, we believe that providing an exceptional living and working environment is essential to supporting our workforce. When you join our team, you will enjoy comfortable accommodations complemented by delicious, freshly prepared meals. Beyond the workday, our floatels foster community and social engagement, featuring fully equipped games rooms and recreational activities, a dedicated fitness area, and an onboard convenience store to ensure you have everything you need right at your fingertips.


Career Advancement:
At Bridgemans, a job is just the beginning of an exciting professional journey. We are dedicated to fueling your long-term growth by supplying and supporting essential marine certifications, actively opening doors to dynamic marine careers around the world. Whether you are looking to advance within our fleet or expand your horizons across the global maritime industry, we provide the tools, training, and pathways you need to chart a successful course for your future.


Benefits:
Your health, well-being, and peace of mind are top priorities. That is why we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support you both on and off the job.


Schedule:
Getting you to and from the floatel is completely seamless and stress-free. Bridgemans pays for your flights (from major Canadian cities) and transportation to and from the project site, ensuring your travel is fully arranged and supported for every shift rotation.

Rotational schedule may vary by department but is typically 28 days on / 14 days off.


Position Summary:

This is a physical, hands-on position. The Storekeeper regularly pulls, pushes, stages, and moves pallets, bins, carts, and supplies as well as lifts up to 25kg. The role requires strong attention to food safety, inventory accuracy, requisition control, product rotation, cleanliness, and documentation.

The Storekeeper is responsible for the physical receiving, inspection, storage, issuing, and record-keeping of food, supplies, chemicals, disposables, and related operating stock for Saga X movement.

The role is heavily focused on galley operations, with a smaller portion of the position supporting Saga Store receiving and stock movement.

Primary Responsibilities

Receiving and Product Inspection:


  • Receive incoming deliveries for the galley, including fresh, frozen, refrigerated, dry goods, beverages, cleaning supplies, paper goods, chemicals, disposables, and operational stock.
  • Check deliveries against purchase orders, packing slips, invoices, or approved order sheets.
  • Confirm product name, quantity, weight, case count, packaging condition, expiry/best-before dates, and product quality.
  • Identify and report shortages, overages, substitutions, damages, missing items, temperature concerns, or rejected products to the Executive Chef, Sous Chef, Storekeeper, or designate.
  • Label, stage, and direct products to the correct dry storage, cooler, freezer, chemical, or operational storage area.
  • Ensure refrigerated and frozen products are moved promptly to controlled-temperature storage.

Physical Handling, Pallets, and Safe Movement of Goods:


  • Pull, push, move, stage, and organize pallets, carts, totes, bins, and heavy cases as part of daily receiving and stock movement.
  • Use approved equipment such as pallet jacks, hand trucks, carts, dollies, or other vessel-approved material-handling equipment.
  • Break down pallets and move product safely into storage, production, or issuing areas.
  • Maintain clear aisles, safe walkways, and properly stacked storage areas.
  • Follow safe lifting, pushing, pulling, and manual-handling procedures at all times.
  • Report unsafe loads, damaged pallets, blocked exits, trip hazards, or equipment defects immediately.



Food Safety and Temperature Control:

  • Follow all food safety requirements when receiving, transporting, storing, and issuing food products.
  • Check and record receiving temperatures for refrigerated and frozen products when required.
  • Reject or hold products that are damaged, spoiled, contaminated, thawed, out of temperature, or otherwise unsafe.
  • Keep raw, ready-to-eat, allergen-sensitive, chemical, and non-food products separated as required.
  • Support FIFO rotation and ensure older stock is used before newer stock where appropriate.
  • Maintain clean, organized, and sanitary receiving, storage, cooler, freezer, and staging areas.
  • Use required PPE when handling food, chemicals, pallets, heavy items, or cold-storage products.


    Issuing Requisitions and Stock Distribution:

    • Issue products to galley areas based on approved requisitions, par levels, production needs, or instructions from galley leadership.
    • Pick, stage, and distribute food and supplies accurately to the correct department, meal period, or production area.
    • Record issued stock using the approved requisition process, manual log, or inventory system.
    • Ensure requisitions are complete, accurate, signed or approved when required, and filed according to procedure.
    • Communicate with the galley team when stock is short, substituted, damaged, unavailable, or requires priority use.

    Inventory Counts, Stock Rotation, and Storage Control:

    • Conduct daily, weekly, monthly, or spot inventory counts as assigned.
    • Update inventory records accurately, including counts, issues, receipts, transfers, and adjustments.
    • Maintain proper stock rotation for perishable and non-perishable products.
    • Monitor par levels and notify leadership of low stock, excess stock, slow-moving items, or ordering concerns.
    • Keep storage areas organized, labelled, accessible, and ready for inspection.
    • Assist with inventory reconciliation and investigate discrepancies when requested.

    Logs, Records, and Documentation:

    • Update daily receiving logs, temperature logs, requisition records, inventory sheets, discrepancy reports, and other operational records as required.
    • Maintain accurate records for food safety, inventory control, audits, and operational reporting.
    • Ensure paperwork is completed clearly, legibly, and on time.
    • File or submit delivery documents, receiving records, requisitions, and inventory records according to Saga X procedures.
    • Communicate exceptions clearly at shift handover or to the supervisor on duty.

    Saga Store Support:

    • Receive, check, and organize Saga Store inventory as assigned.
    • Support store stock rotation, storage, replenishment, and inventory counts.
    • Report damaged, missing, short-shipped, or incorrect Saga Store items to the appropriate supervisor.
    • Ensure Saga Store support does not interfere with the primary responsibility of supporting galley operations.

    Required Skills and Abilities:

    • Physically capable of frequent pushing, pulling, lifting (up to 25kg), carrying, bending, reaching, and standing for extended periods.
    • Comfortable working with pallets, pallet jacks, carts, dollies, and heavy cases in a vessel environment.
    • Good attention to detail when checking quantities, products, dates, temperatures, and records.
    • Basic understanding of food safety, FIFO, temperature control, product separation, and sanitation.
    • Ability to issue requisitions accurately and maintain inventory documentation.
    • Ability to work independently while following direction from galley leadership.
    • Strong communication skills and willingness to report problems early.
    • Reliable, organized, punctual, and able to work in a fast-paced operation.

    Preferred Qualifications:

    • Previous experience in receiving, stores, warehouse, food service, camp, hotel, vessel, or galley support.
    • Experience with food-service inventory, requisitions, receiving logs, and stock counts.
    • Food safety certification or willingness to complete required training.
    • WHMIS or chemical-handling knowledge is an asset.
    • Pallet jack or material-handling experience is preferred, subject to vessel and company requirements.

    Physical Requirements:

    • Must be able to safely pull and push loaded pallets, carts, bins, and dollies within approved limits and procedures.
    • Must be able to lift and move cases and supplies using safe work practices and assistance where required.
    • Must be able to work in coolers, freezers, dry stores, loading/staging areas, and galley-adjacent spaces.
    • Must be able to climb, bend, reach, stand, walk, and work on vessel surfaces while following safety procedures.
    • Must be able to manage repetitive physical tasks during delivery windows and inventory periods.

    Performance Expectations:

    • Galley deliveries are received, checked, stored, and issued accurately.
    • Food safety standards are followed during receiving, storage, and product movement.
    • Temperature logs, receiving records, requisitions, inventory counts, and daily logs are completed accurately and on time.
    • Storage areas remain organized, rotated, labelled, clean, and inspection-ready.
    • Discrepancies and safety concerns are reported promptly.
    • Saga Store support is completed as assigned while keeping galley support as the priority.
    • The Receiver works safely, professionally, and cooperatively with the Saga X hospitality team.

    Example Daily Duties:

    • Prepare receiving area before delivery windows.
    • Receive and check incoming goods against paperwork.
    • Record required temperatures and note any issues.
    • Move product to dry storage, coolers, freezers, chemical storage, or galley production areas.
    • Break down and organize pallets safely.
    • Issue requisitioned items to the galley and record stock movement.
    • Update daily logs, receiving records, and inventory sheets.
    • Clean and organize receiving and storage areas before the end of shift.
    • Communicate shortages, damaged goods, low stock, and follow-up items to the supervisor.


    At Bridgemans Services Group we believe that each employee contributes directly to our growth and success. We are committed to workplace excellence, safe work environments and the communities where we work and live. Bridgemans hires on the basis of merit and is committed to employment equity and diversity.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Reliability, Infrastructure, and Tooling
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Software Engineer - Reliability, Infrastructure, and Tooling based in Romania.

This is a senior engineering role focused on building reliable, scalable infrastructure for demanding real-time and AI workloads.
You’ll work closely with product engineering teams to design systems that are secure, maintainable, observable, and resilient at global scale.
The role goes beyond traditional operations, combining infrastructure engineering, reliability, tooling, and hands-on product development.
You’ll tackle complex challenges involving distributed systems, Kubernetes, networking, real-time media, and secure execution environments.
Your work will help engineering teams self-serve infrastructure and reliability capabilities without creating unnecessary operational bottlenecks.
You’ll also contribute to incident management, on-call practices, architectural decisions, and long-term reliability improvements.
This is an opportunity to work remotely with experienced engineers while contributing to infrastructure supporting billions of real-time interactions.

Accountabilities

  • Ramp up on a complex global architecture involving distributed databases, messaging systems, networking infrastructure, Kubernetes, and other core platform technologies, identifying areas of reliability debt and improvement.

  • Design and ship reliability-focused engineering work directly within production codebases, including load balancing, load shedding, instrumentation, scalability, and efficiency improvements.

  • Build and evolve internal infrastructure and developer tooling that enables product engineering teams to independently operate reliable workloads.

  • Partner closely with product development teams to co-design systems and ensure reliability, security, maintainability, and operational readiness are considered throughout development.

  • Develop observability capabilities that make system behavior measurable, understandable, and actionable, using appropriate signals and visualization techniques.

  • Participate in a shared on-call rotation and contribute to effective incident response, investigation, remediation, and prevention of recurring reliability issues.

  • Investigate complex system-level problems across distributed infrastructure, networking, application behavior, and production environments.

  • Improve configuration management and infrastructure practices across diverse systems, reducing unnecessary complexity, errors, and technical debt.

  • Contribute technical perspectives to architectural discussions and help establish engineering practices that support both short-term delivery and long-term scalability.

  • Support systems with demanding workloads, including real-time media, secure customer code execution, advanced networking, and other highly concurrent services.

  • Collaborate with engineering partners on potentially contentious reliability and operational decisions with clarity, pragmatism, and strong technical judgment.

  • Automate repetitive operational processes wherever possible to improve engineering efficiency and reduce manual intervention.

    • Requirements

    • Strong professional experience building and operating non-trivial production applications, particularly systems involving high concurrency, distributed workloads, or complex control loops.

    • Significant experience with Kubernetes or an equivalent large-scale container orchestration platform.

    • Strong understanding of Linux internals and networking, with the ability to investigate issues across multiple layers of a production system.

    • Proven experience using observability, monitoring, logging, and related tooling to diagnose difficult production problems.

    • Experience operating large-scale, globally distributed systems, including the configuration management, reliability challenges, and technical debt that emerge as systems grow.

    • Experience responding to and managing complex production incidents, including identifying root causes and implementing durable corrective actions.

    • Experience operating open-source infrastructure technologies such as Kafka, ClickHouse, or comparable distributed systems.

    • Strong systems-thinking skills and an ability to reason about infrastructure in terms of signals, feedback, dependencies, and control mechanisms.

    • Strong communication and collaboration skills, particularly when working with partner engineering teams and navigating competing priorities.

    • A pragmatic approach to engineering that balances immediate delivery needs with long-term maintainability, reliability, and operational cost.
