POSITION SUMMARY

The Quality Inspector is responsible for inspecting and verifying that products meet the required standards and specifications in compliance with DoD and aerospace regulations. This role involves conducting detailed inspections, documenting findings, and collaborating with engineering, manufacturing teams, and the quality manager to resolve quality issues


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Perform Incoming, In-Process, and Final Inspections: Inspect raw materials, components, subassembly and completed electronic assembly to verify they meet specifications and quality standards, including DoD and aerospace requirements.
  • Document Inspection Results: Accurately and meticulously document all findings, nonconformities, and inspection results in accordance with internal procedures and regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure Compliance with Standards: Conduct inspections following AS9100, ISO 9001, MIL-STD, and other applicable aerospace and defense standards.
  • Use Precision Measurement Tools: Operate and maintain various inspection tools, including calipers, micrometers, gauges, and CMMs (Coordinate Measuring Machines), to validate product dimensions and tolerances.
  • Identify and Report Nonconformities: Identify defects and nonconformities, complete Nonconformance Reports (NCRs), and communicate quality issues to relevant departments for corrective action.
  • Collaborate with Cross-Functional Teams: Work closely with engineering, manufacturing, and quality assurance teams to troubleshoot quality issues and lead improvements to inspection processes.
  • Support Root Cause Analysis and Corrective Actions: Participate in root cause analysis investigations and lead the implementation of corrective and preventive actions to reduce recurring quality issues.
  • Audit Processes and Procedures: Work closely with the quality manager to assist in internal audits to ensure adherence to quality standards and assist with preparation for external audits, including DoD, AS9100, and customer audits if requested.
  • Maintain Documentation: Ensure that all inspection documentation, records, and certifications are accurate, organized, and retained according to company and regulatory standards.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • High school diploma or equivalent; technical degree or relevant certifications (such as Certified Quality Inspector (CQI)) preferred.
  • 1-5 years of experience in quality inspection, ideally in a DoD, aerospace, or similarly regulated manufacturing environment.
  • Familiarity with AS9100, ISO 9001, and MIL-STD standards.
  • Previous experience with DoD contracts and understanding of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) handling is a plus

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Technical Proficiency: Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, blueprints, and specifications.
  • Attention to Detail: Strong attention to detail to identify quality issues and ensure compliance with exact specifications.
  • Measurement Tool Competency: Skilled in using a variety of inspection tools and precision measuring equipment, including calipers, micrometers, and CMMs.
  • Problem-Solving Skills: Capability to identify issues, recommend corrective actions, and assist with continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Strong Communication: Effective verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly document findings and work collaboratively with teams.
  • Organizational Skills: Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks, ensuring thorough documentation and adherence to timelines.

SECURITY / EXPORT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS

title: Principal / Senior Principal Scientist- Investigative Toxicology
description:
We advance science so that we all have more time with the people we love.

Genentech’s Investigative Toxicology group within the Translational Safety department is dedicated to elucidating the mechanisms underlying toxicities observed for novel therapeutics spanning from drug discovery through clinical development. By employing state-of-the-science in vitro and ex vivo experimental approaches, the group provides fit-for-purpose solutions to address target safety assessments, guide lead optimization, and de-convolute complex safety liabilities.

We are seeking an experienced and forward-thinking to join our team as an individual contributor. In this role, you will be responsible for driving the strategy, development, and implementation of predictive and mechanistic safety capabilities specifically tailored to support our Neuroscience and Cardiovascular, Renal, and Metabolic (CVRM) portfolios. Operating in newly established spaces characterized by emerging therapeutic modalities, you will establish unique preclinical safety roadmaps, interface directly with cross-functional project teams, lead matrixed experimental execution with laboratory staff, and partner with internal predictive modeling groups and external consortia to advance New Approach Methodologies (NAMs).

**The Opportunity:**

**The responsibilities of this Senior Scientist position will :**

1. Portfolio Strategy & Project Team Engagement

- Serve as the primary Investigative Toxicology subject matter expert and representative on discovery and early development project teams across the Neuroscience and CVRM portfolios.
- Apply a deep working knowledge of drug discovery/development workflows to identify rate-limiting safety liabilities early, define critical path questions, and influence candidate selection.
- Partner with Project Team Toxicologists, Discovery Scientists, and Pathologists to guide nonclinical safety strategies and mechanistic de-risking plans.

2. Preclinical Safety Roadmaps for Emerging Modalities

- Establish, qualify, and execute hypothesis-driven preclinical safety roadmaps tailored to novel and emerging therapeutic modalities (e.g., advanced biologics, nucleic acid therapies, cell and gene therapies, multi-specifics).
- Operate effectively in ambiguous, newly established scientific areas by identifying technological gaps and designing innovative solutions to characterize on-target and exaggerated pharmacology liabilities.

3. Capability Development & Matrixed Execution

- Drive the strategic identification, validation, and implementation of next-generation capability needs for Neuro and CVRM safety assessment.
- Act as the lead scientific strategist leveraging matrixed support from Investigative Toxicology wet-lab members to design, oversee, and interpret complex experimental studies.
- Ensure rigorous data integrity, thorough electronic laboratory notebook documentation, and publication-ready technical reports.

4. Predictive Toxicology Integration

- Partner closely with colleagues across the Predictive Toxicology group—specifically Model Development / Complex In-Vitro Systems (CIS) and Computational Toxicology—to establish translatable, predictive workflows.
- Co-develop and implement human-relevant cellular systems (e.g., organ-on-a-chip, microphysiological systems, iPSC-derived cellular models, high-content imaging, and toxicogenomics) to tailor assay platforms to project-specific liabilities.

5. External Consortia & Scientific Representation

- Represent the Investigative Toxicology group and Genentech in key external industry, academic, and regulatory consortia (e.g., HESI, IQ Consortium, NC3Rs).
- Spearhead external engagement and publication efforts around the qualification and regulatory adoption of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) within the Neuro and CVRM domains.

**Who Are You:**

Education/ Experience

- Principal Scientist: Ph.D. with 3-5+ years of relevant postdoctoral or industry experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or CRO environments.
- Senior Principal Scientist: Ph.D. with >5+ years of industry experience demonstrating successful safety leadership and cross-functional impact within drug discovery/development project teams.
- Proven track record of operating within a drug discovery/development setting, with demonstrated ability to identify, prioritize, and de-risk rate-limiting liabilities.
- Prior experience working with emerging therapeutic modalities and developing custom preclinical safety strategies.

Technical & Domain Expertise

- Strong mechanistic understanding of safety assessment, cellular pathways, and organ-level physiology relevant to Neuroscience and/or CVRM.
- Working familiarity with advanced in vitro models, microphysiological systems (MPS / organ-on-a-chip), iPSC technologies, high-content phenotypic assays, and multi-omics/transcriptomics.
- Demonstrated experience collaborating with computational biologists and predictive modelers to interpret complex datasets.
- Proficiency with statistical and data visualization tools (e.g., GraphPad Prism, Spotfire, JMP, R, or Python).

Leadership & Collaboration

- Demonstrated ability to lead via influence in a matrixed environment, guiding experimental work executed by laboratory technical staff.
- Exceptional oral and written communication skills; ability to distill complex mechanistic toxicology data into actionable project team recommendations.
- Willingness and ability to represent Genentech authoritatively in external scientific working groups and consortia.

Relocation Assistance benefits are available for this posting.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Reliability, Infrastructure, and Tooling
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Software Engineer - Reliability, Infrastructure, and Tooling based in Spain.

This is a senior engineering role focused on building reliable, scalable infrastructure for demanding real-time and AI workloads.
You’ll work closely with product engineering teams to design systems that are secure, maintainable, observable, and resilient at global scale.
The role goes beyond traditional operations, combining infrastructure engineering, reliability, tooling, and hands-on product development.
You’ll tackle complex challenges involving distributed systems, Kubernetes, networking, real-time media, and secure execution environments.
Your work will help engineering teams self-serve infrastructure and reliability capabilities without creating unnecessary operational bottlenecks.
You’ll also contribute to incident management, on-call practices, architectural decisions, and long-term reliability improvements.
This is an opportunity to work remotely with experienced engineers while contributing to infrastructure supporting billions of real-time interactions.

Accountabilities

  • Ramp up on a complex global architecture involving distributed databases, messaging systems, networking infrastructure, Kubernetes, and other core platform technologies, identifying areas of reliability debt and improvement.

  • Design and ship reliability-focused engineering work directly within production codebases, including load balancing, load shedding, instrumentation, scalability, and efficiency improvements.

  • Build and evolve internal infrastructure and developer tooling that enables product engineering teams to independently operate reliable workloads.

  • Partner closely with product development teams to co-design systems and ensure reliability, security, maintainability, and operational readiness are considered throughout development.

  • Develop observability capabilities that make system behavior measurable, understandable, and actionable, using appropriate signals and visualization techniques.

  • Participate in a shared on-call rotation and contribute to effective incident response, investigation, remediation, and prevention of recurring reliability issues.

  • Investigate complex system-level problems across distributed infrastructure, networking, application behavior, and production environments.

  • Improve configuration management and infrastructure practices across diverse systems, reducing unnecessary complexity, errors, and technical debt.

  • Contribute technical perspectives to architectural discussions and help establish engineering practices that support both short-term delivery and long-term scalability.

  • Support systems with demanding workloads, including real-time media, secure customer code execution, advanced networking, and other highly concurrent services.

  • Collaborate with engineering partners on potentially contentious reliability and operational decisions with clarity, pragmatism, and strong technical judgment.

  • Automate repetitive operational processes wherever possible to improve engineering efficiency and reduce manual intervention.

    • Requirements

    • Strong professional experience building and operating non-trivial production applications, particularly systems involving high concurrency, distributed workloads, or complex control loops.

    • Significant experience with Kubernetes or an equivalent large-scale container orchestration platform.

    • Strong understanding of Linux internals and networking, with the ability to investigate issues across multiple layers of a production system.

    • Proven experience using observability, monitoring, logging, and related tooling to diagnose difficult production problems.

    • Experience operating large-scale, globally distributed systems, including the configuration management, reliability challenges, and technical debt that emerge as systems grow.

    • Experience responding to and managing complex production incidents, including identifying root causes and implementing durable corrective actions.

### Summary

**THIS RECRUITMENT MAY CLOSE BEFORE THE DEADLINE LISTED ABOVE OR UPON RECEIPT OF THE FIRST 100 APPLICATIONS, WHICH EVER COMES FIRST.**

**_**POSITIONS IN THIS CLASSIFICATION ARE GRANT FUNDED UNDER THE CANNABIS AWARENESS SAFETY AND ENFORCEMENT ("CASE") PROGRAM THROUGH DECEMBER 31, 2031.  ABSENT ADDITIONAL GRANT OR ALTERNATIVE FUNDING AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2031, POSITIONS IN THIS CLASSIFICATION WILL BE ELIMINATED.  ADDITIONALLY, THE DUTIES OF THIS CLASSIFICATION ARE IN NO WAY INTENDED TO REPLACE OR ENCROACH UPON THE DUTIES OF ANY OTHER CLASSIFICATION REPRESENTED BY THE GENERAL UNIT OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE.**_**

**DEFINITION**

Under general supervision, works within the Police Department’s Community Relations Office to develop, coordinate, and implement community education, outreach, and engagement on public education initiatives through a variety of electronic and print media, with an emphasis on cannabis-related crime prevention, youth education, and community safety and awareness through social media platforms; participates in the development and implementation of crime prevention programs;  serves as a primary liaison between the Department and the community on assigned areas; performs related work as assigned.

**SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXERCISED**

Receives general supervision from assigned supervisory or management personnel.  Exercises no direct supervision over staff.

**CLASS CHARACTERISTICS**

This non-sworn journey level classification is responsible for independently performing administrative duties in support of the Police Department, including primary support in the development and implementation of drug and alcohol education and crime prevention programs.   Positions at this level exercise judgment and initiative in their assigned tasks, receive only occasional instruction or assistance as new or unusual situations arise and are fully aware of the operating procedures and policies of the work unit.

### Essential Functions / Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

**Examples of TYPICAL JOB FUNCTIONS** **(Illustrative Only)**

_Management reserves the right to add, modify, change, or rescind the work assignments of different positions and to make reasonable accommodations so that qualified employees can perform the essential functions of the job._

- Assists in the planning and development of and coordinates and teaches specialized educational programs addressing crime prevention, public safety, cannabis-related laws and regulation, impaired driving, youth cannabis use, and related community concerns for members of the community, including elementary through college age students.
- Develops accurate, up-to-date, age/audience-appropriate educational presentations, informational materials, flyers, brochures, digital content, and other public education resources.
- Conducts presentations, workshops, and educational sessions for schools, youth organizations, neighborhood groups, businesses, civic organizations, parent groups, and other community stakeholders.
- Plans, coordinates, and facilitates community engagement activities, including neighborhood meetings, educational workshops, public safety events, outreach campaigns, and Department-sponsored events; coordinates Department participation in community events.
- Identifies emerging community concerns and develops educational strategies to address those concerns; evaluates community engagement efforts and recommends improvements based on participation, feedback, and identified community needs.
- Promotes crime prevention strategies and encourages community participation in public safety initiatives.
- Develops, coordinates, and assists with the preparation of Department social media content in accordance with Department policies and established City communication standards.
- Creates educational and informational social media posts concerning crime prevention, public safety, community programs, cannabis-related issues, youth safety, impaired driving, and other assigned topics.
- Develops graphics, informational materials, videos, photographs, and other digital content for Department communication platforms.
- Ensures conformance with applicable grant sponsored programming initiatives and activities; collects and compiles data to document program outcomes and grant performance measures; assists with the preparation of grant reports and supporting materials; participates in grant-related meetings and training.
- Maintains current information and research regarding drugs, drug trends, effects of drug use, and prevention methods and techniques.
- Compiles, writes and/ or designs manuals, pamphlets, and informational documents for departmental personnel and the public.
- Maintains organized records of community contacts, events, presentations, educational materials, and program activities.
- Observes and complies with all City and mandated safety rules, regulations, and protocols.
- Performs other duties as assigned under the City’s cannabis program.

### Minimum Qualifications

QUALIFICATIONS

**Knowledge of:**

- Basic functions, principles and practices of law enforcement agencies.
- Activities and programs of the City’s Police Department.
- Principles of drug abuse and child safety including knowledge of various narcotics, drugs, and their characteristic effects.
- Principles and practices of educational program development and implementation including curriculum planning and program monitoring.
- Basic law enforcement practices and terminology.
- Methods for evaluating program quality and effectiveness.
- Basic techniques for interviewing.
- Research and reporting methods, techniques, and procedures.
- Principles and procedures of record-keeping and preparation of correspondence and reports.
- Applicable Federal, State, and local laws, codes, and procedures relevant to assigned area of responsibility.
- City and mandated safety rules, regulations and protocols.
- Techniques for providing a high level of customer service by effectively dealing with the public, vendors, contractors, and City staff.
- The structure and content of the English language, including the meaning and spelling of words, rules of composition, and grammar.
- Modern equipment and communication tools used for business functions and program, project, and task coordination, including computers and software programs (with an emphasis on social media and graphic art applications) relevant to work performed.

**Ability to:**

- Develop, implement, present, and coordinate specialized educational programs.
- Evaluate the effectiveness of specialized programs and make sound recommendations for improvement.
- Provide effective basic counseling services.
- Exercise sound independent judgement and discretion within established guidelines.
- Represent the city in contacts with school districts, students/youth, parents, the business community, and the public.
- Prepare clear, concise reports and other written materials.
- Establish and maintain effective working relations with those contacted in the course of work, including the media.
- Maintain accurate records.
- Perform non-sworn tasks to support the department’s law enforcement programs.
- Organize and prioritize a variety of projects and multiple tasks in an effective and timely manner; organize own work, set priorities, and meet critical time deadlines.
- Use tact, initiative, prudence, and independent judgment within general policy, and procedural, guidelines.
- Effectively use computer systems, software applications relevant to work performed (with an emphasis on and social media and graphic art applications), and modern business equipment to perform a variety of work tasks.
- Continually build and enhance graphic art and social media production skills through educational opportunities.
- Communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing, using appropriate English grammar and syntax.

**Education and Experience:**

_Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities is qualifying.   A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be:_

Education:

Equivalent to completion of the twelfth (12th) grade, supplemented by completion of college coursework in education, public health, communications, social work, or a related field.

Experience:

Two (2) years of experience performing administrative or field work in a law enforcement or educational setting that includes the development and implementation of a public education program or provides in-depth knowledge of drug and alcohol abuse and crime prevention programs.

Licenses and Certifications:

- Possession of a valid California Driver’s License to be maintained throughout employment.

**Other Requirements:**

- Passage of a detailed background investigation prior to employment.
- Availability to work evenings and weekends.

### Additional Information

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS**

Must possess mobility to work in a standard office setting and use standard office equipment, including a computer; to maintain mobility, physical strength, and stamina to respond to emergency situations and accidents; vision to read printed materials and a computer screen; to operate a vehicle and patrol assigned areas of the City; and hearing and speech to communicate in person, before groups, and over the telephone or radio.

The job involves fieldwork requiring frequent walking or running or standing on uneven terrain, and climbing and descending structures to identify problems or hazards.  Finger dexterity is needed to access, enter, and retrieve data using a computer keyboard or calculator and to operate police services equipment. Positions in this classification frequently bend, stoop, kneel, reach, and climb to perform work and inspect work sites.  Employees must possess the ability to lift push, and pull materials and objects averaging a weight of 30 pounds, in all cases with the proper use of equipment and/or assistance from staff.

Positions also work in a secondary office or station environment, and use standard office equipment, including a computer.

**ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS**

Employees work in outdoor conditions, and are exposed to loud noise levels, cold and hot temperatures, inclement weather conditions, moving vehicles, and hazardous physical substances and fumes.  Employees also work in an office or station environment with moderate noise levels, controlled temperature conditions, and no direct exposure to hazardous physical substances.  Employees may interact with upset staff and/or public and private representatives in interpreting and enforcing departmental policies and procedures.

The principal duties of this class are performed in a field or police station environment with exposure to criminal offenders, mentally ill individuals, and persons potentially infected with communicable diseases.

**E-Verify**: The City of El Monte is an E-Verify employer.  E-Verify is an Internet based system operated by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in partnership with the Social Security Administration (SSA) that allows participating employers to electronically verify the employment eligibility newly hired employees in the United States.

title: CS Strategy & Operations Program Manager
description:
Company Overview



Docusign brings agreements to life. Over 1.5 million customers and more than a billion people in over 180 countries use Docusign solutions to accelerate the process of doing business and simplify people’s lives. With intelligent agreement management, Docusign unleashes business-critical data that is trapped inside of documents. Until now, these were disconnected from business systems of record, costing businesses time, money, and opportunity. Using Docusign’s Intelligent Agreement Management platform, companies can create, commit, and manage agreements with solutions created by the #1 company in e-signature and contract lifecycle management (CLM).


What you'll do



As a CS Strategy & Operations Program Manager, you will be responsible for designing, owning, and driving the company's most complex and mission-critical transformation programs for Customer Success. This role extends beyond managing project timelines to leading the successful execution of key initiatives, ensuring that all initiatives are strategically aligned, integrated, and deliver significant, measurable business value. The successful candidate will act as a trusted advisor to leadership and across key stakeholders, proactively identifying opportunities, proactively mitigating risks, and providing clear, decisive direction across multiple, interdependent workstreams.

This position is an individual contributor role reporting to the Senior Director, Customer Success Strategy & Analytics.

Responsibilities

  • Own and help define the overarching CS Strategy & Operations program roadmap and vision for major Customer Success Operations initiatives, with a bias to agentification and automation
  • Collaborate with senior leaders to proactively plan program objectives, scope, and deliverables, and manage expectations on an ongoing basis to ensure outcomes that materially improve customer experience and business performance.
  • Design and facilitate strategic brainstorming and working sessions with SMEs, cross-functional stakeholders, and CS leaders to surface, shape, and pressure-test new initiatives before they enter the program roadmap.
  • Enable all activities from strategic inception through to successful delivery and adoption, directing cross-functional program activities, and driving a shared understanding and accountability across multiple workstreams and with stakeholders at all levels, including the C-suite as needed.
  • Lead the development and presentation of executive-level communications, including Steering Committee updates, to ensure a shared understanding of program status, strategic value, and business impact.
  • Create and manage program-level artifacts, including long-range strategic plans, cross-program dependency maps, and holistic risk and issues logs that inform and guide executive decision-making.
  • Define and track program-level success metrics tied to business outcomes (e.g., adoption, GRR, efficiency gains)
  • Model and champion AI-augmented program management practices: using AI tools to synthesize cross-functional updates, surface risks earlier, accelerate reporting/Steering Committee prep, and scale program oversight across a growing initiative portfolio.
  • Lead and evolve our CS Strategy & Operations program management methodology and best practices, sharing lessons learned and driving a culture of continuous improvement across the organization.

Job Designation



Hybrid: Employee divides their time between in-office and remote work. Access to an office location is required. (Frequency: Minimum 2 days per week; may vary by team but will be weekly in-office expectation)

Positions at Docusign are assigned a job designation of either In Office, Hybrid or Remote and are specific to the role/job. Preferred job designations are not guaranteed when changing positions within Docusign. Docusign reserves the right to change a position's job designation depending on business needs and as permitted by local law.


What you bring



Basic

  • 8+ years of combined strategy/operations and program management/enterprise transformation experience, with a proven track record of owning and delivering multiple, large-scale programs.
  • 5+ years of experience specifically with Customer Success, Sales, or broader GTM Space within a SaaS or subscription-based business.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and build consensus with working teams, senior leadership and C-level executives.
  • Strong problem solver and sense of urgency
  • Extensive experience driving digital transformation with a focus on cross-functional, interdependent programs.
  • Exceptional skills in simplifying highly complex issues and developing strategic frameworks to facilitate broad organizational understanding and action.
  • BS/BA degree or equivalent relevant experience
  • Excellent executive communication skills and interpersonal aptitude

Preferred

  • Experience in Management Consulting, Customer Success, Sales or broader GTM Operations in a SaaS context
  • Adept at building close working relationships and establishing personal credibility across an organization, maintaining a high level of professionalism and self-motivation
  • Expertise in Agile methodologies and productivity tools (e.g., SmartSheet, Jira, Confluence), with a focus on applying these tools at a program, not just project, level.
  • Fluency with AI tools for program management workflows (e.g., synthesizing status updates, drafting executive communications, risk/dependency analysis); Comfort using AI to increase program velocity and personal leverage.

Wage Transparency



Pay for this position is based on a number of factors including geographic location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Based on applicable legislation, the below details pay ranges in the following locations:

California: $132,700.00 - $206,800.00 base salary

This role is also eligible for the following:

  • Bonus: Sales personnel are eligible for variable incentive pay dependent on their achievement of pre-established sales goals. Non-Sales roles are eligible for a company bonus plan, which is calculated as a percentage of eligible wages and dependent on company performance.
  • Stock: This role is eligible to receive Restricted Stock Units (RSUs).

Global benefits provide options for the following:

  • Paid Time Off: earned time off, as well as paid company holidays based on region
  • Paid Parental Leave: take up to six months off with your child after birth, adoption or foster care placement
  • Full Health Benefits Plans: options for 100% employer paid and minimum employee contribution health plans from day one of employment
  • Retirement Plans: select retirement and pension programs with potential for employer contributions
  • Learning and Development: options for coaching, online courses and education reimbursements
  • Compassionate Care Leave: paid time off following the loss of a loved one and other life-changing events

Work Authorization Notice: Please note that we do not provide visa sponsorship or immigration support for this position. Applicants must already be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time, permanent basis without the need for current or future sponsorship.


Life at Docusign



Working here

Docusign is committed to building trust and making the world more agreeable for our employees, customers and the communities in which we live and work. You can count on us to listen, be honest, and try our best to do what’s right, every day. At Docusign, everything is equal.

We each have a responsibility to ensure every team member has an equal opportunity to succeed, to be heard, to exchange ideas openly, to build lasting relationships, and to do the work of their life. Best of all, you will be able to feel deep pride in the work you do, because your contribution helps us make the world better than we found it. And for that, you’ll be loved by us, our customers, and the world in which we live.

Docusign is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application procedures. If you need such an accommodation, or a religious accommodation, during the application process, please contact us at accommodations@docusign.com.

If you experience any issues, concerns, or technical difficulties during the application process please get in touch with our Talent organization at taops@docusign.com for assistance.

Equal Opportunity Employer



It's important to us that we build a talented team that is as diverse as our customers and where all employees feel a deep sense of belonging and thrive. title: Sr Project Analyst
description:
Overview

Join our Team as Senior Project Analyst!

We are excited to share the opportunity to join Boys & Girls Clubs of America as our next Senior Project Analyst.

Imagine a place where who you are, where you’re from, or the circumstances that surround you don’t determine your access to experiences or opportunities. Now imagine a mission created to enable all young people, especially those who need us most, to reach their full potential as productive, caring, responsible citizens. That’s what we do. At Boys & Girls Clubs of America (BGCA), we’re committed to doing whatever it takes to build great futures for America’s youth. Behind that mission are teams, systems, and processes that help our organization operate effectively and turn strategy into action. As our Senior Project Analyst, you’ll play an important role in making that happen, bringing together technology, project management, operations, and data to help teams solve problems, improve how work gets done, and successfully execute strategic priorities.

Make an Impact

The Operations & Alignment team functions as an internal consulting and execution partner for Field Operations, helping leaders solve complex challenges, improve organizational effectiveness, and deliver strategic initiatives. We partner across the organization to translate strategy into action through strong planning, data-informed decision-making, and scalable systems and processes. As our Senior Project Analyst, you’ll sit at the intersection of technology, project management, operations, and data. You’ll help manage and optimize key business systems, particularly our Salesforce ecosystem, while leading projects and process improvements that make it easier for teams to work effectively and leaders to make informed decisions. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys figuring out how systems and processes can work better, can move comfortably between technical and business conversations, and knows how to take an idea from concept through implementation.

Responsibilities

What You’ll Do

Own & Optimize CRM Solutions

You’ll serve as a key business partner for our Salesforce/CRM ecosystem, helping ensure the technology supports how our teams actually work. You will:

  • Help manage, maintain, and optimize Salesforce and related CRM functionality, including workflows, automations, dashboards, reporting, and new features.
  • Translate business needs into practical system requirements and solutions.
  • Partner with stakeholders, technology teams, and vendors on system enhancements, integrations, troubleshooting, upgrades, and ongoing maintenance.
  • Lead user acceptance testing (UAT) and help ensure new functionality works as intended before implementation.
  • Monitor system utilization and data quality and identify opportunities to improve adoption, consistency, and the user experience.
  • Develop documentation, standards, training, and resources that help employees use systems effectively.
  • Support an expanding Salesforce ecosystem that may include additional business processes and functionality over time.

Turn Strategy Into Execution

You’ll help move high-priority initiatives from ideas and plans to measurable results. You will:

  • Build project plans, workbacks, timelines, milestones, and communication plans for multiple concurrent initiatives.
  • Coordinate work across teams, keeping stakeholders aligned and deliverables moving.
  • Track progress, dependencies, risks, decisions, and action items—and raise issues before they become barriers.
  • Facilitate project meetings and create the structure and accountability needed to keep work on track.
  • Support change management as new systems, processes, and ways of working are introduced.
  • Bring consistency to project management practices, tools, documentation, and reporting.

Use Data to Solve Problems

You won’t just produce reports, you’ll help teams understand what the information means and what to do next. You will:

  • Develop dashboards, scorecards, KPIs, and reporting that provide visibility into organizational and project performance.
  • Analyze CRM and other operational data to identify trends, gaps, and opportunities.
  • Translate findings into clear, actionable insights for leaders and stakeholders.
  • Prepare executive-level presentations, reports, and briefings that make complex information easier to understand and act upon.

Improve How Work Gets Done

You’ll bring a continuous-improvement mindset to the team by:

  • Evaluating workflows and business processes to identify unnecessary steps, manual work, and inefficiencies.
  • Designing practical, scalable solutions that connect people, process, technology, and data.
  • Developing templates, tools, standards, and resources that can be used consistently across teams.
  • Looking for new technologies, approaches, and best practices that can improve organizational effectiveness.

What Success Looks Like

You’ll know you’re making an impact when projects consistently move forward with clear ownership and accountability; Salesforce and other tools are increasingly useful, reliable, and adopted by the teams they support; and leaders have timely, accurate information to make decisions. You’ll also help create measurable efficiencies by reducing manual work and process redundancies, while building scalable tools, documentation, and practices that make the organization less dependent on individual knowledge.

Qualifications

What You Bring

We’re looking for someone who brings a blend of technical aptitude, project execution, analytical thinking, and business partnership. You should have:

  • 5-7 years of experience in project management, business operations, consulting, CRM/business systems, analytics, or a related field.
  • Hands-on experience working with Salesforce or a comparable CRM/business platform, with the ability to understand how systems can be configured and improved to meet business needs.
  • Strong project management skills and experience managing multiple priorities, stakeholders, and deadlines simultaneously.
  • The ability to gather business requirements and translate them into workflows, processes, system enhancements, or other practical solutions.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including comfort working with data, dashboards, KPIs, and reporting.
  • Experience partnering across functions and influencing work without direct authority.
  • Strong written, verbal, facilitation, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate with senior leaders.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; experience with tools such as Smartsheet, Power BI, Tableau, Salesforce, or similar platforms is preferred.
  • A bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, Project Management, Finance, Operations, or a related field.
  • CAPM or PMP certification is strongly preferred.

The Competencies That Matter Most

  • Systems Thinking: You see the connections between technology, processes, data, and people and can design solutions that work across the broader organization.
  • Operational Excellence: You bring structure to complex work, manage details without losing sight of the larger objective, and consistently follow through.
  • Analytical Thinking & Problem Solving: You dig into problems, use evidence to understand root causes, and develop practical solutions rather than simply identifying issues.
  • Collaboration & Influence: You build credibility across functions, facilitate productive conversations, and help stakeholders reach alignment even when you don’t have formal authority.
  • Innovation & Continuous Improvement: You’re curious about what could work better and proactively identify new tools, approaches, and efficiencies.

Work Environment & Travel

This is a hybrid role based in Atlanta, with employees working in the office Tuesday and Wednesday and remotely on other days based on business needs. The position may require up to 25% travel to support meetings, conferences, and strategic initiatives.

Compensation

The salary range for this role is $70,000.00 to $80,000.00. BGCA takes into consideration a combination of a candidate’s education, training and experience, as well as the position’s scope and complexity, the discretion and latitude required for the role and other external and internal data when establishing a salary level. We are highly invested in every employee’s total well-being and offer a substantial and comprehensive total rewards package.

title: Canvasser
description:
Canvasser

About MF Professional Services, Inc.

MF Professional Services, Inc. (MFPS) provides human resources, payroll, benefits administration, and operational support to mission-driven organizations. This position may perform services on behalf of MFPS clients, including Mi Familia Vota and Mi Familia en Acción.

Position Summary

The Canvasser conducts voter registration, voter education, civic engagement, and voter-mobilization activities within assigned communities.

This field-based position requires traveling through assigned neighborhoods and community locations to engage residents using approved scripts, materials, forms, and outreach methods. Canvassers must accurately document voter contacts, protect voter information and registration materials, and comply with all field, safety, reporting, and voter-registration procedures.

This is a temporary position. The duration of the assignment will depend on campaign timelines, available funding, and organizational needs. Temporary employment does not guarantee continued employment or an extension of the assignment.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Canvass assigned residential neighborhoods, businesses, community locations, public spaces, and events.

  • Conduct door-to-door outreach within designated geographic areas.

  • Engage community members regarding voter registration, voter education, voting options, Get Out the Vote activities, and other approved civic-engagement initiatives.

  • Use only approved scripts, talking points, forms, literature, digital tools, and calls to action.

  • Provide accurate, approved, and non-misleading information.

  • Respect individuals who decline to participate or ask that an interaction end.

  • Provide voter-registration applications and approved assistance in accordance with applicable laws and organizational procedures.

  • Review voter-registration forms for apparent completeness without altering information or completing forms on behalf of applicants unless specifically permitted.

  • Protect completed, incomplete, spoiled, and unused voter-registration forms from loss, damage, alteration, or unauthorized access.

  • Return all forms, equipment, identification, and campaign materials according to established procedures and deadlines.

  • Never falsify, alter, discard, withhold, or misuse voter-registration forms.

  • Immediately report suspected misconduct, falsification, data manipulation, lost materials, or form-handling concerns.

  • Attend required launches, trainings, safety briefings, check-ins, and daily debriefings.

  • Follow assigned turf, schedules, goals, geographic boundaries, and reporting expectations.

  • Maintain regular communication and required check-ins with the Canvass Lead.

  • Accurately record doors knocked, successful contacts, voter-registration activity, responses, and other assigned metrics.

  • Enter information into VAN, MiniVAN, spreadsheets, mobile applications, databases, or other approved systems.

  • Submit complete and accurate daily reports, forms, and data within established deadlines.

  • Protect confidential voter, community-member, employee, and organizational information.

  • Follow workplace, field, vehicle, weather, heat, emergency, and incident-response procedures.

  • Promptly report injuries, threats, harassment, accidents, law-enforcement interactions, unsafe conditions, or other incidents.

  • Treat community members, coworkers, supervisors, and members of the public with dignity and respect.

  • Accept direction, coaching, retraining, and constructive feedback.

  • Accurately record all time worked and follow organizational timekeeping, attendance, meal-period, and rest-break procedures.

  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Previous canvassing, voter-registration, campaign, community outreach, organizing, customer service, sales, or other public-facing experience preferred.

  • Strong communication, listening, interpersonal, and customer-service skills.

  • Dependable, punctual, accountable, and comfortable approaching and speaking with members of the public.

  • Ability to follow scripts, instructions, turf assignments, reporting requirements, and safety procedures.

  • Ability to remain professional and composed during difficult or unexpected interactions.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to complete forms and records accurately.

  • Ability to accept coaching and work independently and collaboratively as part of a field team.

  • Ability to use a smartphone, tablet, mobile canvassing application, or comparable field technology.

  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and protect sensitive voter and organizational information.

  • Experience working with Latino or other diverse communities preferred.

  • Professional proficiency in English and Spanish preferred.

  • Ability to work flexible schedules, including daytime, evening, and weekend assignments.

  • Ability to travel throughout assigned communities and field locations.

  • Must satisfy any voter-registration eligibility, training, appointment, or certification requirements applicable in the assigned jurisdiction.

Physical and Work Requirements

This is a field-based position requiring extended periods of walking and standing outdoors. The employee must be able to travel on foot through assigned neighborhoods and community locations while navigating sidewalks, stairs, uneven surfaces, and varying terrain.

The position requires the ability to carry outreach materials weighing up to 25 pounds and regularly use a mobile device, clipboard, voter-registration forms, literature, and other field equipment.

Work may occur in heat, cold, rain, wind, direct sunlight, traffic, noise, crowds, and other changing field conditions. Reasonable accommodations will be considered for qualified individuals with disabilities.

title: Simulation Software Engineer (Vehicle Engineering)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SIMULATION SOFTWARE ENGINEER (VEHICLE ENGINEERING)

As a Software Engineer on the Simulations team, you will design, develop, and test our in-house simulation software supporting all SpaceX flight systems. You will program the core simulation infrastructure and collaborate on the building of models of fluids, electronics, and multi-body physics systems. This is a high impact role where you will work across the engineering groups to build high fidelity simulations used to develop cutting-edge software and hardware. Our simulation software is critical to current and future mission successes including Falcon, Falcon Heavy, Dragon, Starlink, and Starship. SpaceX is looking for smart, motivated software engineers who enjoy taking on complex challenges, work well in dynamic environments and care about software best practices.

Help us build world class software that is critical to SpaceX mission to Mars.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop and maintain the high-fidelity real-time simulation software used for all vehicles
  • Develop prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints
  • Maintain the highest standards of excellence, never settle for the status quo
  • Improve reliability and performance of simulation software
  • Work with simulation software users to develop new features and improve user experiences

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or STEM discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience in software development in lieu of a degree
  • 1+ years development experience in C++

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Strong software design and development skills in C++
  • Understanding of distributed computing systems, networking protocols, memory management, and CPU scheduling
  • Thorough knowledge of classical physics and math (algebra, calculus, Euclidean geometry)
  • Strong skills in debugging, performance optimization and unit testing
  • Creative approach to problem solving
  • Experience with open source C++ simulators such as ROS2 and Gazebo
  • Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements
  • Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willing to work extended hours and weekends when needed
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $125,000.00 - $160,000.00
Level 2: $145,000.00 - $195,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Project Manager
description:
About Us

Sabre Ltd. is a leading electrical and instrumentation solutions provider headquartered in Calgary, Alberta. We deliver customized electrical systems and field services to customers across a wide range of commercial and industrial markets.


Our capabilities include electrical construction, switchgear, modular buildings and E-Houses, instrumentation, control panels, installation, testing, commissioning, and maintenance. Sabre supports projects throughout Canada and the United States with a focus on quality, reliable execution, innovation, and long-term customer relationships.


The Opportunity

Sabre is seeking an experienced Electrical Project Manager to lead the successful delivery of industrial electrical projects. This is a field-focused role that combines project management, customer engagement, and on-site leadership, requiring regular collaboration with customers, field supervisors, and crews throughout project execution. From initial planning and estimating support through execution, closeout, and ongoing customer support, the successful candidate will combine strong project management and commercial skills with practical knowledge of industrial electrical construction to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and in alignment with customer expectations.


The Electrical Project Manager will work closely with customers, field supervision, project coordinators, estimating, procurement, safety, quality, and other Sabre divisions. This is a customer-facing role supporting key accounts in the mining, forestry, manufacturing, utilities, and industrial sectors.



Who We're Looking For

We're looking for a collaborative and results-driven leader who can build strong customer relationships, lead project teams, and deliver successful outcomes in complex industrial environments.


  • Visible and supportive leader who builds strong relationships with customers, field supervisors, and crews while driving project success.
  • Customer-focused with a commitment to building trusted relationships.
  • Strong communicator who can influence, collaborate, and align customers, field teams, and internal stakeholders.
  • Organized and accountable, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Decisive and solutions-oriented when faced with challenges and changing conditions in both project and field environments.
  • Commercially aware, balancing customer needs with project performance.
  • Proactive in identifying risks, opportunities, and continuous improvements.
  • Adaptable and resourceful in fast-paced industrial environments, with the ability to respond effectively to changing site conditions.
  • Committed to safety, quality, and operational excellence.



What You'll Do

  • Manage electrical projects from award through planning, execution, commissioning, and closeout, with regular site involvement to support successful field execution.
  • Develop project execution plans, schedules, budgets, forecasts, cash-flow projections, and resource requirements.
  • Coordinate field labour, supervision, subcontractors, materials, equipment, travel, and site access requirements.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for assigned customers and develop strong, long-term client relationships.
  • Monitor project performance, including labour productivity, costs, schedule, gross margin, billing, and cash collection.
  • Identify scope changes, prepare change orders, and ensure additional work is documented and approved.
  • Review contracts, purchase orders, specifications, drawings, and customer requirements to identify commercial and execution risks.
  • Work with estimating and operations teams to develop proposals, budgets, schedules, clarifications, and execution strategies.
  • Conduct project kick-off meetings, progress reviews, forecasting updates, and project closeout meetings.
  • Provide leadership and support to field supervisors and crews by removing roadblocks, clarifying priorities, coordinating resources, and monitoring project progress at customer sites.
  • Ensure project activities comply with Sabre's safety, quality, environmental, and project management requirements.
  • Maintain accurate project documentation, including correspondence, meeting minutes, progress reports, cost reports, change logs, completion records, and turnover packages.
  • Coordinate invoices and ensure completed work is billed accurately and promptly.
  • Identify follow-on opportunities and support account growth with existing and prospective customers.
  • Provide regular project reporting to divisional leadership and escalate emerging risks in a timely manner.
  • Travel to customer sites as required, including occasional overnight travel.



What You'll Bring



Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of project management experience in industrial electrical construction, maintenance, instrumentation, or a related field, with demonstrated experience working directly with field crews and site supervision.
  • Journeyperson Electrician certification, Electrical Engineering Technology diploma, engineering degree, or equivalent industry experience.
  • Experience leading field execution activities, coordinating labour resources, and managing work in active industrial environments.
  • Strong understanding of industrial electrical construction, labour planning, commissioning, and field execution.
  • Proven experience managing project budgets, schedules, forecasts, change orders, and customer relationships.
  • Ability to interpret electrical drawings, specifications, contracts, and scopes of work.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project management or scheduling software.
  • Strong communication and leadership skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders.
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel to project sites as required.



Preferred Qualifications

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) designation.
  • Red Seal Electrician or Master Electrician certification.
  • Demonstrated success leading field-based project execution, coordinating labour and resources, and driving performance in active industrial environments.
  • Experience delivering projects within mining, forestry, utilities, manufacturing, or other heavy industrial sectors.
  • Experience managing shutdowns, maintenance programs, brownfield projects, and remote-site operations.
  • Knowledge of instrumentation, controls, commissioning, and low-voltage electrical systems.
  • Demonstrated experience managing a diverse portfolio of projects, from service and maintenance work to multimillion-dollar construction projects.

Ready to Join Us?

If you're a motivated project professional who thrives on building relationships, leading field and project teams, and delivering successful industrial projects, we'd love to hear from you. Join Sabre and help power critical projects across Western Canada's industrial sectors.

title: Lab Aide (work-study)
description:
Overview

The Buckner and Long Labs focus on understanding the mechanisms of immune tolerance, examining why this tolerance breaks down in autoimmune diseases, and developing therapies to improve it. The Human Immunophenotyping (HIP) core at the Benaroya Research Institute (BRI) provides access to cutting-edge technologies and services enabling study of human immune-mediated diseases.

This position offers hands-on experience, exposure to laboratory techniques used in immunology research, and an opportunity to build relationships with scientific researchers.

This work-study position is for 10 to 19 hours each week, within the hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday (exact schedule to be determined quarterly, in consideration of class schedule).

To be considered for this position the student must have completed a financial aid application and received a work study award. Proof of work study eligibility is necessary to complete this application.

Responsibilities

The Lab Aide will perform routine work in a research laboratory including equipment maintenance and providing general assistance to technical laboratory personnel to help keep the lab in a clean and orderly state. Other duties include:

  • Assisting with experiment set-up
  • Maintaining and organizing lab records and data
  • Preparing media and reagents, such as stock solutions
  • Maintaining a clean and orderly laboratory area
  • Cleaning and maintaining lab equipment
  • Checking and replenishing supplies

Qualifications

High school diploma or GED and enrollment in a university-level science degree program (e.g., biology, chemistry, or biochemistry) are required. Previous or current coursework in biology and/or chemistry and past laboratory experience are preferred. Experience with molecular biology techniques is highly desirable. Demonstrated accuracy, attention to detail, and ability to learn new skills quickly is essential.

This position is solely open to candidates who are work-study eligible.

Benefits

$22.00 to $26.38 per hour

About Us

Benaroya Research Institute (BRI) has a bold mission: to advance the science to predict, prevent, reverse and cure immune system diseases, from autoimmune disease to cancer to asthma and allergies. We create detailed pictures of the immune system in health and disease, aiming to understand how disorders start and how to rebalance the immune system back to health. Equipped with innovative tools and robust biorepositories, our team chips away at the biggest mysteries behind these conditions to work toward our vision of a healthy immune system for everyone. BRI is a nonprofit research institute based in Seattle and affiliated with Virginia Mason Franciscan Health. We collaborate with clinicians and patients to accelerate the path from innovative lab discoveries to life-changing patient care.

At BRI, each individual is valued as an important contributor to our vision and mission. Consider making a difference by joining our team. Because together, we are powering possibility.

title: People Business Intelligence Analyst
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a People Business Intelligence Analyst based in India.

This role sits at the intersection of people analytics, business intelligence, and data engineering, helping leaders make informed workforce decisions through trusted data. You’ll own data mapping across HR systems and a cloud data warehouse, ensuring information is accurate, consistent, and well governed. You’ll build dashboards and reporting solutions that bring workforce trends and key people metrics to life. The position combines technical expertise with close collaboration across HR, Talent Acquisition, Compensation & Benefits, and leadership teams. You’ll work with sensitive employee data while applying strong privacy, access-control, and data governance practices. This is a fully remote opportunity with an international working environment and exposure to modern analytics, cloud, and AI-powered technologies.

Accountabilities:

  • Map and document data flows from HR source systems, including HRIS, ATS, payroll, and engagement survey platforms, into a Redshift data warehouse.
  • Define and maintain field definitions, data lineage, business logic, data dictionaries, and metric glossaries to ensure consistent reporting across teams and dashboards.
  • Build and maintain dashboards using QuickSight, Power BI, Tableau, or similar business intelligence platforms, covering metrics such as headcount, turnover, hiring funnel performance, DEI representation, engagement, compensation equity, and span of control.
  • Write, troubleshoot, and optimize SQL queries in Redshift to support recurring reporting, ad hoc analysis, and leadership reporting requirements.
  • Partner with HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Compensation & Benefits, and People leadership to understand business questions and translate them into effective data models, analysis, and visualizations.
  • Ensure sensitive HR information, including personally identifiable information, compensation data, and protected-class information, is handled according to privacy and access-control requirements.
  • Identify and resolve data quality issues at the source or within the data mapping layer, including duplicate records, inconsistent coding structures, and broken joins across systems.
  • Support recurring reporting cycles, including monthly headcount reviews, quarterly board reporting, annual compensation reviews, and ad hoc leadership requests.

    • Requirements

    • 6+ years of experience in Business Intelligence, Analytics, Data Visualization, or a related field.
    • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, or a comparable discipline.
    • Strong SQL skills with experience writing, troubleshooting, and optimizing queries against cloud data warehouses such as Amazon Redshift.
    • Advanced experience building and maintaining dashboards using Amazon QuickSight, Power BI, Tableau, or similar BI platforms.
    • Practical experience with data mapping and ETL concepts, including understanding how data moves from source systems into data lakes and warehouses and how to identify and resolve data issues.
    • 3+ years of experience in People Analytics, Recruiting Analytics, HR data, or another highly regulated and governance-driven data environment is an asset.
    • Exposure to HRIS platforms such as Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, ADP, or BambooHR and ATS platforms such as Greenhouse or Lever is an asset.
    • Familiarity with people metrics frameworks, including SHRM and ANSI HR metrics standards, is an asset.
    • Experience with AWS data technologies such as S3, Glue, Athena, and Redshift is an asset.
    • Basic proficiency in Python or R for data cleaning, automation, and analysis is an asset.
    • Experience with prompt engineering and generative AI or agentic AI solutions is an asset.
    • Willingness to work United States East Coast hours (UTC-4 / UTC-5) is an asset.
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify patterns in complex datasets and translate findings into practical business insights.
    • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with both technical and business stakeholders.
    • Highly organized, detail-oriented, curious, and comfortable working independently.
    • Ability to handle sensitive information responsibly and maintain a strong focus on data accuracy, privacy, and governance.
    • Openness to learning new technologies and applying emerging tools to improve analytics and reporting capabilities.

      • Benefits

      • Fully remote position, allowing you to work from home in India.
      • Remote-friendly and flexible approach to working arrangements.
      • Flexible scheduling designed to support work-life balance.
      • Competitive compensation package, with potential eligibility for annual bonuses or incentives.
      • Paid time off.
      • Retirement savings benefits, which may include applicable pension or savings schemes.
      • Equity grants and potential participation in an employee stock purchase plan, depending on role and location.
      • Competitive health benefits and coverage.
      • Family-friendly benefits, including parental leave.
      • Annual lifestyle benefit that can be used toward travel, wellness, or other eligible personal expenses.
      • Tuition assistance for qualifying educational and professional development programs.
      • Matching contributions for qualifying charitable donations.
      • Employee assistance program providing resources and support for personal and professional challenges.
      • Employee referral program with rewards for successful referrals.
      • Opportunities to work with modern people analytics, cloud data, business intelligence, and AI-powered technologies.
      • Inclusive environment that values diverse perspectives, transferable skills, continuous learning, and professional growth.

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, WW Sustainability
description:
Join us at the forefront of Amazon's sustainability initiatives to work on environmental and social advancements to support Amazon's long term worldwide sustainability strategy. Amazon's Worldwide Sustainability (WWS) team works to build a sustainable business for our customers and the planet. Within WWS, the Sustainability Science & Innovation (SSI) team advances Amazon's sustainability commitments through applied science, data analytics, and strategic research programs — translating complex environmental and supply chain challenges into actionable intelligence for Amazon's business units.

You'll lead lead cross-organizational coordination and external collaboration for a high-priority sustainability science programs within SSI. You will be the operational anchor for a multi-stakeholder program — managing internal alignment across business units, driving external partnership execution with research institutions and industry bodies, and owning the program's delivery rhythm from roadmap to executive reporting. This role requires someone who can operate comfortably at the boundary between technical and business domains, build trust with senior stakeholders across organizational lines, and keep complex, multi-workstream programs on track without close supervision. You'll lead mechanisms that translate breakthrough science into scalable pilots and Amazon workflows, establishing best practices that compound impact across the organization.

This is a high-visibility role requiring the ability to influence technical direction across Amazon, drive alignment with senior leadership on multi-year investments, and serve as a thought leader bridging science, product, and business strategy.


Key job responsibilities
- Own stakeholder engagement across teams within WWS and SSI — securing data and resource commitments, aligning on shared deliverables, and maintaining consistent messaging across all stakeholder touchpoints
- Drive data and information-sharing agreements across teams, including access governance; facilitate joint planning sessions and translate program outputs into team-level action plans
- Manage the operational cadence of Amazon's external research partnerships — including academic institutions, national laboratories, and government-funded research programs — tracking deliverables and milestones
- Own the program roadmap — translating science and engineering priorities into a sequenced set of data products and decision-support tools; drive the program's weekly and quarterly update cadence to Director-level stakeholders; negotiate resources and priorities across contributing teams and unblock work before it stalls
- Build and maintain governance structures for program operations, including data access policies, budget tracking, and decision logs; identify and proactively resolve operational bottlenecks before they impact program timelines

A day in the life
You'll own a portfolio of solutions with company-wide impact, working with scientists and engineers across diverse domains, AI/ML teams, TPMs, and business unit stakeholders to orchestrate pilots and drive adoption at scale.

About the team
Sustainability Science and Innovation (SSI) is a multi-disciplinary team within WW Sustainability science, analytics, economics, statistics, machine learning, and engineering expertise. We use data across the sustainability imperatives (carbon, water, waste, biodiversity, environmental risk and more) and these skills and capabilities to identify, develop, experiment, and scale the scientific solutions and innovations necessary for Amazon, customers and partners to help them solve their hardest unmet and evolving sustainability needs and goals.

title: Event Data and Software Assistant
description:
Overview

Venue Services strives to “Exceed the Expectation – Anticipate the Need – Be the Solution” for Utah State University’s on-campus event operations. This is a unique opportunity to be involved in the behind-the-scenes action for large events on campus, from football games to the USU Howl to fine art performances.

This position serves as the primary event database specialist for Venue Services and supports the continued implementation and development of the software called SwitchBase across campus. This position will be part of the Venue Services Office Assistants team. Responsibilities include maintaining and updating the software, assisting with implementation efforts within the Office of Events venues, providing user training and support and serving as a resource for campus partners and stakeholders. The specialist will also be responsible for providing on-site event support, a responsibility that can be shared among the assistant team. This position will report to the Assistant Director of Venues.

The successful candidate should be adaptable, organized, and comfortable learning new systems in a fast-paced environment. Strong communication, problem-solving, and customer service skills are essential, as this role will collaborate with university departments, third-party contacts, and event service partners to support effective software adoption and ongoing operations.

As a part-time student position, this employee will be able to set their own in-office hours to accommodate their class schedule and event schedule. Generally, 20-25 hours in the office is expected weekly during the school year. The office is open between 7:30 am and 5:00 pm, Monday through Friday. Elevated hours per week are available during the summer months.

Responsibilities

  • Regularly work in and update the Venue Services event database software, currently SwitchBase, under established processes and procedures.

  • Provide onsite event support using SwitchBase, including monitoring event activity, documenting issues, and assisting with the tracking of operational requests as needed.
  • Assist with developing and providing training materials and training sessions for users across campus.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in administrative, operations, or event support environments

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Attention to detail and accuracy in documentation
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
  • Strong customer service and interpersonal skills
  • Strong organizational and time management skills
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines
