title: Conservation Corps Fiscal Specialist
description:
CAREER DETAILS:

CAREER TITLE: Conservation Corps Fiscal Specialist

LOCATION: AYW Headquarters, Austin,TX

DIVISION: Conservation Corps

DEPARTMENT: Finance

POSITION REPORTS TO: Chief Financial Strategy Officer

POSITION SUPERVISES: None

CLASSIFICATION: Regular, Full-time, Non-Exempt


POSITION PURPOSE:

The Conservation Corps Fiscal Specialist is responsible for the timely and accurate billing, reimbursement, accounts receivable tracking, and fiscal administration of American YouthWorks’ Conservation Corps grants, contracts, and fee-for-service projects across all operating sites. This position translates contract terms and program documentation into accurate, supportable, and collectible revenue; maintains current grant and contract balances; prepares assigned funder financial reports; monitors fiscal performance and deadlines; and ensures billing and financial records remain complete and audit-ready.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND BASIC DUTIES:

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Under the direction of the Chief Financial Strategy Officer, the Conservation Corps Fiscal Specialist performs the following duties:

  1. Contract and Grant Fiscal Administration (10%)
    1. Maintain a centralized fiscal record for each active Conservation Corps grant, contract, agreement, and fee-for-service project, including executed agreements and modifications, funding periods, contract ceilings, rates, billing methodology, grant codes, cost centers, work-order numbers, reporting requirements, deadlines, and partner billing contacts.
    2. Review the fiscal and billing requirements of new and renewed agreements and identify missing, inconsistent, or unclear terms before billing begins.
    3. Coordinate with Finance and Conservation Corps leadership to establish or verify customer records, grant codes, cost centers, billing templates, and system configurations.
    4. Track contract utilization, amendments, expiration dates, remaining balances, renewal dates, and closeout requirements.
    5. Support the Chief Financial Strategy Officer and Conservation Corps leadership with financial data for project budgets, proposals, rate calculations, renewals, and contract modifications.
  2. Billing, Reimbursement, and Accounts Receivable (40%)
    1. Prepare and submit accurate and timely invoices, reimbursement requests, payment requests, and draw packages for Conservation Corps grants, contracts, and project partners.
    2. Validate billing support against agreement requirements, including project logs, crew and member hours, work dates, locations, rates, equipment, materials, travel, work orders, cost centers, and required approvals.
    3. Confirm that billings do not exceed contract ceilings, approved budgets, available funding, or applicable period-of-performance limitations.
    4. Enter and maintain invoices in Sage MIP, Veoci, partner portals, and other approved systems in accordance with established procedures.
    5. Maintain complete, organized, and version-controlled invoice files with all required supporting documentation.
    6. Track invoice submission, approval, payment, aging, and outstanding balances and conduct timely follow-up with partners and internal staff.
    7. Research and resolve rejected invoices, payment discrepancies, unapplied receipts, incorrect funding assignments, and other routine billing issues.
    8. Conduct a monthly completeness review to confirm that all eligible Conservation Corps work has been billed or documented as pending and escalate internal delays that place revenue or deadlines at risk.
  3. Reconciliation, Budget Monitoring, and Fiscal Analysis (20%)
    1. Reconcile invoices, payments, accounts receivable, project trackers, partner records, Sage MIP balances, and grant or contract balances.
    2. Identify and escalate unbilled revenue, duplicate or unsupported charges, underbilling, overbilling, aging receivables, incorrect work-order assignments, and approaching funding limits.
    3. Monitor budget-to-actual performance for assigned Conservation Corps grants, contracts, and operating sites and communicate significant variances or emerging risks.
    4. Assist with revenue projections, cash-collection forecasts, accrual support, deferred-revenue tracking, fiscal-year closeout, and grant or contract closeout.
    5. Prepare recurring fiscal reports or dashboards showing revenue budgeted, amounts billed and collected, outstanding accounts receivable, earned but unbilled revenue, remaining balances, upcoming deadlines, and significant fiscal risks.
    6. Participate in regular fiscal review meetings with the Chief Financial Strategy Officer, Conservation Corps Director, and appropriate site leaders.
  4. Funder Reporting, Compliance, and Audit Support (10%)
    1. Prepare assigned financial reports and reimbursement documentation, including expenditure reports, payment or reimbursement forms, performance expenditure reports, SF-270s, SF-425s, and other funder-required fiscal forms.
    2. Coordinate with Conservation Corps and Compliance staff to obtain programmatic, participant, performance, and narrative information required for combined reports.
    3. Maintain audit-ready fiscal records for assigned grants, contracts, invoices, amendments, reports, and closeouts.
      Prepare documentation and respond to assigned requests for audits, monitoring visits, fiscal reviews, and funder testing.
    4. Monitor compliance with fiscal requirements related to allowable costs, cost allocation, match, indirect costs, documentation, reporting periods, and record retention.
    5. Identify fiscal exceptions or potential questioned costs and promptly escalate them to the Chief Financial Strategy Officer and appropriate program leadership.
    6. Support corrective actions related to assigned billing, documentation, reporting, or fiscal findings.
  5. Expense report review and approval (10%)
    1. Review employee expense reports in our software for accuracy and complete information.
    2. Verify itemized receipts and invoices to line items to confirm proper spending.
    3. Enforce Policies to ensure all claims follow company travel and spending rules.
    4. Flag Issues including duplicate charges, missing details, and incorrect coding and hold them for review.
    5. Communicate with staff to fix errors or ask for missing receipt copies.
    6. Approve and Process reports timely to ensure expenses are included in reimbursement billings
  6. Systems, Documentation, and Cross-Functional Support (10%)
    1. Maintain and improve billing calendars, project trackers, contract logs, reconciliation tools, standard templates, checklists, and written procedures.
    2. Establish consistent file-naming, documentation, version-control, and retention practices for Conservation Corps fiscal records.
    3. Train and support Conservation Corps staff on project documentation and submission requirements necessary for timely billing and reimbursement.
    4. Return incomplete or inconsistent billing documentation for correction and escalate recurring or deadline-sensitive issues.
    5. Collaborate with Accounting, Compliance, Development, Operations, and Conservation Corps leadership to improve communication, handoffs, controls, and fiscal workflows.
    6. Perform other related duties consistent with the purpose and classification of the position.


QUALIFICATIONS:

Minimum Required

EDUCATION / CERTIFICATION:

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, public administration, nonprofit management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and directly related experience.

EXPERIENCE:

  • Minimum 3–5 years of experience in nonprofit finance, grant management, contract administration, or similar roles.
  • Experience with invoicing, budget monitoring, financial tracking, or contract compliance.
  • Experience with Sage MIP, Veoci, funder portals, or comparable accounting and workflow systems.
  • Experience supporting fiscal audits, monitoring reviews, grant closeouts, or corrective-action processes.
  • Experience with fee-for-service billing, government work orders, and project-based revenue tracking.
  • Familiarity with conservation corps, workforce development, or multi-site program operations.

EQUIVALENT

  • 60 hours toward a bachelor’s degree with at least 12 hours in a related field and 3 years of specified work experience; OR
  • High school diploma/GED and 6–8 years of progressively responsible fiscal, grants, or contract experience with a successful track record, OR

  • A combination of education, training, and directly related experience that demonstrates the ability to perform the essential functions of the position may be considered in lieu of the formal education requirement.

Preferred

  • Experience with AmeriCorps, YouthBuild, or federal grants, municipal or governmental contracts, conservation corps, workforce development, or other multi-site nonprofit programs and federal/state grant compliance.
  • Experience preparing performance expenditure reports, expenditure reports, SF-270s, SF-425s, or similar reimbursement and financial-reporting forms.
  • Experience preparing audit documentation or supporting fiscal reviews.



KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES

KNOWLEDGE:

  • Federal grant administration and fiscal compliance requirements, including 2 CFR 200 (Uniform Guidance).
  • Nonprofit and fund accounting principles, including grant- and contract-based revenue and expense tracking.
  • Grant, contract, reimbursement, and fee-for-service billing practices.
  • Accounts receivable, reconciliations, fiscal closeout, and revenue tracking.
  • Cost allocation, budget development, forecasting, and financial reporting.
  • Contract development, administration, tracking, and reconciliation.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer, CI/CD Platform (Developer Experience)
description:
Hey there, Kubernetes people!

Dé el siguiente paso en su carrera profesional ahora: desplácese hacia abajo para leer la descripción completa del puesto y envíe su solicitud.

Every engineer here waits on CI several times a day. We want someone who finds that wait personally annoying.

Why this role exists?

Hundreds of developers push to a large Ruby on Rails monorepo, and every push lands on a runner fleet that the Developer Experience team builds, runs and keeps fast.

That fleet is self-hosted Kubernetes on bare metal in European datacentres, in the low hundreds of machines, running ephemeral GitHub Actions runners that peak above a thousand concurrent pods. We own all of it: the hardware, the clusters, the runner images, the caches and the delivery pipelines on top. We add nodes by hand rather than letting an autoscaler do it, so capacity planning is genuinely part of the job.

The leverage is unusual. Shave a minute off the average build and every engineer in the company gets that minute back, several times a day.

The mission

- Own the CI and CD Kubernetes clusters end to end: capacity, reliability, upgrades, security and cost.

- Run the self-hosted GitHub Actions platform at scale with Actions Runner Controller. Runner scale sets, ephemeral pods, docker-in-docker, and the runner images themselves.

- Keep the data services our tests depend on fast and healthy. MySQL, Redis and ClickHouse come up per job, alongside Rails application containers.

- Design and tune the caching that makes builds quick: node-local overlay, image and artifact caches we build ourselves, plus pull-through registry mirrors.

- Bring queue wait and build duration down, with measurement behind it. Instrument the platform, set targets, and show the improvement.

- Manage it all as code. Terraform planned and applied from pull requests, GitOps delivery with Flux and Argo CD, Kustomize and Helm for manifests.

- Provision and operate bare metal. Linux, networking across datacentre segments, and troubleshooting that sometimes ends up at the disk or the kernel.

- Lead incident response for the platform, run blameless postmortems, and turn each one into an alert, a guardrail or a runbook.

- Treat the platform as a product whose users are engineers. Talk to them, watch where they get stuck, and build paths that make the right thing easy.

Your day to day

- Rightsizing runner tiers against a week of CPU and memory data, then opening the pull request that changes them.

- Tracking a flaky job from a red check down to the container runtime, the kernel, or a clock that drifted.

- Adding machines to the fleet: install, enrol, network, verify, document.

- Cutting p95 queue wait by working out which stage actually blocks.

- Upgrading a cluster or a controller without anyone noticing.

- Pairing with a product engineer on a workflow that has been slow for a reason nobody has looked at yet.

Your profile

- 5+ years running production infrastructure, with Kubernetes at the centre of it.

- Real depth in Kubernetes: scheduling, requests and limits, evictions, node pressure, DaemonSets, controllers and operators. You have debugged a cluster that was lying to you.

- Strong Linux and container fundamentals. containerd or Docker internals, cgroups, namespaces, storage drivers, networking.

- Terraform and infrastructure as code, with a feel for module design and state hygiene.

- CI/CD at the platform level: shared workflows, reusable templates, runner architecture, build caching.

- Comfortable with GitHub Actions, including self-hosted runners.

- You script to automate. Bash, plus at least one of Python or Go.

- Observability as a working method. Metrics, logs, traces, dashboards and alerts that people trust, with OpenTelemetry and Prometheus style tooling.

- Operational maturity. On-call, incident command, postmortems, and the discipline to chase causes.

- Capacity and cost awareness. You can size a fleet and explain the bill.

- Clear written English. You document what you build, because the next person on call will not be you.

Bonus points

- Large Ruby on Rails test suites, and what it takes to parallelise them honestly.

- Operating MySQL, Redis or ClickHouse yourself.

- Bare metal: provisioning, hardware failure, and the different rhythm it has compared to cloud.

- Overlay and WireGuard style mesh networking, VLANs, and Kubernetes CNIs such as Cilium.

- Building internal developer tooling, portals or platform APIs.

- Supply chain and build security. Runner isolation, secret scoping, image provenance.

- Working across more than one cloud. We use AWS, Azure and Cloudflare alongside our own hardware.

- Contributions to open source infrastructure projects.

How we work

At Factorial, we believe the best products are built when people come together, in person, to collaborate, challenge ideas, and move fast. That’s why our Engineering Team follows an office-first, flexible approach.

We work on-site several days a week (80%), using that time to connect, align, and innovate as a team. However, we also support remote work when it makes sense (20%) for deep focus or personal needs.

At Factorial we don't evaluate you by years of experience but by your knowledge and skills.

We use our Career Path with a rubric framework where we define what is expected for each experience level and skill. This framework allows you to know your current level and what you need to keep growing. We love transparency, so our Career Path includes the salaries for each level, which we share during the first interview to ensure alignment.

Our Hiring Process

1. Intro Call → Chat with our Talent Partner about your journey and goals.

2. Hiring Manager Interview → Deep dive into your product mindset, teamwork, and problem-solving.

3. Technical Interview → A collaborative technical conversation with the team based on real-life problems.

4. Final Coffee Chat → A relaxed conversation with our CTO & VP of Engineering to explore our vision, culture, and your growth.

And that’s it! Feel free to request any other conversations you want, with team members or to address specific concerns at any time in the process. The whole process is remote, using videoconferencing tools!

About Factorial

At Factorial, we’re building the leading AI Business Management Software for companies of all sizes. Our platform centralizes key workflows across HR, Finance, Talent, Operations, and IT, freeing teams from manual processes so they can focus on what really matters: leading, growing, and taking care of their people.With over 1,500 employees across Europe, Asia, Africa, and America. We are one of Europe’s fastest-growing SaaS companies, proudly headquartered in Barcelona. If you're excited to shape the future of business management technology, we’d love to meet you.

We believe in diverse talent: we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and strongly encourage people of diverse experiences and identities to apply.

We believe in inclusion: we are committed to equal opportunities and actively promote workplace inclusion of people with disabilities. If you would like to learn more about our inclusive recruitment processes, you are welcome to indicate so optionally and we will share additional information with you.

Our Values

- We own it: We take responsibility for every project. We make decisions, not excuses.

- We learn and teach: We're dedicated to learning something new every day and, above all, share it.

- We partner: Every decision is a team decision. We trust each other.

- We grow fast: We act fast. We think that the worst mistake is not learning from them.

Wanna learn more about us? Check our website! xqbhyrx

Perks of being part of Factorial

- High growth, multicultural and friendly environment

- Alan as private health insurance

- Healthy life with Wellhub (Gyms, pools, outdoor classes)

- Save expenses with Cobee

- Language classes

- Breakfast in the office and organic fruit

title: Deputy Director of Indigenous Programs
description:
Working at Yale means contributing to a better tomorrow. Whether you are a current resident of our New Haven-based community, eligible for opportunities through the New Haven Hiring Initiative, or a newcomer, interested in exploring all that Yale has to offer, your talents and contributions are welcome. Discover your opportunities at Yale!

Overview

The Deputy Director of Indigenous Programs will drive the growth and day-to-day development of YCEJ's Indigenous Programs, with a particular focus on building the center's Indigenous co-management program, accelerating co-management partnerships in the United States, mainstreaming Indigenous knowledge, and stewarding an appropriate global footprint for the program's international work. This role requires someone with a deep respect for and knowledge of Indigenous cultures, traditions, and environmental challenges, along with a proven ability to design, fund, and deliver programs. The Deputy Director will liaise with Indigenous communities, scholars, and leaders in the United States and internationally to develop, implement, and evaluate initiatives that further the mission of the YCEJ. The position is part-time with the possibility of conversion to full-time within the year.


Key Responsibilities

  • Co-Management Program Development: Lead the development of YCEJ's Indigenous co-management program.
  • Capacity-building initiatives with Indigenous communities and partners in the United States and the Amazon, with potential expansion to New Zealand.
  • Design and launch of a certificate program in Indigenous co-management as the program's cornerstone offering, including curriculum development, partner and faculty engagement, and institutional approvals.
  • Interim programming while the certificate program is being built, including field workshops, webinars, and community needs assessments.
  • Accelerating Co-Management in the United States: Appropriately accelerate co-management work in the U.S., including building and deepening partnerships with the National Congress of American Indians (NCAI), the Native American Rights Fund (NARF), and other tribal organizations and agencies engaged in co-management of lands, waters, and resources.
  • Mainstreaming Indigenous Knowledge: Build and lead a program to help mainstream Indigenous knowledge within research, education, policy, and environmental decision-making, in ways that respect Indigenous data sovereignty and intellectual property and that are co-designed with Indigenous knowledge holders.
  • Global Footprint: Manage an appropriate global footprint for YCEJ's Indigenous Programs, prioritizing engagements (including in the Amazon and potentially New Zealand) that align with the center's strategic vision, capacity, and community partnerships. Resource Development and Fundraising: Secure funding for Indigenous Programs, including grants, philanthropic gifts, and institutional partnerships; manage program budgets; and ensure the allocation of resources in line with strategic objectives.
  • Strategic Leadership: Support the development and oversight of Indigenous programs in line with YCEJ's strategic vision, ensuring alignment with the broader goals of the center.
  • Research and Scholarship: Collaborate with Indigenous communities and scholars to conduct and promote research on environmental justice issues specific to Indigenous communities.
  • Teaching and Training: Teach classes and/or conduct workshops in area(s) of expertise.
  • Community Engagement: Build and strengthen partnerships with Indigenous communities, leaders, and organizations, fostering mutual respect and collaboration.
  • Team Management: Help build, lead, and mentor a team, fostering an inclusive and culturally respectful working environment.
  • Continuous Learning: Stay updated on Indigenous environmental justice issues, challenges, and opportunities to ensure the relevancy of the center's programs.

Required Skills & Abilities

1. Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of Indigenous cultures, traditions, and contemporary issues.

2. Proven track record of successful program development and implementation, ideally including educational or certificate programs.

3. Demonstrated success in securing and managing grants or other funding sources.

4. Strong leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills.

5. Ability to navigate academic, policy, and community spaces with cultural sensitivity and respect.

Principal Responsibilities

1. Directs one or more functional areas within an administrative department of the University and ensure compliance with University policies and procedures. 2. Directs analytic and research support for educational policies and planning and develops and approves administrative policies affecting assigned functional areas of the University. 3. Directs and establishes parameters for major projects for the department and University. 4. Interprets federal policies and regulations and educates staff and administration about regulations, restrictions, and the legal responsibilities of the University. 5. Directs and implements policy and program modifications and develops standards to ensure compliance with federal, state and local regulations. 6. Develops and administers an operating budget for the assigned department consistent with University policies and procedures. 7. Develops cost savings objectives and goals; authorizes major purchases and negotiates contracts that range from routine to complex in nature. 8. Establishes and implements long- and short-range goals for the functional area consistent with University goals and objectives. 9. Directs the development of related automated systems to support the function; determines office policies and procedures for use of automated systems. 10. Directs the evaluation and selection of vendors and negotiates contract details including work steps and pricing with the vendors on behalf of the assigned functional area. 11. Works with internal and external contacts to solve problems that range from routine to complex in nature. 12. Represents the University in discussions and negotiations with various governmental agencies. 13. Directs a staff of exempt and nonexempt employees. 14. May perform other duties as assigned. Required Education and Experience Bachelor’s Degree in related field. Five years of experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

title: Patient Services Representative
description:
ABOUT OUR ORGANIZATION

Orthopaedics East & Sports Medicine Center is Eastern North Carolina's premier orthopedic specialty practice, headquartered in Greenville. Our orthopedic surgeons - most of whom are fellowship-trained - along with our physician assistants, physical therapists, and occupational therapists, provide a variety of general and specialized operative and non-operative orthopedic services to meet the musculoskeletal needs of patients across Eastern North Carolina. Services include joint replacement, sports medicine, pediatric orthopedics, worker's compensation care, fracture care, regenerative medicine, bracing and casting, physical therapy, and on-site X-ray and MRI imaging. We have served as the preferred providers of orthopedic care for East Carolina University Athletics for more than 30 years.


Orthopaedics East offers a comprehensive benefits package. Full-Time employees are eligible for Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, along with employer-provided Life, AD&D, Short-term, and Long-term insurance. Full-Time employees also receive paid holidays and a monthly accrual of paid time off (PTO), and eligible employees may participate in the Practice's 401(k) deferral program.


JOB PURPOSE

The primary duties of this position are patient check-in duties, patient check-out duties, and patient registration responsibilities. Also, other duties as assigned by Supervisor.


This position requires compliance with OrthoEast's compliance standards, including its Code of Conduct, Compliance Program, and policies and procedures. Such compliance will be an element required as part of the Patient Services Representative's job duties and is considered during performance evaluations.


Employment begins with a 90-day probationary period, during which performance, attendance, and suitability for the position are evaluated. Completion of the probationary period does not change the at-will nature of employment, which may be ended by either the employee or the Practice at any time, with or without cause or notice.


DETAILED WORK ACTIVITIES

Promote the mission, vision, and values of the Practice.
- Greets and directs all patients, salespeople, and visitors as appropriate.
- Verifies patient registration is up to date and accurate.
- Process and scan pre-registration information.
- Process paperwork and verify I.D.'s for PHI picked up at the front desk.
- Collect copays from patients.
- Verify that all patients have been marked arrived.
- Schedules phone appointments as time allows.
- Manages fail to keep appointments.
- Re-schedules appointments as assigned.
- Collects patient demographic information and health benefit information and enters it into the practice management system.
- Verifies insurance benefits.
- Other related duties as required.


WORK CONTENT

Work Environment

This is an on-site role at the Practice. The schedule is subject to change based on Practice need to accommodate patient volume. Work is performed at the front desk of a busy orthopedic medical practice with frequent in-person and telephone contact with patients and visitors.

Physical Demands

  • Extended periods of sitting, keyboarding, and talking on the telephone.
    - Occasional lifting and/or moving up to 10 pounds.
    - Must be able to receive and respond to detailed verbal and written instructions.


SKILLS

Basic Skills

Critical Thinking - Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to complex technical problems.
- Systems Thinking - Understanding how components of the platform interact and how changes in one area affect overall outcomes, reliability, and security.
- Ownership & Accountability - Taking initiative on features and incidents end-to-end, monitoring and assessing one's own work, and taking corrective action without prompting.
- Active Listening - Giving full attention to stakeholders and teammates, understanding requirements being conveyed, and asking clarifying questions as appropriate.
- Reading & Writing Comprehension - Understanding and producing clear technical and work-related documentation.


KNOWLEDGE

Education and Experience

Required:

- High School diploma or (GED) required.
- Minimum of one-year clerical experience.
- Basic computer skills required.
- Experience in maintaining confidentiality in dealing with sensitive issues.
- Proven ability in making sound and accurate judgments in problem solving work issues.
- Successful record of follow through on commitments and demonstrated dependability.

Preferred:

- Clerical experience in a medical office setting.


JOB REQUIREMENTS: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed must be representative of the knowledge, skills, minimum education, training, licensure, experience, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Orthopaedics East & Sports Medicine Center is an equal opportunity employer and provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with applicable law.

### Description

**_The City of Fairfield is accepting applications for a Building Inspector I within the Community Development Department!_**

Are you ready to play a vital role in ensuring the safety, structural integrity, and high quality of development in one of California's most vibrant communities? The City of Fairfield is seeking a dedicated and detail-oriented professional to join our Building Division as a **Building Inspector I**. In this role, you will serve as a frontline representative of the City, working directly with contractors, developers, and homeowners to inspect residential, commercial, and industrial structures for compliance with building, plumbing, mechanical, and electrical codes. If you possess a strong eye for detail, excellent communication skills, and a commitment to public safety, Fairfield offers an exceptional environment to advance your career and make a lasting impact on our growing community.

_Interviews are tentatively scheduled for_ _November 5, 2026_

**WORKING CONDITIONS:**

Work is performed primarily outside and may include exposure to construction noise, heights, potential electrical shock, and construction machinery. May include exposure to unsanitary conditions, odors, and hazardous chemicals. At times, work may include reviewing plans at a desk and covering front counter duties.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

Duties may include transporting light to heavy objects (up to 50 pounds), reaching, pushing, pulling, crawling, climbing, stooping, prolonged periods of standing; walking on uneven surfaces, stepping over trenches, walking on roofs up to 8/12 pitch; climbing ladders and scaffolding two to four stories in height; using a computer keyboard / tablet for data input and typing reports. Ability to see well enough to read gauges, manufacturers' labels and fine print on plans; depth perception to climb ladders and walk on roofs and multi-level framing; ability to distinguish colors to determine correct wiring.

**DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS:**

The Building Inspector I/II/III classifications are flexibly staffed. Incumbents may advance to the higher level after gaining experience, obtaining the required certifications and demonstrating a level of proficiency that meets the qualifications of the higher-level class.

**SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXCERCISED:**

Supervision is received from the Building Inspector Supervisor or other management staff. Training, guidance and direction may be provided by the Senior Building Inspector. The Building Inspector III may provide limited guidance to other inspectors as needed.

### Minimum Qualifications

Experience:

One (1) full-time year of building inspection experience with a public agency inspecting all of the major trade fields (carpentry, mechanical, electrical, plumbing) is required.

OR

Four (4) full-time years of responsible and relevant journey-level experience in either one of the major trade fields or in the performance of a wide variety of building trades work performed in conformance with standard building, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing codes are required.

An Associate's degree in Building Construction / Inspection Technology may be substituted for one (1) year of the required experience.

Education:

Education equivalent to completion of the twelfth grade is required. Related college course work and certification with the International Conference of Building Officials (ICBO), International Code Council (ICC), or American Construction Inspectors Association (ACIA) are highly desirable.

**REQUIRED LICENSES AND / OR CERTIFICATES:**

- Possession of a valid California Driver's license is required.

- Certification from the ICC as a Residential Building Inspector - or equivalent certification under the ICBO legacy program - is required to be complete within the first six (6) months in the position. Certification shall be maintained as a condition of employment.


### Examples of Duties

**For the complete job description please visit:** [**https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/fairfield/classspecs**](https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/fairfield/classspecs)

**THE SELECTION PROCESS:**

Based on the information provided in the application documents, the best-qualified applicants will be invited for further examination. All applicants meeting the minimum qualifications are not guaranteed advancement through any subsequent phase of the examination. Depending upon the number of applications received, the examination may consist of an application screening, written and/or practical exam, oral interview, or any combination.

**HOW TO APPLY:**

Candidates must submit an online application via NeoGov/Governmentjobs.com by 5:00 p.m. of the closing date. If you have any difficulties submitting your online application, please call NeoGov's **Applicant Support Line at (855) 524-5627.**

**Mac users please note: To ensure compatibility, please use Google Chrome and ensure iOS settings are up-to-date.**

If you feel you will need a reasonable accommodation for any portion of the testing/interview process, please contact Human Resources at (707) 428-7394 at least 1 week prior to the application deadline or examination date.

**REFERENCE CHECKS:**

The City utilizes an electronic reference check process to gather references of candidates once mutual interest is established.Please note that if you include your current supervisor in the “References” section of your application, they may be contacted once you have accepted a conditional job offer from the City.

Candidates are encouraged to notify anyone they list in the “References” section to help ensure a timely response. When listing references, please identify persons who can assess your professional qualifications in the context of the workplace. Examples include former colleagues/supervisors, mentors, etc. If you have limited or no work experience, you may identify personal references familiar with your qualifications that correlate to workplace experiences. Examples include teachers, volunteer coordinators, mentors, etc.

title: Scheduling Coordinator - SNF - Logan (55314)
description:
scheduling Coordinator - SNF

Job Description

Department

Nursing

Reports to

Administrator or Director of Nursing

Reporting to this position

CNAs

Job Classification

Non-Exempt

Position Purpose

Provides education, scheduling, guidance to certified nursing assistants in accordance with care plans, facility policies and procedures and at the direction of supervisor(s).

Required Qualifications

Minimum requirements include the following:

  1. Certified Nursing Assistant in good standing with the state.
  2. High school diploma or equivalent (Preferred)
  3. Current CPR/BLS certification
  4. Food Handler’s Permit (as required)

Must have no disciplinary action in effect against certification.

At least one year of experience as a certified nursing assistant.

Major Duties and Responsibilities

Responsible for developing, implementing and maintaining the schedules for nursing assistants (NA), certified nursing assistants (CNA), medication aides, restorative aides and licensed nurses and other departments as needed or required according to PPD and budget

May assist with hiring and disciplinary action involving nursing assistants and certified nursing assistants.

May assist with education and audits to ensure job duties are completed, charting completed, care needs are done per best practices

May provide supportive services to nurse(s) and other staff as needed and performs duties as assigned.

May assist residents with or perform activities of daily living for residents in accordance with care plans and established policies and procedures.

May assist resident with lifting, turning, moving, positioning, and transporting into and out of beds, chairs, bathtubs, wheelchairs, lifts, etc.

May assist with coordinating dining room services at assigned mealtimes, including set-up and clean-up, meal tray delivery, feeding assistance, and documentation of meal intake.

May deliver nutritional supplements or snacks to residents at assigned times and provides assistance as necessary to ensure intake. Documents intake accordingly.

May assist with weighing residents according to facility policy, and records weight in designated locations. Reports weight changes to nurse and supervisor.

May assist with tracking the condition of the resident’s skin. Reports any presence of pressure areas, skin breakdown or skin tears to nurse and supervisor.

May assist nursing staff in carrying out toileting program activities.

Completes flow sheets when required to indicate that the specified task was done. Documents the progress of each resident as directed by supervisor.

Keeps nurse and supervisor informed of factors that interfere with being able to perform the work as assigned (i.e. resident refusal, reassigned to nursing unit).

Reports changes in a resident’s condition to the resident’s nurse and supervisor.

Additional Assigned Tasks

  1. Treats all residents with dignity and respect. Promotes and protects all residents’ rights.
  2. Establishes a culture of compliance by adhering to all facility policies and procedures. Complies with standards of business conduct, and state/federal regulations and guidelines.
  3. Follows appropriate safety and hygiene measures at all times to protect residents and themselves.
  4. Maintains confidentiality of protected health information, including verbal, written, and electronic communications.
  5. Reports noncompliance with policies, procedures, regulations, or breaches in confidentiality to appropriate personnel. Reports any retaliation or discrimination to HR or compliance officer.
  6. Reports any allegations of abuse, neglect, misappropriation of property, exploitation, or mistreatment of residents to supervisor and/or administrator. Protects residents from abuse, and cooperates with all investigations.
  7. Reports any occupational exposures to blood, body fluids, infectious materials, and/or hazardous chemicals in accordance with facility policy.
  8. Participates in all life safety and emergency drills and trainings. Fulfills responsibilities as assigned during implementation or activation of the facility’s emergency plan.
  9. Reports work-related injuries and illnesses immediately to supervisor.
  10. Follows established infection control policies and procedures.
  11. As a condition of employment, completes all assigned training and skills competency.
  12. Attend care-plan meetings of assigned residents.
  13. Participate in QAPI or facility assessment activities as needed, such as carrying out duties assigned as part of a performance improvement committee.
  14. Accept certified nursing assistant assignments as staffing needs require. Perform certified nursing assistant duties as assigned, in accordance with facility policies and procedures.
  15. Use proper lifting and body mechanics while delivering care to residents.

Personal Skills and Traits Desired/Physical Requirements/Working Conditions

  1. Ability to read, write, speak and understand the English language.
  2. Must be a supportive team member, contribute to and be an example of team work.
  3. Ability to make independent decisions when circumstances warrant such action.
  4. Ability to deal tactfully with personnel, residents, family members, visitors, government agencies/personnel and the general public.
  5. Must have patience, tact, and willingness to deal with difficult residents, family and staff.
  6. Must be able to relay information concerning a resident’s condition.
  7. Must not pose a threat to the health and safety of other individuals in the workplace.
  8. Must be able to move intermittently throughout the workday.
  9. Meets general health requirements according to facility policy, including medical and physical exams and checking immunity status to various infectious diseases.
  10. Ability to work beyond normal working hours and on weekends and holidays when necessary.
  11. Ability to assist in evacuation of residents during emergency situations.
  12. Ability to bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, perform overhead lifting and perform other common physical movements as needed for the position.
  13. May be subject to falls, burns from equipment, and/or odors throughout the day; encounter reactions from dust, tobacco smoke, disinfectants, and other air contaminants.
  14. Subject to exposure to infectious waste, diseases and/or conditions which include AIDS, Coronavirus, Hepatitis B, and Tuberculosis.
  15. May be subject to hostile or emotional residents, family members, visitors or personnel.
  16. Strong listening skills and ability to deal with conflict with professionalism and courtesy.
  17. Basic computer skills, including ability to navigate electronic medical record systems.
  18. Positive interpersonal relationship skills, including with persons of all ages and cultures.
  19. Ability to walk, stand, sit, bend, and stoop for extended periods.
  20. Dexterity of hands and fingers to perform resident care.
  21. Ability to lift, move, push or pull a minimum of 35 pounds.
  22. May work beyond assigned working hours, including weekends and holidays, when necessary.

Compliance as a Condition of Employment and Performance Appraisal

Agreement to abide by all standards, policies, and procedures of the facility, including the facility’s compliance and ethics program, is a condition of employment. Compliance will be a factor in evaluating job performance. Violations, including failure to report violations, will result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination.

This job description is intended to convey the general scope of the major duties and responsibilities inherent in this position. Other tasks not listed here may be assigned if the tasks are similar or related to the essential duties of the position. Periodic revision may be necessary to reflect changes in expectations placed on the long-term care industry by various governmental agencies. This job description will be reviewed and/or revised annually and as needed.

Individual performance will be evaluated using the following scale:

  1. Unsatisfactory: Achieves results that are far less than the standards identified for the performance factors rated.
  2. Needs Improvement: Achieves results that are less than the standards identified for the performance factors rated. Exhibits the potential to become a competent performer. May be new to job or need skill development.

  4. Exceeds Standards: Achieves results that usually exceed the standards identified for the performance factors rated.

title: LIFE Services Worker/Guide - Community Living
description:
Temporary Position - October 1, 2026 - March 31, 2027


Kinsight is an accredited non-profit organization. We work alongside families of children, youth and adults with developmental delays or disabilities to support growth, development and personal well-being. We work with hundreds of community members and professionals to welcome and include all people, and foster vibrant and healthy communities. We serve the communities of New Westminster, Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, Port Moody, Anmore and Belcarra. Our mission is to provide options and opportunities for people to have meaningful relationships and fulfilling lives.


About L.I.F.E. Services

L.I.F.E. stands for Learning, Inclusion, Friendship and Employment.
The program is part of CLBC’s Community Inclusion category of services. It is available to anyone served by CLBC who has an employment goal, and who also want support to increase confidence and independence, connect to the community, learn new things, build friendships and a network of natural support around them. L.I.F.E. Services are designed to respond to the natural rhythm of a person’s life, and adjusts supports provided over time in response to people's changing goals and needs. The supports offered through L.I.F.E. services enable people to personalize, direct and evaluate their services in a way that works for them.


Kinsight is seeking a L.I.F.E. Services Guide

The Guide works closely with people who use the service to co-design, deliver, evaluate and continually improve the effectiveness of the service. L.I.F.E. Services focus on a blend of supports aimed at assisting people to achieve their ambitions related to employment, community connection and lifelong learning. L.I.F.E. service strategies incorporate the development and strengthening of informal support networks and personal skill and confidence enhancement.

We think the Guide is someone who would describe themselves like this…

“I have a knack for unconventional problem solving and huge reservoir of ideas I am eager to share. I am up to date on all the current best practices around supporting people to connect in community, expand their informal support circles and find work, and yet I am ready to push forward and invent the next best practices. My knowledge, experience and insights fuel my forward movement rather than anchor me in place.


And, I am happy with a flexible work schedule based within Greater Vancouver/Lower Mainland. I am savvy with technology and comfortable connecting with others virtually.


And, I have the energy and optimism to start something new!


Does that sound like you?

If so, please apply and include a cover letter and resume.


*HOURS:

37.5 hours/week - primarily Monday to Friday - on a flex schedule. This position requires flexible working hours, including some evenings/weekends as required by the needs, ambitions and schedules of the people supported. *May be required to work evenings and weekends.

LOCATIONS:

  • Tri-Cities, New Westminster and surrounding communities


QUALIFICATIONS:

title: Senior Software Engineer - Reliability, Infrastructure, and Tooling
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Software Engineer - Reliability, Infrastructure, and Tooling based in Italy.

This is a senior engineering role focused on building reliable, scalable infrastructure for demanding real-time and AI workloads.
You’ll work closely with product engineering teams to design systems that are secure, maintainable, observable, and resilient at global scale.
The role goes beyond traditional operations, combining infrastructure engineering, reliability, tooling, and hands-on product development.
You’ll tackle complex challenges involving distributed systems, Kubernetes, networking, real-time media, and secure execution environments.
Your work will help engineering teams self-serve infrastructure and reliability capabilities without creating unnecessary operational bottlenecks.
You’ll also contribute to incident management, on-call practices, architectural decisions, and long-term reliability improvements.
This is an opportunity to work remotely with experienced engineers while contributing to infrastructure supporting billions of real-time interactions.

Accountabilities

  • Ramp up on a complex global architecture involving distributed databases, messaging systems, networking infrastructure, Kubernetes, and other core platform technologies, identifying areas of reliability debt and improvement.

  • Design and ship reliability-focused engineering work directly within production codebases, including load balancing, load shedding, instrumentation, scalability, and efficiency improvements.

  • Build and evolve internal infrastructure and developer tooling that enables product engineering teams to independently operate reliable workloads.

  • Partner closely with product development teams to co-design systems and ensure reliability, security, maintainability, and operational readiness are considered throughout development.

  • Develop observability capabilities that make system behavior measurable, understandable, and actionable, using appropriate signals and visualization techniques.

  • Participate in a shared on-call rotation and contribute to effective incident response, investigation, remediation, and prevention of recurring reliability issues.

  • Investigate complex system-level problems across distributed infrastructure, networking, application behavior, and production environments.

  • Improve configuration management and infrastructure practices across diverse systems, reducing unnecessary complexity, errors, and technical debt.

  • Contribute technical perspectives to architectural discussions and help establish engineering practices that support both short-term delivery and long-term scalability.

  • Support systems with demanding workloads, including real-time media, secure customer code execution, advanced networking, and other highly concurrent services.

  • Collaborate with engineering partners on potentially contentious reliability and operational decisions with clarity, pragmatism, and strong technical judgment.

  • Automate repetitive operational processes wherever possible to improve engineering efficiency and reduce manual intervention.

    • Requirements

    • Strong professional experience building and operating non-trivial production applications, particularly systems involving high concurrency, distributed workloads, or complex control loops.

    • Significant experience with Kubernetes or an equivalent large-scale container orchestration platform.

    • Strong understanding of Linux internals and networking, with the ability to investigate issues across multiple layers of a production system.

    • Proven experience using observability, monitoring, logging, and related tooling to diagnose difficult production problems.

    • Experience operating large-scale, globally distributed systems, including the configuration management, reliability challenges, and technical debt that emerge as systems grow.

    • Experience responding to and managing complex production incidents, including identifying root causes and implementing durable corrective actions.

    • Experience operating open-source infrastructure technologies such as Kafka, ClickHouse, or comparable distributed systems.

    • Strong systems-thinking skills and an ability to reason about infrastructure in terms of signals, feedback, dependencies, and control mechanisms.

    • Strong communication and collaboration skills, particularly when working with partner engineering teams and navigating competing priorities.

    • A pragmatic approach to engineering that balances immediate delivery needs with long-term maintainability, reliability, and operational cost.

    • A strong interest in observability, reliability engineering, clean configuration, automation, and reducing operational complexity.

    • Nice to have: experience with data engineering and analytics.

    • Nice to have: experience with global Layer 3 networking.

    • Nice to have: experience operating systems with long-lived workloads such as real-time media.

    • Nice to have: experience in Google SRE or another high-scale reliability engineering environment.

    • Nice to have: experience working with compliance frameworks such as PCI.

      • Benefits

      • Equity participation as part of the overall compensation package.

      • Fully remote work with opportunities for collaboration across a globally distributed organization.

      • Health, dental, and vision benefits.

      • Opportunity to work on infrastructure supporting large-scale real-time and AI applications.

      • Opportunity to contribute to open-source projects alongside experienced engineers.

      • Exposure to challenging distributed-systems problems involving real-time media, secure compute, networking, Kubernetes, and globally distributed infrastructure.

title: Senior Technical Animator
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Animator based in Spain.

This is an opportunity to play a key role in developing advanced animation technology for ambitious AAA/AA+ game projects.
You will help shape character pipelines and runtime animation systems in Unreal Engine, with a strong focus on Animation Blueprints and Control Rig.
The role combines hands-on technical animation, character rigging, scripting, optimization, and creative problem-solving.
You will collaborate closely with animators, artists, engineers, and technical leadership to translate creative requirements into robust technical solutions.
You will also research new techniques, improve workflows, and help establish best practices across the animation pipeline.
As a senior contributor, you will provide guidance and mentorship to other technical animators while contributing to project planning and delivery.
The position is fully remote and offers the flexibility to work with an international game development team from anywhere in Europe.

Accountabilities

  • Contribute to the technical vision for character animation pipelines and runtime animation systems within Unreal Engine.
  • Design, implement, and maintain complex animation systems, with particular emphasis on Animation Blueprints, State Machines, and Control Rig.
  • Integrate new characters by creating and implementing Physics and Cloth assets and optimizing Level of Detail (LOD) settings.
  • Research, prototype, and introduce new technical animation techniques that improve animation quality, production workflows, and team efficiency.
  • Create and maintain high-quality character and weapon rigs in Maya using internal rigging tools and established technical standards.
  • Skin high-density characters while ensuring high-quality and efficient deformation.
  • Modify and adapt Python-based rig definitions to accommodate unique character requirements while maintaining consistency across the codebase.
  • Work closely with engineers and other technical specialists to resolve complex technical challenges and ensure animation systems remain performant and stable.
  • Partner with the Technical Animation Lead and Director to translate artistic and gameplay requirements into effective technical solutions.
  • Provide technical guidance, feedback, coaching, and mentorship to junior and mid-level technical animators.
  • Document technical animation workflows, standards, and best practices to promote consistency and quality across projects.
  • Track progress, contribute to task evaluation and scheduling, and communicate upcoming priorities effectively.

    • Requirements:

    • 5+ years of professional experience in technical animation within the games industry, including experience operating at a senior level.
    • Proven experience shipping at least one AA+ game title in a technical animation role.
    • Expert-level knowledge of Unreal Engine, particularly Animation Blueprints, State Machines, and Control Rig.
    • Strong understanding of dynamic asset systems, especially Physics and Cloth assets.
    • Demonstrated expertise in Maya character rigging and skinning, particularly for realistic characters and high-density assets.
    • Strong proficiency in Python tools programming and the ability to modify and maintain Python-based rigging systems.
    • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with artists, animators, engineers, and technical leadership.
    • Strong problem-solving abilities and an interest in researching new technical approaches and improving animation workflows.
    • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a distributed, multidisciplinary team.
    • C++ proficiency is desirable.
    • Experience with procedural animation techniques is an advantage.
    • Passion for and knowledge of the Action-RPG or Soulslike genre is desirable.
    • A gameplay portfolio demonstrating relevant technical animation and rigging work is expected; creature-related work is particularly welcome.
    • Applicants must have the right to work in the country where they reside.

      • Benefits:

      • 5-month freelance contract with an immediate start.
      • Fully remote work arrangement.
      • Flexible working schedule with core collaboration hours from 10 AM to 4 PM CET.
      • Opportunity to work on ambitious, high-profile game projects with cutting-edge animation technology.
      • Collaboration with talented international artists, animators, engineers, and game development professionals.
      • Opportunity to contribute to advanced Unreal Engine animation systems and modern technical animation workflows.
      • International and diverse remote working environment.
      • Inclusive workplace committed to welcoming people regardless of background, identity, age, disability, or social status.
      • Opportunity to work from the Netherlands while collaborating with a distributed European team.
      • Freelance compensation structured around a daily rate in EUR, with the rate determined based on experience and engagement terms.

description:

title: Licensing Operations Lead
description:
About Quad Lock 🚀
Quad Lock is one of Australia’s fastest-growing companies and a certified Great Place to Work. Based in Melbourne, Quad Lock revolutionised the smartphone mounting game with our patented case-based mounting system. Originally launched in 2011, the Quad Lock range now includes mounts for Cycling, Motorcycling, Driving, Running, Marine and a range of Lifestyle options. To date, millions of Quad Lock products have been shipped to over 100 countries and sales continue to grow worldwide at a rapid pace.

About our People 👥
At Quad Lock not only do we work hard and love what we do, we are also a great bunch of people with a diverse range of interests. We have keen cyclists and motorbike riders, runners and car enthusiasts (of course). But did you know we also have movie buffs, musicians and entrepreneurs, but most importantly we’re all super proud to be part of the Quad Lock team.

About the Role 💭

We're looking for a Licensing Operations Lead to own the commercial engine behind Quad Lock's licensed product ranges. This role turns licence agreements into commercial outcomes: leading range-level planning, protecting licence terms, and driving cross-functional execution across Finance, Operations and Product.
Working hand in hand with the Global Head of Sports Marketing, the role ensures every licensed range launches on time, performs against target and strengthens our partnerships with world-leading brands. A great opportunity to bring your commercial expertise to a highly collaborative role, connecting teams and partners to help our licensed ranges thrive globally.
#LI-CG1

What You'll Do 🏎️

  • Lead the commercial planning and outcomes for Quad Lock's licensed product ranges, owning range-level revenue forecasts, margin targets and sell-through performance across all markets

  • Collaborate with the Global Head of Sports Marketing on licence terms and conditions, and ensure they are followed across the business, including royalty obligations, minimum guarantees, territory and channel restrictions, approval workflows and brand usage requirements

  • Hold cross-functional accountability with Finance, Operations and Product teams on all licensed products. This includes:

  • Finance: royalty calculations, reporting and reconciliation, minimum guarantee tracking, licensor statements, and margin and pricing analysis for licensed SKUs

  • Operations: demand planning and inventory management for licensed ranges, purchase order timing against launch windows and licence periods, and end-of-licence sell-through planning

  • Product: licensed range development milestones, licensor design and sample approval workflows, and packaging and compliance sign-off

  • Support end-to-end go-to-market plans for licensed ranges, from launch timing and channel strategy through to campaign approvals and post-launch performance reviews

  • Act as the operational point of contact for licensors on approvals and reporting, supporting the Global Head of Sports Marketing on renewals and new licence opportunities

  • Track and report licensed range performance against commercial targets, providing regular updates to leadership

What You'll Bring 🤝

  • Proven commercial planning experience including: building range forecasts, margin models and revenue targets, and delivering against them

  • Proven experience in commercial, licensing or category management roles within consumer products or related industries

  • Licensing experience with a working knowledge of licence agreements, royalty structures, minimum guarantees and licensor approval processes

  • Strong cross-functional collaborator, with a track record of driving outcomes across finance, operations and product teams

  • Experience supporting go-to-market execution across retail, distribution and e-commerce channels

  • Sharp analytical and reporting skills, confident presenting commercial performance to senior stakeholders

  • Experience in consumer products, sporting goods or lifestyle brands (highly regarded, not essential)

What it’s like to work at Quad Lock 👀

🌐 Employee Assistance Program for team members and their families

You’ll join a highly cohesive, vibrant and collaborative culture in a business where you can continue to build your skill set. This is a chance to grow and develop your career whilst working in an environment with colleagues that love what they do, encourage innovation and bring a contagious energy to work every day!

title: Proof Listener
description:
Pocket FM is the world's largest audio-series platform, where powerful stories travel effortlessly across languages, cultures, and continents. From India and the US to Europe and beyond, we're redefining how stories are created, discovered, and experienced across the globe.

With one of the largest creator ecosystems in entertainment, Pocket FM is home to millions of listeners and an ever-growing catalog of original serialized content. We're building the future of storytelling by bringing together exceptional writers, creators, and creative leaders to develop stories audiences can't stop listening to.

About the Role

Pocket FM is looking for Proof Listeners to help ensure the quality and consistency of our Japanese audio content before it reaches listeners. This is a hands-on quality assurance role focused on listening to completed audio episodes, identifying audio, narration, pronunciation, and other production-related issues, and accurately documenting them for the relevant teams.

As a Proof Listener, you will listen carefully to full-length audio episodes, identify any errors or inconsistencies, and log each issue in Pocket FM's CMS with an accurate timestamp and clear description. You will be trained on Pocket FM's quality standards, review process, and CMS workflow to ensure issues are identified and reported consistently and accurately.

The ideal candidate has professional experience in fictional audio entertainment, such as audio dramas, audiobooks, podcasts, or voice-over production, and has a strong understanding of Japanese-language audio and narration quality. Experience in proofreading, proof-listening, editorial review, or audio quality assurance is also highly relevant.

Responsibilities

  • Listen to full audio episodes carefully and systematically to identify errors, inconsistencies, and quality issues.

  • Review audio for issues including, but not limited to, abrupt audio changes or jerks, glitches, distortion, incorrect or inconsistent pronunciation, narration issues, missing or repeated audio, unnatural pauses, and other production or listening-quality concerns.

  • Evaluate Japanese-language narration and dialogue for pronunciation, wording, delivery, and other issues that may impact the listener experience.

  • Identify the precise timestamp at which each issue occurs.

  • Accurately document each identified issue, including the timestamp, type of issue, and a clear description of the problem.

  • Log all identified errors into Pocket FM's CMS portal using the prescribed review and documentation process.

  • Follow Pocket FM's audio quality guidelines and review standards consistently across episodes.

  • Distinguish genuine audio or content-quality issues from acceptable variations based on the quality standards provided during training.

  • Ensure reported errors are specific, actionable, and sufficiently detailed for the relevant production teams to investigate and resolve.

  • Maintain a high level of attention to detail and consistency when reviewing long-form fictional audio content.

  • Complete assigned audio reviews within expected timelines and communicate any issues that may affect delivery.

  • Incorporate feedback from the quality team and continuously improve accuracy and consistency in identifying and categorizing errors.

  • Maintain confidentiality of unreleased Pocket FM content and any information accessed as part of the freelance engagement.

Qualifications

  • Professional experience in fictional audio entertainment is required, such as audio dramas, audiobooks, podcasts, voice-over production, or other narrative-driven audio content.

  • Native-level or highly proficient Japanese language skills are required, with a strong understanding of Japanese pronunciation, dialogue, and natural spoken language.

  • Professional experience in audio production, audio editing, sound production, voice production, or a related field is highly preferred.

  • Experience with proofreading, proof-listening, editorial review, content quality assurance, or similar detail-oriented creative work is highly preferred.

  • Strong ability to listen attentively to long-form audio and identify subtle inconsistencies or quality issues.

  • Excellent attention to detail and ability to identify and document issues accurately.

  • Ability to identify the precise timestamp of an issue and clearly describe what is wrong.

  • Strong written communication skills, particularly the ability to write concise and actionable issue descriptions in Japanese.

  • English-language proficiency is a strong plus, particularly for communicating with cross-functional teams and documenting or discussing issues with non-Japanese-speaking team members.

  • Comfortable working with digital tools and web-based content management systems; experience with CMS platforms is a plus.

  • Ability to follow established quality standards, review guidelines, and workflows consistently.

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple episodes and review assignments independently.

  • Reliable internet connection and access to a computer suitable for extended audio review work.

title: Principal Product Manager - Goals and Projects
description:
Overview

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

With a sufficient timezone overlap with the team, we're able to hire eligible candidates for this role from any location in Australia.

About the team

We're the Goals & Projects team. Goals is where an organization sets its objectives and tracks progress against them. Projects is where a team describes a piece of work and reports on how it's going, separate from the Jira space where the individual work items live. Together they connect what a team is working on to the organization's overarching goals.

Both apps are included with every Atlassian cloud plan, and some of their more advanced capabilities are part of Strategy Collection. They show up where teams already work, inside Atlassian Home, Jira, Confluence, Rovo, Focus or Talent, so a lot of what we ship we build with the teams who own those surfaces. Our customers range from the teams doing and tracking the work to the leaders and admins who need to see how it's progressing across a large organization. We're light on process and heavy on trust.

Responsibilities

About the role

As a Principal Product Manager on Goals & Projects, you'll own a major product area spanning both apps, from vision through launch and iteration. This is an individual contributor role.

Two areas are moving quickly right now. We're transforming both apps with AI, and we're using that to reach more of Atlassian's customer base than we have before.

You'll work on problems where the answer isn't obvious yet: how organizations set objectives and see honest progress against them, how a team's work becomes legible to the rest of the company without manual reporting, and where AI helps in that loop. You'll make principled trade-offs between staying consistent with the rest of Atlassian and moving quickly in Goals and Projects, and set the standard for product thinking on the team.

Responsibilities include:

  • Set the vision, strategy, roadmap, and measurable outcomes for a major product area spanning Goals and Projects, aligned with Atlassian's wider product and AI strategy.

  • Drive the AI roadmap for Goals and Projects, deciding where AI genuinely helps the people using these apps and setting the quality bar for what it produces.

  • Shape ambiguous opportunities with lightweight specs, prototypes, and clear written narratives.

  • Own the administration and governance capabilities that large, complex organizations need, including permissions, roles, and audit.

  • Run discovery directly with the teams, leaders, and admins who use these apps, and separate what they ask for from what they need.

  • Drive cross-functional execution across Engineering, Design, Research, and Analytics, and align senior stakeholders when priorities compete.

  • Work with the Atlassian product teams who own the surfaces these apps appear in, and settle the open questions with them directly.

  • Make the hard calls on defaults, rollout, and migration paths, grounded in data, customer evidence, and the effects on admins and end users.

  • Partner with go-to-market teams on launches, documentation, positioning, and measurement.

  • Know how the apps are performing across usage, adoption, retention, and satisfaction, investigate the changes, and use what you learn to steer the roadmap.

  • Influence product direction beyond your immediate team, and mentor other product managers.

Compensation

At Atlassian, we strive to design equitable, explainable, and competitive compensation programs. We follow consistent hiring practices and account for each candidate's skills, knowledge, and experience when setting base pay within the range.

This role may also be eligible for benefits, bonuses, commissions, and equity.

Qualifications

What we're looking for

  • 7+ years of product management experience, including ownership of a significant product area at scale.

  • A track record of delivering outcomes across multiple related products or teams.

  • Experience shipping AI-powered experiences to real customers, with a point of view on where AI helps.

  • Proven success shipping in ambiguity: you've taken a 0-to-1 or direction-changing initiative from strategy through launch and iteration.

  • The ability to clarify complex decisions and align senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority.

  • You use AI tools daily as a working method. You can prompt, iterate, and evaluate AI outputs to draft specs, analyze data, synthesize research, and build prototypes.

  • Technical fluency to work effectively with senior engineers on product and architectural trade-offs.

  • Strong customer discovery, synthesis, prioritization, and written communication skills.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and making pragmatic trade-offs without lowering the quality bar that large customers expect.

Nice to have

  • Product experience in work management, enterprise planning, or portfolio management.

  • Experience making a product succeed inside a larger platform, through cross-app integration or shared data models.

  • Experience with enterprise administration surfaces such as permissions models, admin controls, and audit.

Benefits & Perks

Atlassian offers a wide range of perks and benefits designed to support you, your family and to help you engage with your local community. Our offerings include health and wellbeing resources, paid volunteer days, and so much more. To learn more, visit go.atlassian.com/perksandbenefits.

About Atlassian

At Atlassian, we're motivated by a common goal: to unleash the potential of every team. Our software products help teams all over the planet and our solutions are designed for all types of work. Team collaboration through our tools makes what may be impossible alone, possible together.

We believe that the unique contributions of all Atlassians create our success. To ensure that our products and culture continue to incorporate everyone's perspectives and experience, we never discriminate based on race, religion, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, or marital, veteran, or disability status.
