This is a remote opportunity within a fast-paced Trust Services team focused on helping customers navigate security and compliance requirements.
You’ll take ownership of customer security questionnaires and due diligence requests, delivering accurate and timely responses.
The role combines technical security knowledge, GRC expertise, research, documentation, and cross-functional collaboration.
You’ll work with established security frameworks, compliance resources, control libraries, and customer-specific requirements.
The team operates with a strong focus on speed, precision, consistency, and reliable delivery, with typical customer deliverables completed within one to three business days.
You’ll collaborate closely with security and compliance professionals while helping customers use security and compliance capabilities to support business relationships.
This role is well suited to a detail-oriented security professional who can navigate ambiguity, manage high-volume workflows, and communicate clearly with global stakeholders.

title: Assistant Utility Site Superintendent
description:
About the Project:

The Eglinton Crosstown West Extension will bring the Eglinton Crosstown LRT another 9.2 kilometers farther west, creating a continuous rapid transit line from the east end of Toronto into Mississauga. The Stations, Rail, and Systems (SRS) package encompasses the design, construction, integration, and commissioning of key project components.

Position Overview

TRP has a current vacancy for an experienced Assistant Site Superintendent.


TRP is seeking an experienced Assistant Site Utility Superintendent to support the Utility Site Superintendent in the day-to-day field management and coordination of utility construction activities across the ECWE SRS project.

The Assistant Site Utility Superintendent will assist with planning, supervising, coordinating, and monitoring utility work activities, including utility relocations, protection, installation, excavation, tie-ins, testing, restoration, and associated civil works.


This position will work closely with the Utility Site Superintendent, Construction Managers, Project Managers, Utility Coordinators, Engineering, Design, Traffic & Transit, Environmental, Quality, Health & Safety, Survey, Project Controls, utility owners, subcontractors, and field crews.


The successful candidate will have hands-on experience in utility or civil construction and demonstrate the leadership, organization, and technical knowledge required to coordinate construction activities safely, efficiently, and in accordance with project requirements.


Key Responsibilities


Field Construction Supervision

  • The Assistant Site Superintendent supports the Site Superintendent in the day-to-day coordination and supervision of all on-site construction activities for wet utilities, drainage, and earthworks. This role assists in leading foreman coordination meetings, safety briefings, and FLHA reviews, and helps monitor subcontractor performance, productivity, and adherence to scope, schedule, and quality requirements. The Assistant Site Superintendent contributes to the development and updating of three-week lookahead schedules, tracks daily progress and installed quantities, and helps identify and escalate issues that may impact workflow or milestones. Working under the direction of the Site Superintendent, this position maintains a strong on-site presence, supports implementation of safety and quality systems—including compliance with method statements and Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs)—and assists in maintaining accurate daily records, reports, and documentation to support project controls and change management.


Utility Construction

Support construction activities involving:

  • Watermains
  • Sanitary sewers
  • Storm sewers
  • Stormwater infrastructure
  • Telecommunications
  • Fibre-optic infrastructure
  • Gas utilities
  • Traffic signal infrastructure
  • Utility duct banks
  • Utility chambers and vaults
  • Temporary utilities
  • Utility protection and support
  • Utility relocations and abandonments
  • Service connections and tie-ins

Ensure work is coordinated with existing utilities, proposed infrastructure, and adjacent construction activities.


Utility Relocation & Protection

  • Assist with utility relocation and protection activities.
  • Coordinate utility locates, potholing, daylighting, test pits, and investigative work.
  • Verify existing utility locations and conditions in the field.
  • Assist with coordination of temporary utility support and protection measures.
  • Monitor work around live and existing utilities.
  • Assist with utility shutdowns, isolations, cutovers, and tie-ins.
  • Coordinate with utility owners and field representatives as directed.
  • Identify discrepancies between utility records, drawings, and actual field conditions.
  • Immediately report unexpected or potentially hazardous utility conditions.
  • Assist Engineering and Design teams with resolving field utility conflicts.


Excavation & Trenching

  • Assist with supervision of excavation and trenching activities.
  • Ensure utility excavation follows approved construction methods and safety requirements.
  • Monitor trench conditions, access, egress, shoring, protection systems, and dewatering.
  • Coordinate utility bedding, installation, backfill, compaction, and restoration.
  • Ensure existing utilities and adjacent structures are protected during excavation.
  • Coordinate survey and inspection activities prior to backfilling.
  • Ensure crews follow approved excavation and utility installation procedures.
  • Escalate unsafe excavation or trench conditions immediately.


Construction Coordination

  • Coordinate utility work with station excavation, foundations, structures, roadworks, drainage, traffic management, and other civil activities.
  • Coordinate utility activities with other TRP construction teams and subcontractors.
  • Participate in daily coordination and weekly planning meetings.
  • Review upcoming activities to identify utility conflicts and access requirements.
  • Coordinate work sequencing to minimize disruption to other construction activities.
  • Assist in identifying constraints, access issues, material requirements, and resource needs.
  • Support coordination of utility activities across multiple work fronts where required.


Utility Owner Coordination

  • Support coordination with utility owners, municipalities, agencies, consultants, and other external stakeholders.
  • Assist with arranging utility-owner inspections and site meetings.
  • Ensure utility-owner requirements are communicated to field crews.
  • Assist with coordinating inspections, testing, shutdowns, tie-ins, and acceptance activities.
  • Track outstanding utility-owner comments and field requirements.
  • Escalate unresolved issues to the Utility Site Superintendent.
  • Maintain professional relationships with utility representatives and project stakeholders.


Subcontractor & Crew Coordination

  • Assist the Utility Site Superintendent in managing utility subcontractors and crews.
  • Monitor subcontractor productivity, workmanship, staffing, equipment, and compliance with project requirements.
  • Confirm that subcontractors are working from approved drawings and procedures.
  • Assist with daily allocation of work areas and resources.
  • Monitor subcontractor progress against planned activities.
  • Identify productivity or performance concerns and escalate them appropriately.
  • Support coordination of subcontractor access, materials, inspections, and testing.
  • Assist with confirming completed quantities and work activities.


Construction Planning & Scheduling

  • Participate in daily, weekly, and short-term utility planning.
  • Assist with development of look-ahead plans for utility work.
  • Monitor planned versus actual progress.
  • Identify potential schedule delays and constraints.
  • Provide field information to the Utility Site Superintendent and Project Controls team.
  • Assist with recovery planning when activities fall behind schedule.
  • Coordinate manpower, equipment, materials, and subcontractor requirements.
  • Help ensure utility activities are sequenced appropriately with the overall construction schedule.


Quality Control

  • Monitor utility construction to ensure compliance with approved drawings, specifications, standards, and quality requirements.
  • Coordinate required inspections and testing.
  • Assist with implementation of Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs).
  • Verify installation dimensions, elevations, alignments, materials, and workmanship.
  • Coordinate pressure testing, CCTV inspections, compaction testing, mandrel testing, electrical testing, and other applicable testing.
  • Identify deficiencies and ensure corrective action is initiated.
  • Assist with tracking non-conformances and deficiencies.
  • Coordinate utility-owner inspections and acceptance.
  • Ensure quality records and as-built information are captured accurately.


Health & Safety

  • Promote a strong safety culture within assigned utility work areas.
  • Ensure field activities comply with TRP's Health & Safety Plan and applicable Ontario legislation.
  • Participate in daily pre-task planning, toolbox talks, and safety meetings.
  • Monitor safe work practices and identify potential hazards.
  • Pay particular attention to hazards associated with:
    • Excavation and trenching
    • Existing/live utilities
    • Heavy equipment
    • Traffic
    • Lifting operations
    • Confined spaces
    • Underground structures
    • Utility shutdowns and tie-ins
  • Immediately address unsafe conditions and escalate significant hazards.
  • Support incident investigations and corrective actions when required.
  • Ensure subcontractors and crews comply with site-specific safety requirements.


Traffic & Public Interface

  • Assist with coordinating utility construction within active roadways and public areas.
  • Work with Traffic & Transit teams to ensure activities follow approved traffic management plans.
  • Coordinate work around lane closures, pedestrian routes, cycling facilities, transit stops, and property access.
  • Ensure utility work areas are appropriately barricaded, signed, and protected.
  • Assist with coordination of temporary access and traffic arrangements.
  • Escalate potential impacts to residents, businesses, transit users, or other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate with the Stakeholder Engagement team when utility activities require advance notification or stakeholder communication.


Field Documentation & Reporting

  • Prepare and maintain daily utility construction records.
  • Record manpower, equipment, activities, quantities, progress, delays, inspections, testing, and site conditions.
  • Maintain photographic records of utility installations and construction progress.
  • Track completed work and quantities.
  • Record unforeseen conditions and utility conflicts.
  • Assist with RFIs, technical queries, field change documentation, and deficiency reports.
  • Maintain records of utility-owner inspections and approvals.
  • Ensure as-built information is captured before utilities are covered.

title: SOFTWARE QUALITY ANALYST
description:

title: Commercial Implementation Intern (Summer 2027)
description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Commercial Implementation Team

The Commercial Implementation team plays a critical role in ensuring the successful launch and ongoing success of Zipline’s commercial operations. The team defines commercial workflows and compliance processes, tests and validates new features and procedures at test sites and partner sites, creates training materials and onboarding playbooks, and identifies and addresses operational gaps to deliver a smooth and successful P2 experience for all commercial operations. The Commercial Implementation team is deeply knowledgeable in every step of the process from order placed to successful delivery, and works with internal and external partners to optimize the experience for operators and customers.

We build the processes against which our teams and our Partners’ teams will execute operating the Zipline Network.

Commercial Implementation team members work across all Zipline partner verticals and test sites. Site launch, training, and ownership will be determined by a combination of partner type and location.

The Role

As Project Manager on the Commercial Implementation team you will focus on designing, optimizing, and maintaining the workflows that enable seamless partner onboarding, integration, and ongoing operations. Your primary role will be to ensure efficiency, scalability, and compliance while aligning with the team’s mission of delivering exceptional partner experiences.

What You'll Do

  • Design, develop, and implement internal business processes - examples include document change management system and system for collecting subjective customer feedback
  • Map out existing processes to understand their flow and identify inefficiencies
  • Identify process bottlenecks and inefficiencies, and recommend solutions for continuous improvement
  • Collaborate with the Product, Enterprise Systems, Customer Success, and engineering to implement workflows
  • Monitor process performance, track key metrics, and report on process outcomes
  • Document and maintain up-to-date process workflows, guidelines, and SOPs

What You'll Bring

  • Experience in project management, operations, or related roles, preferably in a fast-paced or complex environment
  • Proven track record of working with product, engineering, and customer success teams to align processes with business goals
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills to drive collaboration and alignment
  • Practical experience in analyzing, mapping, and reengineering workflows
  • Ability to gather, analyze, and interpret data to inform process improvements and measure success
  • Strong organizational skills to manage multiple initiatives and ensure process documentation is comprehensive and accessible
  • Reliable vehicle access to travel to our test sites
  • Willingness to travel 1-2 times to out of state commercial sites

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September). Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

The hourly rate for this internship is $34 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

title: Sr Director Conference & Events
description:
Overview

Join our Team as Senior Director Conferences and Events!

Imagine a place where who you are, where you're from, or the circumstances that surround you don't determine your access to experiences or opportunities. Now imagine a mission, created to enable all young people, especially those who need us most, to reach their full potential as productive, caring, responsible citizens. That's what we do.

At Boys & Girls Clubs of America (BGCA), we're committed to doing whatever it takes to build great futures for America's youth, and our conferences and events play an important role in bringing our Movement together to learn, connect, collaborate, and lead. We are seeking a Senior Director, Conferences & Events to provide strategic leadership for a diverse portfolio of national, regional, and role-based convenings serving thousands of attendees annually.

This is an opportunity for an experienced events leader to do more than execute exceptional events. We are looking for a thought partner and industry expert who can help shape how BGCA convenes its Movement, bringing fresh ideas, strong business acumen, operational discipline, and deep expertise in large-scale event strategy and production.

This role is hybrid, with an in-office presence Tuesday and Wednesday, and requires up to 40% travel.

About the Team

The Conferences, Learning & Events team oversees a diverse portfolio of national, regional, and role-based convenings that serve thousands of attendees annually. As a strategic partner to organizational leaders, the team transforms business priorities into exceptional learning and engagement experiences while driving innovation, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across the event ecosystem.

As Senior Director, you will lead a team of three event managers while partnering extensively across BGCA with senior leaders, event owners, Finance, Legal, Learning & Development, Youth Development, Organizational Development, external vendors, hotels, convention centers, and other partners.

Responsibilities

What You'll Do

Set the strategy. You'll serve as the strategic lead for BGCA's national, regional, and role-based conferences and learning events, developing an integrated event roadmap that aligns our convenings with organizational priorities, learning objectives, attendee needs, and business outcomes.

Be a trusted advisor, not simply an executor. You'll partner with senior leaders and event owners to turn their vision into successful experiences while bringing your own expertise to the table. You'll anticipate downstream implications, challenge assumptions when needed, recommend solutions, and help leaders make informed decisions about attendance, venues, programming, budgets, sponsorship opportunities, and the overall attendee experience.

Lead complex, large-scale events. You'll provide strategic oversight for events that can exceed 3,000 attendees and involve multiple hotels, convention facilities, vendors, business partners, internal teams, and competing priorities. You'll ensure planning is coordinated across the entire portfolio rather than approaching each event in isolation.

Build stronger systems and capabilities. You'll assess our current people, processes, tools, and event infrastructure and establish scalable practices that allow the team to work more efficiently and consistently. That includes standardized planning tools, governance, timelines, technology, vendor practices, and enterprise-wide event standards.

Strengthen our in-house expertise. You'll identify capability gaps across the team and build the expertise needed to manage increasingly complex events. That includes areas such as housing management, venue sourcing, hotel blocks, food and beverage, AV and production, registration, attendee communications, and other critical components of large-scale conference operations.

Own the business of events. You'll oversee multimillion-dollar event budgets, forecasting, vendor negotiations, contracting, cost management, and ROI measurement. You'll also understand how event design, exhibitor experiences, sponsorships, and partnerships can support revenue goals—even though fundraising itself is not the primary responsibility of this role.

Elevate the attendee experience. You'll continually look for ways to make BGCA's events more engaging, accessible, innovative, and impactful—from registration and pre-event communications through the on-site experience and post-event engagement.

Develop a high-performing team. You'll coach and develop three event managers, establish clear expectations and accountability, build new capabilities, manage workload and priorities, and create an environment where the team can grow from strong execution to strategic event partnership.

The Competencies That Will Make You Successful

  • Strategic Leadership: Sees beyond individual events to build an integrated strategy that connects organizational priorities, attendee needs, learning, operations, and impact.
  • Executive Partnership & Influence: Operates as a trusted advisor who can listen to a business need, bring expertise and perspective, identify implications, and influence decisions without simply taking an order.
  • Operational Excellence: Brings structure to complexity and builds scalable processes, systems, standards, and tools that enable consistent execution across a large event portfolio.
  • Financial & Business Acumen: Understands the economics of large-scale events and makes sound decisions around budgets, contracts, vendors, sponsorship opportunities, resources, risk, and ROI.
  • Innovation & Continuous Improvement: Stays connected to the events and hospitality industry and actively introduces new ideas, technologies, experiences, and practices that elevate the work.
  • People Leadership & Development: Builds a high-performing team through clear expectations, coaching, accountability, capability building, and meaningful opportunities for growth.

What Success Looks Like

Your early focus will be on understanding the current event ecosystem and determining where BGCA can strengthen its approach. Within your first 90 days, you'll assess the Conferences & Events function through a people, process, systems, and tools lens and establish a clear, prioritized roadmap for improvement.

From there, you'll begin translating that roadmap into action, strengthening team capabilities, building repeatable processes and resources, advancing BGCA's evolving enterprise event strategy, and successfully delivering major conferences and convenings against established participation, financial, experience, and learning outcomes.

Longer term, success means BGCA has a more strategic, scalable, data-informed events function that consistently delivers exceptional experiences, strengthens organizational alignment, manages resources responsibly, and continuously raises the bar for how we convene our Movement.

Qualifications

What You’ll Bring

We're looking for a seasoned events leader with the depth of experience and leadership presence to immediately add value in a complex environment. The strongest candidates will bring:

  • 10+ years of progressive experience leading large-scale conferences, conventions, meetings, hospitality operations, or enterprise events, with experience managing events comparable in complexity to 3,000+ attendee, convention-center-level experiences.
  • Significant experience leading and developing event professionals or teams, including the ability to assess capability gaps and build expertise.
  • Deep knowledge of large-scale event operations, including venue and site selection, multi-property hotel blocks and housing, food and beverage, AV/production, registration, attendee experience, vendor management, and event technology.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multimillion-dollar budgets, forecasting expenses, negotiating complex vendor agreements, and identifying opportunities for cost efficiencies.
  • Strong executive presence and the ability to serve as a credible advisor to senior leaders, bringing recommendations, identifying implications, navigating competing priorities, and constructively influencing decisions.
  • Strong project and portfolio management capabilities with experience coordinating multiple events and complex cross-functional workstreams simultaneously.
  • An understanding of sponsorship, exhibitor, partnership, and other event revenue models and how event design can help maximize partner value and revenue opportunities.
  • A track record of bringing new ideas, technologies, industry trends, and best practices into an organization rather than simply executing established approaches.
  • Experience with event management platforms such as Cvent, CrowdCompass, EventMobi, or comparable technology.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. CMP or comparable industry credentials are strongly valued.

Experience may come from a large hotel or hospitality organization, convention center, association, corporate events environment, nonprofit, or another organization producing events of comparable scale and complexity. What matters most is the depth of your large-scale event expertise and your ability to translate that expertise into stronger strategy, systems, experiences, and results.

Work Environment & Travel

This is a hybrid role with an in-office presence on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Because our work comes to life at conferences and events across the country, this position requires up to 40% travel and the flexibility to work early mornings, evenings, weekends, and extended days during major events.

Compensation

The salary range for this role is $120,000.00 to $135,000.00 BGCA takes into consideration a combination of a candidate’s education, training and experience, as well as the position’s scope and complexity, the discretion and latitude required for the role and other external and internal data when establishing a salary level. We are highly invested in every employee’s total well-being and offer a substantial and comprehensive total rewards package.

title: Agentic AI Developer IV
description:
Overview

RealPage is accelerating the adoption of Generative AI and agentic engineering practices across its technology organization. The Internal AI Center of Excellence is responsible for enabling engineering teams to apply AI effectively, safely, and consistently across the software development lifecycle.

We are seeking an AI Developer IV to help design, build, and scale internal AI solutions that improve engineering productivity, accelerate delivery, and support RealPage’s AI adoption goals. This role will focus on developing reusable AI patterns, agentic workflows, internal developer tools, reference implementations, and enablement assets that help engineering teams move from experimentation to repeatable production use.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on AI engineer with strong software development experience, practical knowledge of LLMs and agentic systems, and the ability to partner with engineering teams to turn AI concepts into usable internal capabilities.

Responsibilities

Internal AI Solution Development

  • Design and build internal AI solutions that support engineering productivity and software delivery, including:
    • AI-powered developer workflows and assistants
    • Agentic SDLC automation patterns
    • Internal tools for code analysis, documentation, testing, migration, and engineering support
    • Reusable prompt, tool-calling, and workflow patterns
    • Reference implementations that can be adopted by engineering teams
  • Develop solutions that are practical, scalable, maintainable, and aligned with RealPage engineering standards.

Agentic Workflow and Platform Enablement

  • Build reusable capabilities that help teams adopt AI consistently across the organization, including:
    • Multi-step agentic workflows
    • Tool-calling and orchestration patterns
    • RAG-based internal knowledge solutions
    • Shared SDKs, templates, and integration examples
    • Reusable components for copilots, agents, and AI-enabled engineering workflows
  • Partner with senior architects and engineering leaders to establish patterns that can scale beyond one team or use case.

Engineering Team Enablement

  • Work directly with engineering teams, champions, and internal stakeholders to help them adopt AI effectively.

Responsibilities include:

    • Pairing with teams on AI use cases and implementation patterns
    • Providing technical guidance on LLM, RAG, and agentic workflow design
    • Supporting proof-of-concept efforts and helping mature them into repeatable practices
    • Creating playbooks, examples, templates, and documentation for internal engineering use
    • Participating in office hours, workshops, and AI enablement sessions

AI Evaluation, Quality, and Responsible Use

  • Help define and apply practical evaluation and governance practices for internal AI solutions, including:
    • Prompt and workflow evaluation
    • Accuracy, relevance, and usefulness testing
    • Safety and responsible AI considerations
    • PII and sensitive-data handling
    • Logging, observability, and feedback loops
    • Human-in-the-loop review patterns where appropriate
  • Ensure internal AI solutions are developed with quality, security, privacy, and reliability in mind.

Delivery and Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with engineering leadership, product teams, architecture, security, and other stakeholders to identify and deliver high-impact AI use cases.

Responsibilities include:

    • Translating engineering productivity needs into AI-enabled solutions
    • Supporting roadmap-aligned internal AI initiatives
    • Contributing to adoption and capacity-improvement goals
    • Helping measure the impact of AI enablement efforts
    • Communicating technical concepts clearly to engineering and non-engineering audiences

Performance, Reliability, and Cost Awareness

  • Design AI solutions with practical performance and cost considerations, including:
    • Model selection and routing
    • Prompt and context optimization
    • Caching and retrieval efficiency
    • Latency and reliability considerations
    • Build-vs-buy recommendations
    • Avoidance of vendor lock-in where practical

Qualifications

  • Typically 6+ years of software engineering experience, with meaningful hands-on experience building production applications or internal platforms.
  • 2+ years of applied AI, LLM, Generative AI, or agentic workflow experience.
  • Strong programming experience in Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, or similar production languages.
  • Experience designing and building cloud-native applications or services in Azure, GCP, or AWS.
  • Practical experience with:

LLM-based application development

Prompt engineering and prompt versioning

Tool calling / function calling

RAG architectures

Vector databases or semantic retrieval

Multi-step workflow or agent orchestration

  • Familiarity with modern software engineering practices, including:
  • CI/CD
  • Git-based development
  • Automated testing
  • API design
  • Observability and logging
  • Experience using or enabling AI coding tools such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, or similar tools.
  • Ability to work directly with engineering teams to understand needs, prototype solutions, and drive adoption.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain AI concepts and implementation patterns clearly.

Nice-to-Have Skills / Abilities

  • Experience building internal developer platforms, engineering productivity tools, or enablement frameworks.
  • Experience with agent frameworks or orchestration tools such as LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, Semantic Kernel, CrewAI, or similar frameworks.

title: Canvas Lead
description:
Canvass Lead

About MF Professional Services, Inc.

MF Professional Services, Inc. (MFPS) provides human resources, payroll, benefits administration, and operational support to mission-driven organizations. This position may perform services on behalf of MFPS clients, including Mi Familia Vota and Mi Familia en Acción.

Position Summary

The Canvass Lead coordinates daily voter outreach and canvassing activities designed to increase civic participation, voter registration, voter education, and community engagement.

This position provides daily direction, training, coaching, and field support to an assigned team of canvassers. Responsibilities include conducting team launches, assigning turf, distributing materials, monitoring field activity, reviewing data, maintaining compliance, and submitting required reports.

The Canvass Lead also participates directly in door-to-door canvassing, voter-registration activities, and other approved community outreach. This position requires substantial fieldwork, frequent walking, flexible scheduling, accurate recordkeeping, and strict compliance with voter-registration, safety, and data-security procedures.

This is a temporary position. The duration of the assignment will depend on campaign timelines, available funding, and organizational needs. Temporary employment does not guarantee continued employment or an extension of the assignment.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Lead the daily activities of an assigned canvassing team.

  • Conduct pre-shift briefings covering goals, schedules, turf assignments, scripts, safety requirements, and campaign updates.

  • Prepare and assign canvassing turf using VAN, MiniVAN, maps, spreadsheets, or other approved tools.

  • Distribute voter-registration forms, literature, mobile devices, identification, and other field materials.

  • Ensure canvassers understand their assignments, geographic boundaries, check-in requirements, and daily goals.

  • Coordinate team deployment, breaks, transportation, return times, and end-of-shift procedures.

  • Monitor field activity and maintain regular communication with canvassers.

  • Provide field demonstrations, coaching, feedback, and retraining as needed.

  • Conduct door-to-door canvassing, voter registration, voter education, and other approved outreach.

  • Engage community members respectfully using approved scripts, talking points, and materials.

  • Review voter-contact results, voter-registration forms, and field reports for accuracy and completeness.

  • Track doors knocked, successful contacts, voter registrations, turf completion, and other assigned performance measures.

  • Enter or upload results into VAN, MiniVAN, spreadsheets, databases, or other approved systems.

  • Submit timely daily and weekly reports to the designated supervisor.

  • Maintain custody and tracking records for voter-registration forms and sensitive voter information.

  • Ensure completed, incomplete, spoiled, and unused voter-registration forms are secured and returned according to established procedures.

  • Immediately report suspected falsification, misconduct, data manipulation, form mishandling, or other compliance concerns.

  • Monitor weather, neighborhood conditions, missed check-ins, and other potential field-safety risks.

  • Report injuries, threats, accidents, law-enforcement interactions, and other significant incidents promptly.

  • Communicate attendance, performance, conduct, safety, staffing, or operational concerns to management.

  • Foster a professional, respectful, inclusive, and accountable team environment.

  • Accurately record all time worked and follow organizational timekeeping procedures.

  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Previous canvassing, voter-registration, campaign, community outreach, field-organizing, or civic-engagement experience required.

  • Previous experience leading, training, coaching, or supporting a canvassing or outreach team preferred.

  • Strong leadership, communication, coaching, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to establish clear expectations, monitor performance, and provide constructive feedback.

  • Ability to manage field schedules, materials, transportation, turf assignments, check-ins, and reporting deadlines.

  • Experience using VAN, MiniVAN, mobile canvassing applications, spreadsheets, or comparable technology preferred.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to review voter-registration forms and field data accurately.

  • Dependable, punctual, organized, and comfortable working directly with employees and community members.

  • Ability to follow voter-registration, data-security, quality-control, safety, and reporting procedures.

  • Ability to remain professional and composed during difficult or unexpected interactions.

  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and protect sensitive voter, employee, community, and organizational information.

  • Experience working with Latino or other diverse communities preferred.

  • Professional proficiency in English and Spanish preferred.

  • Ability to work flexible schedules, including mornings, evenings, weekends, and extended campaign-style hours.

  • Ability to travel throughout the assigned service area.

  • Must satisfy any voter-registration eligibility, training, or certification requirements applicable in the assigned jurisdiction.

  • If driving is required, the employee must maintain a valid driver’s license, legally required automobile insurance, an acceptable driving record, and access to a safe and reliable vehicle unless an organizational vehicle is provided.

Physical and Work Requirements

This is a field-based position requiring extended periods of walking and standing outdoors. The Canvass Lead must be able to canvass and support employees in residential neighborhoods, community locations, public spaces, and events while navigating sidewalks, stairs, uneven surfaces, and varying terrain.

The position requires the ability to carry outreach materials weighing up to 25 pounds and regularly use a computer, mobile device, clipboard, voter-registration forms, and other field equipment.

Work may occur in heat, cold, rain, wind, direct sunlight, traffic, noise, crowds, and other changing field conditions. Reasonable accommodations will be considered for qualified individuals with disabilities.

title: Fire Alarm Technician
description:
Job Purpose

The Fire Alarm Technician is responsible for the inspection, testing, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of fire alarm and detection systems at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH) and designated outlying military installations throughout Hawaii. The position supports the continued safe and reliable operation of fire alarm, detection, mass notification, and emergency communication systems.


Work will be performed in accordance with applicable requirements, including NFPA 72, NFPA 101, UFC 3-600-01, Department of Defense/Navy installation directives, local Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) requirements, and other applicable federal and local codes and standards. The Fire Alarm Technician serves as a subject matter expert for conventional, addressable, and mass notification fire alarm systems.

The position reports to the Project Manager/Site Supervisor and works closely with the installation Fire Department, Facilities Engineering, and Government Quality Assurance Representative (QAR).

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Inspect, test, and maintain fire alarm control panels (FACP), initiating devices, notification appliances, and auxiliary control functions in accordance with NFPA 72 and applicable UFC standards.
  • Perform annual, semi-annual, and quarterly inspections of fire alarm systems as required by the Performance Work Statement (PWS).
  • Troubleshoot and repair fire alarm system malfunctions, including panel faults, open circuits, ground faults, device failures, and communication errors.
  • Replace or recalibrate smoke detectors, heat detectors, manual pull stations, horn/strobes, duct detectors, and other applicable devices as needed.
  • Test and verify the proper operation of mass notification systems (MNS), emergency voice/alarm communication systems (EVACS), and interfaces with building automation and suppression systems.
  • Maintain and update as-built drawings, device schedules, and panel programming documentation.
  • Ensure work complies with NFPA 72, NFPA 101, UFC 3-600-01, DoD/Navy installation directives, and applicable local AHJ requirements.
  • Document inspections, test results, deficiencies, and corrective actions in the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) and/or other government-required reporting formats.
  • Participate in quality control inspections, government QAR reviews, and safety inspections.
  • Maintain a clean and safe work environment and comply with applicable OSHA, installation safety, and environmental requirements.
  • Maintain required certifications and participate in continuing education and training as required.
  • Complete scheduled inspections within the timeframes established by the PWS and NFPA 72.
  • Complete and submit inspection reports within required contract timeframes.
  • Respond to emergency service calls within the response times established by the PWS.
  • Prepare deficiency reports and provide corrective-action recommendations within required timeframes.
  • Perform work in accordance with applicable NFPA, UFC, and AHJ standards and support satisfactory government QAR inspections.


Required Skills and Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Associate's degree or technical/vocational training in electronics, electrical, or fire protection systems preferred.
  • Minimum of 3–5 years of experience inspecting, testing, and maintaining fire alarm systems in commercial, industrial, or government/military facilities.
  • NICET Fire Alarm Systems Level II certification required; Level III preferred.
  • Familiarity with military/DoD facility standards and UFC 3-600-01 strongly preferred.
  • Valid driver's license required, with the ability to operate government or company vehicles on the installation.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a DoD/Navy Base Access credential, including required background screening.
  • U.S. Citizenship required for base access.
  • OSHA 10-Hour Construction Safety certification preferred

Physical Requirements



  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to work at heights using ladders, scaffolding, and aerial lifts.
  • Ability to work in confined spaces, attics, mechanical rooms, and crawl spaces.
  • Ability to work outdoors in Hawaii's tropical climate conditions.
  • Color vision sufficient to read wiring diagrams and identify color-coded conductors.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, and kneel for extended periods.

Work Schedule and Location

The standard work schedule is Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 3:30 PM, or as otherwise directed by the contract. On-call or emergency-response availability may be required, including participation in a rotating on-call schedule.

Work locations include Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam and designated outlying areas, including Ford Island, Lualualei, West Loch, Barbers Point, Kunia, and other designated sites.

description:
Overview

Make your mark at WD-40 CompanyWe’re in the middle of one of the most ambitious ERP transformations in our company’s history — and we’re looking for a collaborative and analytically sharp Solutions Architect who thrives on complex, high-stakes challenges. This is not a maintenance role. You’ll be the highest-level technical authority on our D365 F&O platform, owning architecture decisions that directly shape WD-40’s global digital backbone.

As a Solutions Architect focused on Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (F&O), you will be the thought leader responsible for defining, optimizing, and governing our ERP architecture across a globally distributed team spanning the US, UK, India, and beyond. With the Americas implementation nearly complete and a full EMEA rollout launching in early 2027, you’ll be stepping into a role with real momentum — and real problems left to solve. You’ll partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders, implementation specialists, and external ISVs to deliver integrated, scalable, and forward-thinking solutions that power WD-40’s next phase of global growth.

If you’re a seasoned technical architect who loves owning hard problems, collaborating across cultures and time zones, and building solutions that scale globally — and you’re ready to do that inside a company that actually respects your time — we’d love to hear from you.

This is a remote role with an opportunity to work from anywhere in the US. Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. and should not require visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Responsibilities

  • Shape the future of WD-40’s ERP ecosystem, designing scalable and secure architecture across a complex, multi-region environment as we expand from the Americas and Australia into EMEA and beyond.
  • Serve as the bridge between business vision and technical execution, aligning D365 platform capabilities with organizational goals.
  • Lead end-to-end architectural planning, including data flow, integrations (Salesforce, Atlas, SnapLogic, etc.), system connectivity, and the strategic balance between standardized global templates and country-specific requirements.
  • Collaborate actively with implementation specialists, business process leads, developers, and global business stakeholders to translate requirements into sound architectural decisions — asking the right questions, surfacing trade-offs, and driving alignment across technical and non-technical teams.
  • Guide integration of third-party ISVs, ensuring seamless alignment with enterprise architecture.
  • Provide technical leadership during implementation, including code reviews, design standards, and governance.
  • Stay ahead of industry trends, evaluating new features and managing platform upgrades.
  • Serve as the highest-level escalation point for complex technical issues, with occasional on-site travel to global locations (approximately 4 weeks per year) to support go-lives, resolve critical issues, and collaborate with regional teams across different cultures and time zones.
  • Champion best practices in system performance, security, and compliance.

Qualifications

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in ERP architecture, design, development, and optimization.
  • 5+ years of hands-on architecture experience specifically with Microsoft Dynamics 365 F&O (both Finance and Operations), including full F&O functional coverage — procurement, sales, finance, and manufacturing — as well as ISV integrations and enterprise-scale, multi-country implementations.
  • Solid understanding of multi-system data flows in complex, global environments.
  • Proven success translating business requirements into technical strategies.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field.
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 certifications
  • Enterprise Architecture certifications (preferred).
  • Exceptional collaboration and communication skills — equally comfortable working with developers, business process leads, and executive stakeholders across multiple countries and cultures. This role requires someone who proactively engages, asks the right questions, and drives clarity across a globally distributed team.
  • An analytically sharp, intellectually engaged problem-solver who digs into complexity, evaluates trade-offs rigorously, and is energized by the challenge of scaling a global ERP environment — not someone looking to coast.
  • Demonstrated ability to work across cultural boundaries — experience with global ERP rollouts involving teams or end users in multiple countries or regions is strongly preferred.

About Us

Our “Why”

At WD-40 Company, we believe that purpose-driven, passionate people guided by our values create amazing outcomes. Our "why" is refreshingly simple - we exist to create positive lasting memories in everything we do.

Why You Should Apply

  • Learning-based culture that supports the growth and development of all tribe members
  • Strong values aligned culture whose #1 strategic driver is to build a business for the future that we will be proud to hand down to the next generation
  • Over 93.3% employee engagement as of January 2023 global employee survey
  • A culture where 93% of the tribe report experience a sense of belonging
  • Voted Most Democratic Workplace and certified WorldBlu Freedom Centered Workplace

Do You Align With Our Values?

Please, only consider employment with WD-40 Company if you feel as strongly about our values as we do: We live, breathe, and play by our values every day.

Thank you for considering WD-40 Company in your career search! #PositiveLastingMemories

At WD-40 Company we foster a culture of inclusion where all individuals are recognized, valued, respected, and experience a sense of belonging. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to individual characteristics that make us unique such as our backgrounds, experiences, qualities, talents, traits, beliefs, and preferences. #LI-MH1

We've Got You Covered

Our competitive and comprehensive benefits package provides you protection, security, and peace of mind. We offer life-enhancing health, wellness, and financial programs, including profit sharing, annual cash incentive rewards, tuition reimbursement, and 401K match. In addition, we want you to recharge and take time off, so enjoy short-day Fridays, vacation time, paid holidays, and an additional paid week off between Christmas and the new year to spend with family and friends!

title: Geotechnical Field Technician
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Geotechnical Field Technician based in Canada.

This role offers the opportunity to contribute to a diverse portfolio of environmental, infrastructure, transportation, renewable energy, materials, and building projects.
You will support geotechnical investigations, field testing, monitoring, and inspections under the guidance of experienced geotechnical professionals.
Working primarily in the field, you will gather subsurface information and document site conditions across a variety of project environments.
Your work will contribute directly to reliable engineering assessments and the successful delivery of major infrastructure and development projects.
The position provides hands-on exposure to drilling, sampling, groundwater monitoring, materials testing, and construction inspection.
You will collaborate with engineers, contractors, laboratories, and other project stakeholders while maintaining high safety and quality standards.
It also offers a strong foundation for developing a long-term career in geotechnical engineering, materials testing, construction inspection, or infrastructure consulting.

Accountabilities:

  • Support geotechnical subsurface investigations, including borehole drilling, test pits, soil sampling, and groundwater monitoring.
  • Coordinate drilling activities and utility clearance requirements.
  • Log soil and rock samples under the direction of geotechnical engineers.
  • Monitor field investigations and accurately document site conditions.
  • Install and monitor groundwater observation wells and piezometers.
  • Collect soil, rock, aggregate, asphalt, and groundwater samples for laboratory analysis.
  • Prepare factual reports, summaries, data sheets, and graphs to support supervisors in interpreting test results.
  • Complete field, laboratory, and office activities in accordance with established work plans and safe work practices.
  • Maintain accurate records related to health and safety, equipment calibration certificates, equipment manuals, and applicable standards.
  • Handle challenging situations professionally and diplomatically while maintaining positive relationships with internal and external contacts.
  • Travel out of town, including to remote areas, for extended periods when required to complete field assignments.
  • Consistently apply and promote workplace health and safety procedures.

    • Requirements

    • Technical diploma in Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, or a related field.
    • 3–5 years of experience in geotechnical work, materials testing, or construction inspection.
    • Previous experience with drilling programs, earthworks inspection, or laboratory testing is considered an asset.
    • Experience working on transportation, municipal, infrastructure, or similar projects is preferred.
    • Understanding of soil classification and fundamental geotechnical principles.
    • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and specifications.
    • Familiarity with field testing procedures and technical documentation requirements.
    • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
    • Strong commitment to occupational health and safety and the ability to consistently follow established procedures.
    • Comfortable working outdoors in varying weather conditions.
    • Physically able to lift and carry equipment weighing up to 25 kg.
    • Comfortable walking across uneven terrain and working around active construction sites.
    • Flexibility to work occasional overtime, early mornings, evenings, or weekends depending on project requirements.
    • Valid Ontario G Driver's License.
    • Strong communication, interpersonal, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work effectively with diverse project stakeholders.

      • Benefits

      • Full-time, regular employment opportunity.
      • Salary range of CAD $47,934–$62,913 per year, depending on skills, experience, qualifications, internal compensation structure, and applicable geographic considerations.
      • Comprehensive benefits package, which may include performance incentives or bonus eligibility depending on role level and business unit.
      • Cost-sharing group insurance.
      • Group RRSP.
      • Free telehealth service.
      • Confidential Employee Assistance Program for employees and their families.
      • Multiple opportunities for professional growth, mentoring, and skills development.
      • Exposure to projects across environmental, renewable energy, hydroelectric, transportation, materials, building, climate change, municipal, infrastructure, and development sectors.
      • Hands-on experience that can support career progression in geotechnical engineering, construction inspection, materials testing, and infrastructure consulting.
      • A collaborative work environment focused on innovation, professional development, and positive project impact.

title: Junior Graphic Designer
description:
Turn Crafting Into Connection


Junior Graphic Designer

At Stampin' Up!, we believe creativity has the power to connect people, strengthen relationships, and brighten lives. If you're excited about purposeful graphic design, love collaborating with others, and want to grow your skills alongside a team that genuinely enjoys working together, we'd love to meet you.

About Stampin' Up!

For more than 35 years, Stampin' Up! has inspired people around the world to express their creativity through crafting, handmade cards, scrapbooking, and meaningful moments of connection. We are a global company built on creativity, community, and caring deeply about people.

Our employees bring our mission to life every day by creating exceptional experiences for our demonstrators and customers around the world. We work hard, support one another, celebrate wins together, and believe great ideas can come from anyone.

If you're looking for a workplace where creativity is valued, collaboration matters, and people genuinely enjoy what they do, you'll fit right in.

What You'll Do

As a Junior Graphic Designer, you'll be part of a highly collaborative graphic design team responsible for bringing the Stampin' Up! brand to life across a variety of channels.

One day you might be creating social media graphics or digital promotions. The next, you could be preparing photography assets for our online store, organizing files, improving workflows, or supporting large scale marketing initiatives behind the scenes.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys both the creative and technical sides of design. Success comes from being able to balance artistic thinking with detailed execution, shift comfortably between priorities, and understand how great design contributes to broader business goals.

Our team values creativity, but we value strategic thinking just as much. We look for designers who intentionally use their creativity to solve problems, support marketing objectives, and create exceptional experiences for our customers.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who wants to be part of a positive team culture, actively collaborates with others, and understands that every project, whether highly visible or behind the scenes, contributes to something bigger.

What Success Looks Like

You might be a great fit if you:

  • Learn quickly and are genuinely excited to grow your skills
  • Ask thoughtful questions and aren't afraid to seek clarification
  • Have a strong work ethic and take ownership of your responsibilities
  • Can balance multiple projects and priorities without losing attention to detail
  • Enjoy both creative problem-solving and process-oriented work
  • Stay organized and adaptable when priorities shift
  • Value collaboration and building strong working relationships
  • Contribute positively to team culture and enjoy partnering with marketers, writers, photographers, and other creatives
  • Think strategically about how design supports business objectives

Key Responsibilities

  • Exemplify Stampin' Up!'s core values: We Care About People First, We Act with Courage, We Better Our Best, and We Own It!
  • Create high-quality graphic designs for our online store, promotions, social media, and other digital platforms
  • Understand and execute the Stampin' Up! brand through compelling visual storytelling
  • Prepare and export design deliverables for digital platforms
  • Support creative operations through organization, asset management, workflow improvements, and process efficiencies
  • Participate in team brainstorms, design critiques, and project reviews
  • Give and receive constructive feedback in a collaborative environment
  • Partner closely with marketing, writing, photography, and cross-functional teams
  • Stay current with industry trends, emerging technologies, and design best practices
  • Pursue ongoing professional and personal development

title: Affordable Housing Recertification Specialist, Bridgeport,  CT area
description:
Be a part of the best team in Property Management!


Vesta Management is seeking to hire an experienced, customer service focused, results driven Affordable Housing Recertification Specialist to support operations at our communities in the Bridgeport, CT area. This person will travel between several affordable housing communities in western, CT. If you have a proven track record with affordable housing programs such as LIHTC and Section 8, excellent attention to detail, and passion for customer service, we want to hear from you! TSC and/or COS certifications are strongly preferred.


What we Offer:

At Vesta, we take pride in hiring the best talent in Property Management. We work hard and we have fun doing so. In addition to our generous benefits package, we offer service awards, performance bonuses, team member appreciation events and opportunities for growth. Our benefits include:

  • Medical, dental & vision insurance
  • Company matched 401(K)
  • Paid time off- Vacation, sick, floating holidays
  • 12 additional paid holidays
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • PetPlan Pet Insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Long & Short-Term Disability Insurance
  • AND MORE



The Affordable Housing Recertification Specialist is responsible for managing the annual and interim income recertification process for residents in affordable housing programs (LIHTC, Section 8/HUD, HOME, and other subsidized housing programs). This role ensures continued compliance with federal, state, and local affordable housing regulations by accurately verifying resident eligibility, income, and household composition.

Essential Functions:

  • Process annual, interim, and initial certifications/recertifications in accordance with program guidelines (LIHTC, Section 8, HUD Multifamily, HOME, and/or other applicable programs)
  • Collect, verify, and calculate resident income, assets, and household composition using third-party verification methods
  • Prepare and distribute recertification notices to residents within required timeframes
  • Review and audit resident files for accuracy and completeness prior to submission
  • Calculate rent and utility allowance adjustments based on verified income
  • Maintain accurate resident files in compliance with program requirements and company recordkeeping standards
  • Enter and update resident data in property management/compliance software (e.g., Yardi)
  • Communicate with residents regarding required documentation, deadlines, and recertification outcomes
  • Coordinate with Property Managers and Compliance staff to resolve discrepancies or missing documentation
  • Track and manage recertification calendars/deadlines to ensure timely processing and avoid compliance lapses
  • Prepare files for internal audits, state housing agency monitoring visits, and HUD/REAC inspections
  • Stay current on changing regulations, income limits, and program requirements (HUD, LIHTC, state HFA guidelines)
  • Assist with move-in certifications and waitlist eligibility screening as needed

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Required:

  • Working knowledge of income/asset verification and calculation methods
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook)

Preferred:

  • Experience with LIHTC and/or HUD Section 8 program compliance
  • Experience with property management software (Yardi, RealPage, OneSite, or similar)
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish or other relevant language) a plus

Core Competencies:

  • Accuracy and attention to detail
  • Regulatory/compliance knowledge
  • Time management and deadline-driven workflow
  • Clear written and verbal communication
  • Discretion in handling confidential financial and personal information
  • Customer service orientation with residents

title: Assurance Officer
description:
• Fixed Term – 12 Month Contract
  • Based at 334 Lincoln Road

About us

Comcare is an established Mental Health and Housing provider assisting people with mental health or addiction issues to live well in the community. We provide a rich and diverse range of Mental Health Support Services, Housing and Housing Support Services.


The Performance, Risk & Assurance function plays a key role in supporting good governance, organisational resilience and service excellence. Working across the organisation, the team provides independent assurance, promotes continuous improvement, and helps ensure Comcare meets its regulatory, contractual and quality obligations.


About this role

We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented Assurance Officer to join our Performance, Risk & Assurance team based in Christchurch.


Reporting to the Director - Performance, Risk & Assurance, you will support the delivery of Comcare's assurance programme by undertaking internal audits, compliance reviews, quality improvement activities and assurance reporting. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with audit, quality, risk or compliance experience who is passionate about continuous improvement and strengthening organisational performance.


You will work closely with leaders and teams across the organisation to identify opportunities to improve systems, processes and controls, while helping ensure compliance with regulatory, accreditation and contractual requirements. Your work will directly contribute to maintaining high-quality services and supporting positive outcomes for our clients and communities.


What you’ll be doing

  • Support the planning and delivery of Comcare's risk-based assurance programme, including internal audits and compliance reviews.
  • Conduct audit planning, risk assessments, process reviews, and control evaluations to identify risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Analyse information and evidence to assess compliance, control effectiveness, and organisational performance.
  • Prepare clear audit reports, recommendations, and assurance documentation that support continuous improvement.
  • Monitor corrective actions and coordinate external audits, accreditation reviews, and regulatory assessments.
  • Build strong stakeholder relationships and contribute to the ongoing development of assurance frameworks, reporting, and quality improvement initiatives.


About you

You will bring a curious and analytical mindset, a strong eye for detail, and the confidence to engage effectively with people at all levels of the organisation.

To be successful in this role, you will have:

  • A relevant tertiary qualification and/or practical experience in audit, assurance, quality, risk, compliance or a related field.
  • 3 to 4 years' experience supporting or delivering internal audits, assurance reviews or compliance activities.
  • Professional certifications such as CIA, CA ANZ or CISA (or a willingness to work towards these) would be advantageous.
  • Knowledge of auditing principles, risk management, regulatory compliance requirements, and relevant industry standards.
  • Experience within the health, mental health, addiction, community housing or wider social services sector.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret data and identify practical improvement opportunities.
  • Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement, report writing, and organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, data analysis, and reporting tools, with an interest in leveraging technology.
  • A collaborative and culturally responsive approach, with a commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi, continuous learning, and professional development.


Eligibility

Applicants for this position must have the legal right to work in NZ and consent to undergo a criminal record check process.


What we offer

In return Comcare provides a supportive and positive culture that is committed to the ongoing development of its workforce in an area of growing need.

Modernization efforts enable continued involvement with worldwide operations by revitalizing legacy mission systems, replacing aging computer architectures, integrating multi‑sensor data fusion, and improving global expeditionary readiness and availability.   • Conduct comprehensive program portfolio reviews to evaluate and recommend alternative plans, enhance systems engineering processes, manage and sustain technical baselines, and design/perform system-level tests to ensure subsystem and system performance aligns with approved specifications.

  • Lead commodity management activities across the Gas Delivery portfolio, including supplier selection, qualification, development, and performance management.

  • Develop and execute negotiation strategies that deliver sustainable cost improvements while maintaining supplier competitiveness and operational excellence.

  • Monitor supplier performance through key metrics and drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on quality, delivery, cost, innovation, and ESG objectives.
  • Analyze supplier markets, capabilities, and industry trends to support strategic sourcing decisions and identify new opportunities.
  • Facilitate technology roadmap discussions between suppliers and ASM stakeholders to ensure future product and technology requirements are supported.
  • Proactively assess supply chain risks and implement mitigation strategies, including dual sourcing, supplier development, capacity planning, and business continuity initiatives.

What we are looking for

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • 10+ years of experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, or commodity management with progressively increasing responsibility.
  • 5+ years of experience within the semiconductor industry or a comparable high-technology manufacturing environment.
  • Strong ability to interpret technical drawings, specifications, and engineering documentation.
  • Proven experience managing supplier relationships, commercial negotiations, and supplier performance programs.
  • Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to influence decisions across functions and levels.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

What sets you apart

  • Experience sourcing Gas Delivery systems, gas panels, gas lines, valves, regulators, or related components.
  • Strong understanding of semiconductor manufacturing equipment and associated supply chains.
  • Experience working in a global, matrixed organization and influencing stakeholders across regions and functions.
  • Ability to build trusted supplier partnerships that balance innovation, performance, and risk mitigation.
  • Thrives in dynamic, high-mix, low-volume manufacturing environments.
  • Uses data-driven insights to identify opportunities and drive continuous improvement.
  • Demonstrates agility, resilience, and a collaborative approach to solving complex business challenges.

  • Ability to learn quickly.
  • Ability to work as part of a team.
  • Ability to read and comprehend instructions

  • Desire to treat each customer’s personal vehicle with great care and respect

  • The willingness to come to work on time and stay on task when on the clock

  • The ability to drive both automatic and manual shift vehicles

  • The availability to work Saturday or Sunday and holidays as deemed necessary to meet production needs
  • Commitment to report to work on time and stay on task during shift

Teph Seal is a Drug-Free Workplace. All employment is contingent on successful completion of drug and background screening.

We offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package and all the tools necessary to be successful. Our offerings include: Medical, Dental, Vision Plans, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off and 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match.

We provide a collaborative work place with growth opportunities for career minded individuals.

title: Senior Research Investigator
description:
**University Overview**

The University of Pennsylvania, the largest private employer in Philadelphia, is a world-renowned leader in education, research, and innovation. This historic, Ivy League school consistently ranks among the top 10 universities in the annual U.S. News & World Report survey. Penn has 12 highly-regarded schools that provide opportunities for undergraduate, graduate and continuing education, all influenced by Penn’s distinctive interdisciplinary approach to scholarship and learning. As an employer Penn has been ranked nationally on many occasions with the most recent award from Forbes who named Penn one of America’s Best Large Employers in 2023.

Penn offers a unique working environment within the city of Philadelphia. The University is situated on a beautiful urban campus, with easy access to a range of educational, cultural, and recreational activities. With its historical significance and landmarks, lively cultural offerings, and wide variety of atmospheres, Philadelphia is the perfect place to call home for work and play.

The University offers a competitive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare and tuition benefits for employees and their families, generous retirement benefits, a wide variety of professional development opportunities, supportive work and family benefits, a wealth of health and wellness programs and resources, and much more.

**Posted Job Title**

Senior Research Investigator

**Job Profile Title**

Research Investigator, Senior

**Job Description Summary**

he Infectious Diseases Division seeks a Senior Research Investigator to join Dr. Katharine Bar’s translational HIV research lab focused on understanding HIV persistence during therapy and advancing cure strategies. The role involves

designing and conducting molecular virology experiments (e.g., PCR, sequencing, cloning, and cell culture assays), analyzing data, contributing to manuscripts, and collaborating on research projects. Candidates should have a PhD with relevant postdoctoral experience, strong communication skills, experience with viral and biospecimen work, and a willingness to mentor trainees.

**Job Description**

**Job Responsibilities**

Design, perform and analyze molecular virology experiments, including sequencing, cloning, and infectivity assays

• Perform cell culture based assays to assess virus phenotype

• Process biospecimens

• Analyze, synthesize, generate figures and communicate results of experiments

• Supervise students and technicians

• Assist in ordering, lab management, and regulatory compliance issues

• Other duties as assigned

**Position contingent upon funding**

**Qualifications**

- Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Philosophy, and 5 to 7 years of postdoctoral experience is required.

- Experience with molecular biology and sequencing is required. Experience working with viruses in cell culture strongly preferred. Experience processing biospecimens, including blood and tissues is preferred.

  Prior experience working with viruses and BSL II agents is preferred. HIV research experience preferred. Applicants with prior

  publications and presentations in biomedical science preferred. Strong computer skills are essential. Candidates must be detail-oriented with excellent communication and interpersonal skills including when working closely students; ability to multi-task; and flexibility to shift focus between multiple projects as needed.


**Job Location - City, State**

Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

**Department / School**

Perelman School of Medicine

**Pay Range**

$80,891.00 - $94,753.00 Annual Rate

Salary offers are made based on the candidate’s qualifications, experience, skills, and education as they directly relate to the requirements of the position, and in alignment with salary ranges based on external market data for the job’s level. Internal organization and peer data at Penn are also considered.

**Equal Opportunity Statement**

The University of Pennsylvania is an equal opportunity employer. Candidates are considered for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion, creed, national origin(including shared ancestry or ethnic characteristics), citizenship status, age, disability, veteran status or any class protectedunder applicable federal, state or local law.

**Special Requirements**

Background checks may be required after a conditional job offer is made. Consideration of the background check will be tailored to the requirements of the job.

**University Benefits**

- **Health, Life, and Flexible Spending Accounts**: Penn offers comprehensive medical, prescription, behavioral health, dental, vision, and life insurance benefits to protect you and your family’s health and welfare. You can also use flexible spending accounts to pay for eligible health care and dependent care expenses with pre-tax dollars.

- **Tuition**: Take advantage of Penn's exceptional tuition benefits. You, your spouse, and your dependent children can get tuition assistance here at Penn. Your dependent children are also eligible for tuition assistance at other institutions.

- **Retirement:** Penn offers generous retirement plans to help you save for your future. Penn’s Basic, Matching, and Supplemental retirement plans allow you to save for retirement on a pre-tax or Roth basis. Choose from a wide variety of investment options through TIAA and Vanguard.

- **Time Away from Work:** Penn provides you with a substantial amount of time away from work during the course of the year. This allows you to relax, take vacations, attend to personal affairs, recover from illness or injury, spend time with family—whatever your personal needs may be.

- **Long-Term Care Insurance:** In partnership with Genworth Financial, Penn offers faculty and staff (and your eligible family members) long-term care insurance to help you cover some of the costs of long-term care services received at home, in the community or in a nursing facility. If you apply when you’re newly hired, you won’t have to provide proof of good health or be subject to underwriting requirements. Eligible family members must always provide proof of good health and are subject to underwriting.

- **Wellness and Work-life Resources**: Penn is committed to supporting our faculty and staff as they balance the competing demands of work and personal life. That’s why we offer a wide variety of programs and resources to help you care for your health, your family, and your work-life balance.

- **Professional and Personal Development:** Penn provides an array of resources to help you advance yourself personally and professionally.

- **University Resources:** As a member of the Penn community, you have access to a wide range of University resources as well as cultural and recreational activities. Take advantage of the University’s libraries and athletic facilities, or visit our arboretum and art galleries. There’s always something going on at Penn, whether it’s a new exhibit at the Penn Museum, the latest music or theater presentation at the Annenberg Center, or the Penn Relays at Franklin Field to name just a few examples. As a member of the Penn community, you’re right in the middle of the excitement—and you and your family can enjoy many of these activities for free.

Not only do Penn arts and cultural centers and museums offer free and discounted admission and memberships to faculty and staff. You can also enjoy substantial savings on other goods and services such as new cars from Ford and General Motors, cellular phone service plans, movie tickets, and admission to theme parks.

title: Buyer
